Earlier iterations swung between a +hardcoded `{{else}}` token, name-agnostic separators, nested `{{#else}}` clause blocks, +and back. This is the decision; changes to it require a new ADR. + +## Context + +FlatBars is a *substrate*, not an engine: the core must commit to no semantics, and an engine +supplies meaning. We need a pipeline that makes that split structural rather than merely asserted, +and that does not grow a second parser/AST for "surface" sugar. + +Since the original decision the repository has gained a shared `kernel` package, a token-stream +interior lexer, and a *dialect ladder* (RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars, with MinBars planned). It records every syntactic shape — brace count, identifiers, args, + nesting — and assigns *no name* any meaning. There is **no separate surface parser and no surface + AST**. The interior of a tag is tokenized by a shared, meaning-free tokenizer + (`FlatBars.Token.tokenizeInterior`: `TIdent`/`TStr`/`TNum`/`TLParen`/`TRParen`/`TOp`) and handed to + a *dialect grammar* through two seams on `ParseOptions`: `parseExpr` (output/argument interiors) + and `parseHead` (block-open heads). The default grammar is the shared prefix grammar + (`FlatBars.Expr`); MaxBars swaps in a precedence-climbing grammar through the same seams. + +. *`{{ }}` is structural.* The two-brace stache is a first-class, meaning-free node (`Sep`). + `{{else}}` is just a `Sep` whose head identifier is `else`; the parser cannot tell it from + any other `{{ name }}`. Consequence: `{{` is significant in content and a literal one + is written `{{` (or inside a raw block). The brace *count* is structural data; + "two ⇒ escape" is a *walker* rule, not a parser fact ([lexical](/spec/lexical/) §1.2). + +. *Shape recognition is fixed; shape admission is dialect-gated.* The parser recognizes a *fixed* set + of sigils and tag shapes and knows nothing of what any *name* does — but which shapes are *legal* + is a per-dialect flag. `ParseOptions.extras` gates the Handlebars-only shapes (raw blocks + `{{{{…}}}}`, the inverse block `{{^}}`, unescaped `{{& }}`); RawBars and + MaxBars set `extras = false` and the parser rejects them with `DisallowedShape`. This is a + structural gate (which shapes exist), never a semantic one (what a name means). + +. *The walker is the only thing that assigns name-meaning.* It desugars and builds the real AST in the + same pass. Escaping (`escapeHtml` ⇒ escaped), clause-splitting (`{{else}}` consumed into typed + branches), and — for a surface dialect — paths (`name` ⇒ `lookup this "name"`) are all walker + decisions. The reference lowering is `Kernel.Lower.lower :: Template -> Array RNode`, a + `foldTemplate` ([A.13.2](/appendix/handlebars/#engine-api)). The surface desugar is + `FullBars.Surface.desugar`. + +. *No mandated real AST; one shared reference lowering.* `RNode` (`RIf`/`ROut`/…) is the real AST of + the reference lowering, now living in the shared `kernel` package and used by the whole ladder + (RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars) as a worked example for tool authors. Another engine (e.g. MinBars) may + lower to any shape. Crucially, `lower` is **not on the render path**: the reference renderer + (`runTemplate`, `Kernel.Engine`) interprets the structural tree *directly*; `lower` materializes + the real AST only for tooling (the playground's "Real AST" view) and lints (`escapingWarnings`). + +. *Safe by default.* The reference engine never auto-escapes raw output (`{{{ }}}`); the + `escapingWarnings` lint flags raw output of untrusted data (`lookup`/`this`/scoped accessors not + wrapped in `safe`). +---
+title: "ADR-002: Escaping and the value-policy contract"
+sidebar:
+  label: "ADR-002 Escaping & value policy"
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01. Promised by the [ADR-001 review](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/#review) consensus.
+
+## Context
+
+The core assigns no value policy. The reference engine supplies `truthy`/`escapeHtml`/`stringify`
+(`Kernel.Value`), exposes `stringify` through the engine `Ctl` (`Engine.purs:57`), and never
+auto-escapes raw output (`{{{ }}}`); the surface dialect's `{{ }}` escapes by lowering
+to `escapeHtml`. The ADR-001 debate flagged the tension: framing `escapingWarnings` (an *ignorable
+lint*, `Lower.purs:125`) as the safety mechanism is "opt-in XSS." But the substrate *cannot* mandate
+escaping without choosing a value policy — and a chosen value policy is exactly what makes something
+an *engine*, not a substrate.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *Core mandates no escaping.* HTML-escaping, truthiness, and stringification are an engine concern,
+  surfaced through `Ctl.stringify` and the engine's value module. The substrate stays policy-free.
+
+. *Safety is a conformance contract on engines, not a core feature.* Every conforming engine MUST
+  declare: (a) an HTML-escape function, (b) a `stringify`, (c) a truthiness rule (a `Truthy` =
+  `Value -> Boolean` callback — ADR-022), and
+  (d) a raw-output safety stance — does `{{{ }}}` escape? (Reference answer: no.) This belongs
+  in the [host-api](/engine/host-api/) engine checklist.
+
+. *The reference engine is safe-by-default for the surface.* `{{ }}` escapes (lowers to
+  `escapeHtml`); `{{{ }}}` does not; `escapingWarnings` flags raw output of untrusted accessors
+  (`lookup`/`this`/scoped) not wrapped in `safe`.
+
+. *The lint is on by default in tooling.* The playground already runs it (`Main.purs:211`); the CLI
+  gains it with an explicit `--no-escape-lint` opt-out, rather than being opt-in.
+
+. *One shared `escapeHtml`.* It escapes `& < > " '` and *not* backtick/`=` (`Value.purs:265`)
+  — already Mustache-conformant, so every engine in the family reuses it rather than re-deriving it.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* safety becomes *testable* (a checklist entry) rather than folklore; one `escapeHtml` is
+  shared; the substrate/engine boundary from ADR-001 is preserved exactly.
+* *Con:* XSS protection still depends on an engine honouring the contract — a careless engine can
+  declare a no-op escaper. Mitigation is the lint plus the conformance checklist, not enforcement.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+* *Bake escaping into core.* Rejected: it smuggles a value policy into the substrate, contradicting
+  ADR-001's whole reason to exist.
+* *Auto-escape `{{{ }}}` too.* Rejected: then the language has no raw-output construct at all.

+---
+title: "ADR-003: Strict layering — structural core, shared kernel, dialect packages"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-003 Strict layering
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01. Records the kernel extraction (commits `c131aaf`, `68b0280`,
+`a1c13da`).
+
+## Context
+
+The original `flatbars` package carried *both* the structural core and the engine. The standing
+directive was *strict separation of concerns* — "separating later makes it harder, so do it right":
+each dialect package contains only its own dialect code, the core is structural only, and the shared
+engine is factored into its own package. ADR-001 made the parser/walker split *conceptual*; this ADR
+makes it a *package* split.
+
+## Decision
+
+Three tiers plus adapters, dependencies pointing strictly downward.
+
+. *core (`flatbars`)* — `Lexer`, `Token`, `Parser`, `Syntax`, `Span`, `Error`, `Value`. Meaning-free:
+  no engine, no helpers, no validation. `Value` must live at or below core because `Syntax.Expr`
+  embeds `Lit Value`; pushing it up would cycle `kernel → core`.
+
+. *kernel (new package)* — the shared engine: `Engine` (the IoC driver), `Walk`
+  (`foldTemplate`/`splitClauses`/`validate`/`Schema`), `Helper` combinators, `ToValue`, `Value`
+  (value policy — the named `Truthy` rules / `stringify` / `escapeHtml`), `Env`/`RefEnv`,
+  `Prelude`, `Lower`, and `Render` (the `runResolved` glue).
+
+. *dialects (`rawbars`/`fullbars`/`maxbars`)* — each only its grammar + desugar + render/compile entry
+  points, over the kernel, *never each other*. The single sanctioned exception is `maxbars → fullbars`
+  (the intentional superset; see [adr-0005-dialect-ladder](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/)).
++
+*Isolation is an import property, not the ladder's `⊂`.* "No dialect imports another" is about the
+package graph; the ladder's `⊂` ([adr-0005-dialect-ladder](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/)) is about *surface supersetting*
+(narrowed by the ADR-005 amendment to surface-superset *modulo documented exceptions* — MaxBars is the
+flagship that reuses FullBars's engine wholesale and borrows most, not all, of its surface).
+RawBars *has* import isolation (a FullBars-free closure, [adr-0008-rawbars](/adr/adr-0008-rawbars/)); MaxBars
+*trades* it for reuse because it genuinely is a FullBars superset. The two properties must not be
+conflated — there is exactly *one* sanctioned import crossing.
+
+. *compile* — `flatbars-compile` is the dialect-agnostic emit driver + `Emit` rules, kept FullBars-free
+  (`Compile.Emit` reads `Kernel.Value`); `fullbars-compile` layers the surface compiler on top, so
+  RawBars' dependency closure is fully FullBars-free.
+
+. *adapters* — `json` (JSON ⇆ `Value`, deliberately *out* of core: JSON-ness is a host concern), `js`
+  (FFI), `cli`, `playground`.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* the substrate claim is *structural* (enforced by the package graph), not asserted; RawBars'
+  closure is provably FullBars-free; a new engine plugs onto `kernel` without touching dialects.
+* *Con:* module renames (`FlatBars.Engine → Kernel.Engine`, etc.) rippled to every importer; the
+  workspace is now 11 packages; `spago.lock` must be regenerated when a package is added (else test
+  deps don't resolve). The "no dialect imports another" rule carries one sanctioned exception.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+* *A `common` package.* Rejected: a vague shared bucket with no clear boundary. Extract shared code
+  *lazily*, only on a proven second consumer (this is what [adr-0007-minbars](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/) later
+  triggers for the truthiness-default parameter and the recursion guard).

+---
+title: "ADR-005: The dialect ladder and reuse-by-dependency"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-005 Dialect ladder
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01.
+
+## Context
+
+The family needs several Handlebars-lineage dialects that share one engine without copy-paste, and
+*without* a premature shared-abstraction package. ADR-003 fixed *where* code lives; ADR-004 fixed
+*how* a dialect plugs in its grammar. This ADR fixes the *relationship* between the dialects.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *The ladder: RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars.*
++
+| Dialect | Surface |
+| --- | --- |
+| *RawBars* | the core prefix grammar directly — explicit `{{{ lookup this "x" }}}`, no sugar; `extras = false`. |
+| *FullBars* | adds the surface desugar — paths, `@data`, `as \|x\|`, `{{ }}` auto-escape; `extras = true`. |
+| *MaxBars* | FullBars + infix operators and pipes (`MaxBars.Expr`), desugaring to the same core `Expr`; `extras = false`. |
+
+. *Reuse by dependency, not copy.* MaxBars depends on `fullbars` and reuses its engine, prelude, value
+  policy, surface desugar, and compiler — swapping *only* the interior grammar through the
+  `parseExpr`/`parseHead` seams. A shared semantic kernel is extracted *lazily*, only on a proven
+  second consumer (ADR-003), never speculatively.
+
+. *Shared compile driver + per-dialect `Emit`.* `FlatBars.Compile` is the dialect-agnostic emit driver
+  — the *fourth* instance of the inversion-of-control pattern (interpret / desugar / validate /
+  *compile*). `type Emit = { expr, block }` (`Compile.purs:54`); FullBars' `fullbarsEmit`
+  (`Emit.purs:74`) emits native control flow for `if`/`each`/…. The conformance harness asserts the
+  interpreter and the compiled JS produce byte-identical output.
+
+. *Operators and pipes lower to existing prelude helpers.* Pipe `{{ a | f }}` → `(f a)` (piped
+  value first); infix `&& || ! == != < > <= >=` → `and`/`or`/`not`/`eq`/… per the surface §B.7
+  table. No new engine semantics — only new *surface*.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* one engine, four IoC instances, N dialects as symmetric packages; a new tier is a grammar
+  swap, not a fork.
+* *Con:* `maxbars → fullbars` is a *real* cross-dialect dependency — the single sanctioned violation
+  of ADR-003's "no dialect imports another." The "⊂" is a claim about *surface supersetting*, not
+  about package isolation; the two must not be conflated (see the final review).
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+* *Copy FullBars into MaxBars.* Rejected: guarantees drift between the dialects' shared semantics.
+* *A `common` engine package up front.* Rejected for the same reason as in ADR-003 — extract on a
+  proven overlap, not on speculation.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): `⊂` is surface-superset *modulo documented exceptions*
+
+The original decision wrote the ladder as `RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars` and the final
+review pinned `⊂` as a strict *surface-superset* claim — "every FullBars template is a
+MaxBars template." That overclaims: MaxBars is FlatBars' **flagship** surface, but it
+deliberately does *not* accept a couple of FullBars surface constructs, so the top edge
+is "most of FullBars, not quite all."
+
+Two layers, two different truths — they must not be conflated:
+
+* *Engine reuse by dependency is total and unchanged.* MaxBars still reuses FullBars's
+  engine, prelude, value policy (truthiness aside, ADR-022), surface desugar, and compiler
+  *wholesale* — swapping only the interior grammar through the `parseExpr`/`parseHead`
+  seams. Nothing below the surface diverges.
+* *Surface supersetting is "most, not all."* The MaxBars surface borrows the bulk of
+  FullBars's surface, but rejects, by design:
++
+| FullBars construct | Why MaxBars rejects it |
+| --- | --- |
+| the `{{#*inline}}` *decorator* | MaxBars spells inline partials with bare `{{#inline}}`; the `*`-decorator form is FullBars-only. |
+| `{{> @partial-block}}` | the `@` sigil is reserved in MaxBars, which renders the caller's block body via bare `{{yield}}` instead. |
++
+(Separately, MaxBars *adds* surface — operators, pipes, bare loop vars — and tightens a
+few spellings where its richer grammar would otherwise be ambiguous: a clause-separator
+condition and a block-head pipe must be parenthesised. Those are MaxBars-only additions,
+not FullBars constructs it drops; see [maxbars](/engine/maxbars/) "v1 limitations.")
+
+So `⊂` now reads: **surface-superset modulo the documented exceptions above**, over a
+fully reused engine. The thesis of the original decision is untouched — one engine, four
+IoC instances, dialects as symmetric packages, a new tier as a grammar swap not a fork.
+What changes is only the *honesty of the top edge*: MaxBars is the flagship that reuses
+FullBars and reinterprets its surface, not a strict superset of it.

+---
+title: "ADR-006: MaxBars bare loop variables"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-006 MaxBars loop variables
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted; the *Decision §1–2 bare loop-variable vocabulary* and the *§5 v1 outer-loop limit are
+superseded by* [ADR-021](/adr/adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model/) — bare `{{index0}}`/`{{first}}`
+are replaced by the namespaced `loop.*` object, and `@root`/`../` by `root`/`parent`. The
+normative arithmetic this ADR fixes (§3) carries over unchanged as the `loop`-object field values, and the
+§4 schema-less shadow lint is retired. *Date:* 2026-06-01. Records MaxBars Phases A/B/F (commits
+`26a1f65`, `5caca26`, `8cf6c15`).
+
+## Context
+
+Handlebars exposes loop state through the `@` namespace (`@index`, `@first`, `../`). MaxBars wants a
+richer, *bare* (no-`@`) loop-variable vocabulary that reads as ordinary scoped helpers (ADR-001 §4:
+scope is scoped helpers). The cost is that bare names can shadow data fields.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *MaxBars-only.* FullBars stays as-is (`@index`/`@../`, via `noLoopVars`); MaxBars installs bare
+  scoped helpers via `maxLoopVars` (`MaxBars.purs:41`). The richer each-frame metadata the kernel now
+  exposes (Phase A) backs both.
+
+. *Canonical set + aliases.* `index0 index1 rindex0 rindex1 first last length key`; aliases
+  `index → index0`, `rindex → rindex0`, `size → length`.
+
+. *Normative arithmetic, so interpreter and compiler cannot drift.* `index1 = index0 + 1`;
+  `rindex0 = length − 1 − index0`; `rindex1 = length − index0`; `first = index0 == 0`;
+  `last = index0 == length − 1`. The spec fixes these so both execution paths compute identically.
+
+. *Shadowing is contained by a schema-aware lint.* Dropping `@` lets `first`/`key`/`length` collide
+  with data fields. When a schema is present, a loop variable that collides with a declared field is
+  an *error*.
+
+. *v1 outer-loop limit (documented).* Only the outer element/index/key are reachable, via block
+  params `as |user uidx|`. Outer `first`/`last`/`length`/`rindex` are *not* reachable — labelled loops
+  are future work. The companion spec's claim "compute from a named outer length" is wrong: block
+  params bind only the item plus index/key, so the outer length cannot be named.
+
+. *`depth` (recursion depth) is reserved/deferred* until a recursion construct (a self-including
+  partial) exists.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* ergonomic, Handlebars-free loop variables; drift-proof by construction (the normative
+  arithmetic).
+* *Con:* shadowing is only caught *when a schema is present* — a schema-less template can silently
+  shadow a data field. The final review revisits whether the lint should also warn schema-less.

+---
+title: "ADR-007: MinBars — a Mustache-compatible peer engine"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-007 MinBars
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted (implemented). *Date:* 2026-06-01.
+
+:::note
+*Conformance (full official `mustache/spec`).* MinBars passes *184/184 (100%) of every Mustache module
+it implements* — all six required modules plus the optional `~dynamic-names` and `~inheritance`. Measured
+against the spec's own `expected` (`conformance/mustache/`, gated by `npm run check:mustache-conformance`),
+over the *whole* vendored suite, so it cannot over-claim.
+
+*Lambdas live outside the value, by design.* The optional `~lambdas` module is not a target: a Mustache
+lambda is a *function embedded in the data*, and a `Value` is *pure data, never a function*
+([concepts](/concepts/)). The two jobs a lambda does map to two places, neither inside the value — a
+*value-producing* lambda is *precalculated in a preprocess step* (any host-side computation; in the Lab,
+the JSONata transform) and rendered as plain data; a *section* lambda that rewrites its block body is a
+*helper/block helper* (render-time behaviour — preprocessing never sees the unrendered body). The
+engine-level guarantee is narrow but real: *no arbitrary host code runs from template data, and the
+rendered `Value` stays pure and JSON-serialisable*. JSONata is the Lab's tool for the preprocess step, not
+an engine dependency — the engine, CLI and compiled output only ever receive plain data.
+:::
+
+## Context
+
+A Mustache-compatible engine completes the family. The key decision is its *position*: MinBars is a
+*peer* of FullBars, not a desugar over it. The lattice becomes RawBars ⊂ MinBars (Mustache) and
+RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars, with MinBars and FullBars as siblings over the shared kernel.
+
+The draft spec was reviewed against the real code; that review found several "core is reused
+unchanged" claims to be false. They are recorded here because they reshape the plan.
+
+## Decision (locked)
+
+. *Scope = the full Mustache spec in one pass* — interpolation, sections, inverted, comments, partials,
+  dotted names, implicit iterator, standalone whitespace — *plus* inheritance
+  (`{{<p}}`/`{{$b}}`/`{{<*}}`/`{{/*}}`) and dynamic-name partials
+  (`{{>* }}`). Lambdas are dropped (`Value` has no function arm). Set delimiters
+  (`{{=<% %>=}}`) were initially deferred but are now *implemented* MinBars-exclusively
+  ([ADR-015](/adr/adr-0015-set-delimiters/) + 2026-06-04 scope narrowing; RawBars / MaxBars /
+  FullBars reject the inline form). MinBars passes the full `delimiters` module, 14/14.
+
+. *Truthiness `mustache` default = a shared parameter.* Add `mustache = false null []` to the alias
+  table *and* thread a per-engine default `FalsySet` through `resolveTruthiness` + `runResolved`
+  (today `handlebars` is hardwired, `Value.purs:69`); update the RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars call sites to
+  pass `handlebars` explicitly. Recursion budget default = 64.
+
+. *Conformance harness = a Node-side runner* (`.mjs`, mirroring `packages/compile/conformance.mjs`)
+  against built `output/`, using the mustache/spec *`.json`* fixtures — built-in `JSON.parse`, *no*
+  YAML dependency.
+
+. *Build the shared recursion guard now* — a kernel depth/budget (error past 64) that also hardens the
+  reference engine's currently-unbounded `partialH` (`Prelude.purs:501`).
+
+## Substrate corrections the review found
+
+These were wrong in the draft spec; verified in the code:
+
+* The IoC driver *is* env-polymorphic (`Engine m env`) — but `refEngine` is hardwired to `RefEnv`, so
+  MinBars writes its *own* `Engine m MinEnv`. `MinEnv` must be a *newtype* (the `env → Helper → Ctl`
+  reference is cyclic). Use a closed `resolve` mapping the desugar's fixed helper names to the MinBars
+  prelude — no helper-registry frame needed.
+* `Ctl.render :: env -> Template -> m **String**` (not `m Value`) — section/inverted helpers must
+  ``VSafe <$> ctl.render …`` then `joinWith ""`, like `eachH`; the spec's helper snippets were
+  type-wrong as written.
+* The core lexer recognises a *fixed* sigil set with *no* per-engine seam. Plain-Mustache sigils
+  already exist, but `{{<`/`{{$`/`{{>*`/`{{<*`/`{{/*` are *new* and
+  must be added to the *shared* core lexer/parser, gated like `extras` ([adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams](/adr/adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams/)).
+  "Core reused unchanged" is false.
+* Standalone whitespace is already shared and default-on (`trimStandalone`); the genuinely new work is
+  *partial/inheritance indentation re-application*, not the standalone pass.
+* `escapeHtml` already escapes `& < > " '` and not backtick/`=` — already Mustache-conformant,
+  reuse it ([adr-0002-escaping-and-value-policy](/adr/adr-0002-escaping-and-value-policy/)).
+* MinBars supplies its *own* prelude: the reference `partialH` *throws* on a missing partial (Mustache
+  wants `""`) and Mustache *inherits* the context stack.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* completes the family and forces three genuinely reusable kernel upgrades — the per-engine
+  truthiness default, the recursion guard, and the gated-sigil mechanism. MinBars is the *proven
+  second consumer* that justifies these extractions under ADR-003's "extract lazily" rule.
+* *Con:* the "core is reused unchanged" folklore dies; every new gated sigil enlarges the shared
+  lexer's fixed vocabulary — the ADR-004 *Con* realised for the first time.
+
+## Phase plan
+
+P0 shared prereqs (truthiness default param + `mustache` set; recursion guard; gated core-lexer
+Mustache shapes) → P1 `minbars` package + own `Engine`/`MinEnv` + prelude + desugar → P2 core
+semantics → P3 inheritance + dynamic-names → P4 standalone + indentation → P5 Node conformance harness.

+---
+title: "ADR-008: RawBars — the austere base dialect"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-008 RawBars
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01. The base rung of the ladder fixed by
+[adr-0005-dialect-ladder](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/).
+
+## Context
+
+The dialect ladder (ADR-005) needs a *base*: a dialect that exercises the substrate with **zero**
+surface sugar. It is two things at once — the runnable proof that the engine works on raw core syntax
+(ADR-001's "core syntax renders end-to-end" as an actual package, not an aspiration), and the package
+whose dependency closure must stay *FullBars-free* (ADR-003's isolation claim made testable).
+
+## Decision
+
+. *No surface — authors write core syntax directly.* Explicit `{{{ lookup this "x" }}}`,
+  `{{#each …}}`, `{{else}}`. No path desugar, no `@data`, no `{{ }}`
+  auto-escape, no hash args, no block-param sugar. The seam that distinguishes RawBars from FullBars
+  is precisely the `identity` desugar: `runResolved directives identity nodes dat`
+  (`RawBars.purs:55`) — *same engine, no rewrite*.
+
+. *`extras = false`.* RawBars rejects the Handlebars-only tag shapes — raw blocks
+  `{{{{…}}}}`, inverse `{{^}}`, unescaped `{{&}}` — with `DisallowedShape`
+  (`coreOptions`, `RawBars.purs:44`). The gate is re-forced inside `compileWith`/`compileJsWith`
+  (`opts { extras = false }`) so a caller-supplied `ParseOptions` cannot smuggle them back in. Other
+  front-end knobs (standalone trimming) still pass through.
+
+. *Reuse by dependency, with a FullBars-free closure.* RawBars renders through the shared reference
+  engine via `Kernel.Render.runResolved` and compiles through the shared driver + `fullbarsEmit` from
+  `FlatBars.Compile.Emit`. It imports `kernel` and `flatbars-compile` — **not** the `fullbars`
+  package. Its dependency closure is therefore provably free of FullBars (this is the closure the
+  [final review](/adr/adr-final-review/) asks to lock with a test).
+
+. *Full instantiation set.* The same dialect is offered pure (`render`/`renderDiag`/`renderValue`),
+  async (`renderAff`, in `ExceptT Error Aff`), and as a JS-compiling target
+  (`compileJs`/`compileJsWith`) — so RawBars covers every host shape the engine supports.
+
+. *Host-registered operations.* `renderWithOperations` (ADR-019 addendum) renders against a bag of
+  host-supplied *operations* — the native boundary word for what FullBars calls a *helper*
+  (`renderWith`). RawBars stays *strict*: an unknown head is an `UnknownHelper`, never the lenient
+  `blockHelperMissing`. A *block* operation gets `options.fn(ctx)` / `options.inverse(ctx)` and may
+  supply scoped data through `options.fn(ctx, { data })` (read back as a core operation name, since
+  RawBars has no `@var` surface). It has *no* `options.hash` and *no* block params — core syntax has
+  no `k=v` or `as |x|` to write. From JS, `renderRawWith` marshals plain functions in.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* the substrate's central promise is a *running dialect*, not prose; the FullBars-free closure
+  turns ADR-003's layering into something a CI test can assert.
+* *Con:* authoring is verbose (every `lookup` is explicit) — RawBars is the desugared core surface, a base/test dialect, not
+  the one most authors should reach for. The module docstring still says "the FullBars reference
+  engine"/"the compiler's FullBars `Emit`," which is cosmetic drift: that engine and that `Emit` now
+  live in `kernel`/`flatbars-compile`, which is *why* the closure is FullBars-free.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): inline-partial hoisting is shared, so RawBars has full parity
+
+RawBars previously could *not* hoist `{{#inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}` definitions: the
+`hoistInline` pre-pass lived in `FullBars.Surface`, so only FullBars/MaxBars ran it, and a RawBars
+`{{#inline}}` was a no-op (the matching `{{#partial}}` then failed as an unregistered
+partial). That was a *functional* gap, contradicting this ADR's "same engine, no rewrite": hoisting
+is not surface sugar — it is the semantic step that populates the registry the prelude's `partial`
+helper reads.
+
+`hoistInline` is now `Kernel.Hoist.hoistInline`, a shared concept every dialect runs. RawBars'
+`render`/`renderWithOperations`/`compileJs` hoist before rendering/compiling exactly as
+FullBars/MaxBars do; FullBars/MaxBars re-import it (behaviour unchanged). So `{{#inline}}` +
+`{{{yield}}}` (the bare-core spelling of FullBars' `{{> @partial-block}}`) now work in
+RawBars, and the three dialects differ *only* in surface syntax (and truthiness, ADR-022) — the
+ladder's actual contract. Inline-free templates render byte-identically (the hoist is a no-op on
+them), so the change is additive; `test:compile` stays 300/300.

+---
+title: "ADR-009: FullBars — the reference engine and surface dialect"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-009 FullBars
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01. The middle rung of the ladder
+([adr-0005-dialect-ladder](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/)); "flat bars" to FlatBars' "bare rods."
+
+## Context
+
+The substrate needs *one* worked, Handlebars-faithful engine — to validate the host API (ADR-001
+§A.13), to be the family's reference and Handlebars migration target, and to be the surface the other
+dialects are defined against. FullBars is "one *possible* engine over the substrate" (ADR-001), not a
+privileged one; the architecture must keep it swappable even as it serves as the default.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *FullBars = value policy + environment + prelude + lowering + surface desugar*, wired into
+  convenience renderers. After the kernel extraction (ADR-003) the value policy
+  (`truthy`/`escapeHtml`/`stringify`), `RefEnv`, prelude, and `lower` live in `kernel`; the `fullbars`
+  package owns the *surface desugar* (`FullBars.Surface`), the convenience renderers, and the helper
+  *catalog* (the single source of truth for `gen:catalog`).
+
+. *`extras = true`.* FullBars admits the Handlebars-only shapes (raw blocks, inverse, unescaped) that
+  RawBars ([adr-0008-rawbars](/adr/adr-0008-rawbars/)) and MaxBars reject.
+
+. *The surface is a desugar, not a parser* (ADR-001). `FullBars.Surface.desugar` is a pure
+  `Template → Template` rewrite into core forms, then the reference renderer (or `lower`) runs the
+  result unchanged. It rewrites: `{{ E }}` ⇒ escaped `{{{ escapeHtml E }}}`; bare/dotted
+  *paths* ⇒ `lookup` chains (`name` ⇒ `lookup this "name"`, `a.b`, `a.[1]`, `../a` ⇒
+  `lookup (parent) …`); `@data` ⇒ scoped calls (`@index` ⇒ `(index)`, `@root.x`); `else if` chains ⇒
+  flat `{{elif}}`; hash args `k=v` ⇒ a trailing `dict`; block params `as |item i|` ⇒ string
+  args (and a bare in-scope reference ⇒ a call `(item)`); partials `{{> name ctx k=v}}`;
+  `{{#partial}}`/`{{#inline}}`.
+
+. *`noLoopVars` — every bare name is a data path* (the Handlebars rule); scoped loop state is reached
+  only through `@`. This is the deliberate contrast with MaxBars
+  ([adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables](/adr/adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables/)), which maps bare names to loop variables through the
+  *same* `LoopVars` hook.
+
+. *Safe-by-default* ([adr-0002-escaping-and-value-policy](/adr/adr-0002-escaping-and-value-policy/)): `{{ }}` escapes,
+  `{{{ }}}` is raw, and `escapingWarnings` flags raw output of untrusted accessors.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* one engine doubles as the Handlebars migration target *and* the catalog's source of truth;
+  the surface-as-rewrite is the concrete proof of ADR-001's "no surface parser, no surface AST."
+* *Note:* the Handlebars block sigils `{{#> name}}` and `{{#*inline}}` are now accepted
+  (the core lexes them as the distinct `PartialBlock` / `Decorator` sigils — each with a clean head
+  and a `{{/…}}` close that repeats it — gated by `ParseOptions.partialBlocks` / `decorators`,
+  and they desugar to the `{{#partial}}`/`{{#inline}}` core spellings).
+* *Con:* because every other dialect is defined *relative to* FullBars, it carries gravitational
+  weight despite being "just one engine" — the same tension ADR-001 logged as the
+  shared-reference-lowering point.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-03): inline partials require the `{{#*inline}}` decorator
+
+FullBars now *requires* the Handlebars decorator form `{{#*inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}`
+for inline partials and *rejects* the bare `{{#inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}` spelling with a
+located `DisallowedShape` parse error. This matches Handlebars, where `inline` is a *decorator*, not
+a block helper. The original "Note" above — that `{{#*inline}}` is merely accepted and
+desugars to a `{{#inline}}` core spelling — is superseded *for the FullBars surface*: the
+decorator is now the author form, and it still desugars internally to the core `inline` helper
+(hoisted by `hoistInline`).
+
+This is a *FullBars-surface-only* gate (`FullBars.checkBareInline`, which also governs the CLI
+`--surface` path). The shared kernel `inline` helper is *retained* (a no-op block), so *RawBars and
+MaxBars are unchanged*: they still accept bare `{{#inline}}` (MaxBars's grammar bans the `*`
+head, so bare is its only inline form). The generated helper catalog is unaffected — the helper still
+exists.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-05): FullBars carries the blessed i18n operations (ADR-029)
+
+FullBars's prelude includes the blessed i18n operations `t` / `number` / `date` / `selectPlural` /
+`relative` ([ADR-029](/adr/adr-0029-i18n-helper/)), which *Handlebars does not have*. This is a
+*deliberate, documented exception* to "Handlebars-faithful", recorded here so faithfulness is never
+claimed by omission: these names are reserved at the prelude level, host-driven through the first-class
+`Translator` seam (`RefEnv.translator` / `rt.registerTranslator`, the i18n analogue of the truthiness
+seam — ADR-022), and render their argument's plain text when no host is wired.
+
+Why this does *not* erode the faithfulness the ADR rests on:
+
+* *No behavioural divergence on real Handlebars templates.* The operations only fire when *applied with
+  arguments* (`{{t "k"}}`); a bare `{{t}}` still reads the data field `t`. A Handlebars
+  template that never calls `t`/`number`/`date` is byte-identical (the `handlebars` conformance corpus
+  stays 49/50 — but note the *guarantee* is the application-gated semantics, not merely that the corpus
+  happens not to exercise them).
+* *Shared-prelude scope is deliberate.* They live in the *core-surface* prelude (RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars)
+  so FullBars's `{{t …}}` has a desugar target; they are *absent from MinBars* (its closed
+  Mustache prelude), so [ADR-007](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/)'s "pure Mustache" claim is intact.
+* *No bundled CLDR.* The seam carries no locale data; the brain is the host's (ADR-029).
+
+In short: FullBars is "Handlebars + the host-pluggable i18n seam", and that "+" is stated, not hidden.

+---
+title: "ADR-010: Header directives — `@truthiness` and `@trim`"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-010 Header directives
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted for `@trim`; the *`@truthiness` half is **Superseded** by*
+[ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/) (2026-06-03). *Date:* 2026-06-01. Records the standalone `@trim`
+directive and the original per-file `@truthiness` spec (Phases 0–5). Companion spec:
+[directives](/engine/directives/).
+
+:::note
+*The per-file `@truthiness` directive is superseded.* Team review ([ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/))
+found the per-file *configuration surface* — the directive meaning, the alias table, the shape-literal
+list, lexical per-partial scoping (`partialFalsy`), the linter's truthiness-*materialization* phase, and
+the compiler's `$falsy` baking — to be over-engineered: it has **zero golden-case usage**, yet costs a
+24-file blast radius and a dedicated linter phase. Truthiness becomes a *fixed per-engine rule* expressed
+as a lambda the engine plugs in (FullBars/RawBars/MaxBars: the Handlebars rule; MinBars: Mustache), with
+the named rules kept as introspectable data the engine selects from. `includeZero` is re-homed as a
+per-call helper option. A leftover `@truthiness` directive is carried but inert, and `directiveLints`
+warns it as deprecated. Decision points 2 and 3 below are retained for the historical record; ADR-022 is
+the live design. *`@trim` (point 4) is unaffected* and remains Accepted.
+:::
+
+## Context
+
+Two behaviours must be selectable *per file* — without a helper call and without per-render host
+configuration: the truthiness policy of conditionals, and standalone-whitespace handling. They need a
+carriage mechanism that does not breach the meaning-free core (ADR-001).
+
+## Decision
+
+. *Directives ride in a short `{{! … }}` comment at the file head*, keyed `@key`/`@key: value`.
+  The core lifts them *meaning-free* (the `Sep` precedent for comments); the engine assigns meaning.
+  Because carriage lives in the core parser, every dialect (RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars) inherits
+  directives uniformly. Directives are *header-only* — a real tag closes the header, after which a
+  directive is a `DirectiveAfterHeader` error. Long `{{!-- … --}}` comments are inert prose (so
+  JSDoc `@param`, e-mail handles, etc. are safe by construction). Unknown keys are *carried and
+  lint-warned*, not errors (forward compatibility).
+
+. [.line-through]##*`@truthiness` selects the falsy set*## — *superseded by [ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/); retained for the record.*
+  `@truthiness` selected the falsy set for `if`/`unless`/`and`/`or`/`not` (and MaxBars'
+  `&&`/`||`/`!`), per file, *lexically* scoped — a condition branches by the set declared where it is
+  *written*, never render-global, never inherited across a partial boundary. The value is *one alias*
+  *or* a non-empty space-separated list of shape-literals (`false null "" 0 [] {}`). Canonical aliases:
+  `empty` (= the `handlebars` default), `minimal` (= `ruby`/`nil`/`lua`), `presence`, `always`; plus
+  `mustache` for MinBars. Docs always print the *expansion* beside a name (a name says nothing the
+  explicit set does not). `includeZero` on a single `if`/`unless` is a per-call exception. The empty
+  value is illegal — use the `always` alias.
+
+. [.line-through]##*The per-engine default is a kernel parameter.*## — *superseded by [ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/).*
+  `resolveTruthinessWith :: FalsySet -> Array Directive -> Either Error FalsySet` (`Value.purs`) took the
+  absent-directive default; the Handlebars-family dialects passed `handlebars`, MinBars `mustache`. Under
+  ADR-022 the *resolver disappears* (no directive to resolve) and the per-engine default becomes the
+  *only* rule — the lambda the engine plugs in directly. The MinBars-vs-Handlebars split survives as two
+  fixed lambdas, so [adr-0007-minbars](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/) §2's prerequisite is still met.
+
+. *`@trim` selects standalone-whitespace handling* — `standalone` (default; strips the line a lone
+  block/comment tag sits on) or `none`. It is acted *in the core lexer* (`trimStandalone`), default-on
+  (`defaultParseOptions.trimStandalone = true`). Precedence: a `@trim` directive overrides the CLI
+  `--trim` flag, which overrides `flatbars.json`'s `{ "trim": … }`, which overrides the default.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* per-file policy with no runtime config and no helper; meaning-free carriage keeps the core
+  clean and gives every dialect directives for free; one truthiness resolver and one standalone pass,
+  shared.
+* *Con:* directives are header-only (no mid-file switch — deliberate, for lexical clarity); alias names
+  are sugar over an explicit set (mitigated by always printing the expansion); `@trim` interacts with
+  `{{else}}`-standalone, which needs dialect clause-awareness (a `Lexer` caveat).
+
+## Known gap
+
+[.line-through]##`directives.adoc`'s alias table does not yet list `mustache`.## — *moot under
+[ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/):* the alias table itself is removed (the named rules become an
+engine's plugged-in lambda, not a per-file directive value), so there is no table row to reconcile.

+---
+title: "ADR-011: Compile to JS — dual execution path, byte-identity gate"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-011 Compile to JS
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01. The fourth IoC instance introduced by
+[adr-0005-dialect-ladder](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/) §3, recorded in full here.
+
+## Context
+
+FlatBars must drop into the same places Handlebars does — including ahead-of-time *compiled*
+templates, not only interpretation. A compiler that silently diverges from the interpreter is worse
+than no compiler. The decision is therefore not "add a compiler" but "keep *two* execution paths and
+*gate* them against each other."
+
+## Decision
+
+. *The compiler is the fourth inversion-of-control instance* (interpret / desugar / validate /
+  *compile*): a dialect-agnostic *emit driver* (`FlatBars.Compile`) walks the structural `Template`
+  and assembles JS source; a per-dialect `Emit` record (`type Emit = { expr, block }`) decides how an
+  expression and a block become JavaScript. Output is one ES module —
+  `export default function (data, rt)` — run against a small runtime
+  (`packages/compile/runtime/flatbars-runtime.mjs`).
+
+. *Two `Emit` tiers.* The faithful baseline routes everything through `rt.call`/`rt.block` (the
+  reference behaviour). The FullBars optimiser (`fullbarsEmit`) additionally emits *native* JS control
+  flow for `if`/`unless`/`each`/`with`. Data-dependent work (truthiness, lookup) is deferred to the
+  runtime, so compiled code operates on plain JS values — not the `Value` ADT.
+
+. *The runtime contract is versioned.* `runtimeVersion` is stamped in the compiled module header and
+  checked by the runtime; it is bumped on any runtime-incompatible codegen change. The engine's
+  truthiness rule is a *callback* the root frame is seeded with — `rt.truthyHandlebars` (FullBars),
+  `rt.truthyNonEmpty` (RawBars/MaxBars), or `rt.truthyMustache` (MinBars); no baked falsy-set
+  ([ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/) superseded the old `$falsy` constant).
+
+. *The interpreter is the executable spec; a conformance gate enforces equality.*
+  `packages/compile/conformance.mjs` (`npm run test:compile`) renders every case with *both* the
+  interpreter (`FullBars.renderWith`) and the compiled function, and asserts *byte-identical* output.
+  The corpus is the inline `conformance/cases.mjs` plus the golden `examples/`. The harness imports
+  from `output/` (the build product), so it always tests current source.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* AOT performance with a *hard* correctness guarantee; the optimiser tier can be aggressive
+  precisely because the gate catches any drift; all dialects share the one driver.
+* *Con:* every codegen change must keep the gate green — *byte-identical*, not merely "equivalent";
+  there are two execution paths to maintain; the runtime is a separately versioned artifact whose
+  contract must be honoured by both the emitter and any host.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+* *Compile only (no interpreter).* Rejected: loses the inspectable executable spec the gate compares
+  against — there would be nothing to be "correct" *relative to*.
+* *Interpret only (no compiler).* Rejected: forfeits the Handlebars-parity ahead-of-time story that
+  motivates dropping into Handlebars' niche.

+---
+title: "ADR-012: Recursion and resource budget"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-012 Recursion budget
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted — implemented (commit `fdc0b33`). *Date:* 2026-06-01. Required by
+[adr-0007-minbars](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/) §4 and the [final review](/adr/adr-final-review/).
+
+## Context
+
+The reference engine's partial helper (`partialH`, `Prelude.purs`) *was* unbounded: a self-including
+or mutually-including partial recursed until the stack overflowed. This was a live gap, independent of
+any unshipped engine. MinBars (inheritance, dynamic-name partials) made it acute, and any future
+recursion construct (self-including partials, labelled loops — [adr-0013-labelled-loops](/adr/adr-0013-labelled-loops/))
+needs a defined limit.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *A shared kernel depth/budget*, default **64**, that — when exceeded — raises a *located*
+  `RecursionLimit` error rather than crashing the host.
+. *It hardens the reference `partialH` immediately*, so the unbounded-recursion gap closes regardless
+  of MinBars.
+. *Overridable per file* via a header directive (mechanism per [adr-0010-header-directives](/adr/adr-0010-header-directives/);
+  spelling — e.g. `@budget` — TBD).
+. *Counts render-time re-entry* (partial/block expansion depth), not expression nesting, which is
+  already bounded structurally by the parser.
+
+## Implementation
+
+Shipped in commit `fdc0b33`: `RefEnv` carries a `depth` field (0 in `emptyEnv`); `recursionBudget`
+is a kernel constant (**64**); `partialH` increments via `enterPartial` on entering a registered
+partial and raises `RecursionLimit recursionBudget` once `depth >= budget` — so the reference engine
+is bounded (decision items 1, 2, 4). MinBars' `parent`/`partial` reuse the same guard (`f4e98a0`).
+The per-file `@budget` *override* (item 3) is not yet implemented — it remains the open question below.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* no unbounded recursion; a single guard serves MinBars, the reference engine, and future
+  recursion constructs — a textbook ADR-003 lazy extraction with three consumers.
+* *Con:* a global default may be too low for legitimate deep partial trees (hence the override); the
+  guard adds a counter to the hot path.
+
+## Open questions
+
+* *Depth-only vs. a work/node budget.* A depth cap is simple but lets a shallow-but-explosive template
+  through; a node budget is fairer but harder to explain.
+* *The default value* (64 is borrowed from the MinBars decision; no corpus has validated it).
+* *The directive spelling* and whether it is engine-wide or per-call.

+---
+title: "ADR-013: Labelled loops (lifting the outer-loop limit)"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-013 Labelled loops
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted and *implemented*. *Date:* 2026-06-03 (implemented; accepted 2026-06-02; proposed
+2026-06-01). Lifts the v1 limit documented in [adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables](/adr/adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables/) §5. *Extended by*
+[ADR-021](/adr/adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model/), which generalises the labelled-loop frame-object into
+the full `this`/`loop`/`root`/`parent`/`outer` model (`outer` = a `label NAME`) and makes the frame chain
+(`loop.parent`, `parent.parent`).
+
+## Context
+
+MaxBars v1 reaches only the *outer element/index/key*, via block params `{{#each users as |user uidx|}}`.
+The outer loop's `first`/`last`/`length`/`rindex` are unreachable, and the companion spec's "compute from a
+named outer length" idea was shown wrong: block params bind only the item plus index/key, so the
+outer length cannot be named. Reaching full outer-loop state needs a *naming/scoping* construct, not
+another block param.
+
+The design rests on one observed fact about the surface desugar. A loop already builds a per-iteration
+frame (`Kernel.Prelude.iterate`): `this`, `index0`…`length`, `first`, `last`, `key`, `parent`. A path
+*head* resolves against that frame **only if the name is in the desugar's `scope` set**, which `as |…|`
+populates. A block param reaches it — `{{#with o as |c|}}{{c.deep.n}}` renders `n` — but the
+frame's own `parent` helper does *not* (`{{parent.title}}` renders empty), because `parent` is
+not scope-declared. So a label must be a **scope-declared binding**, exactly like a block param.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *A label is a block param bound to the loop frame reified as an object* — not a `../` walk or a
+  `@parent` stack (ADR-001 §4, "scope is scoped helpers", stays intact). `each` reifies the current
+  frame as a `VObject` and binds it to the labelled name; an inner body then reads
+  `{{outer.length}}` / `{{outer.rindex0}}` / `{{outer.first}}` as an ordinary path
+  lookup on that object — the same mechanism a block param already uses for `{{c.deep.n}}`.
+. *Surface syntax: a `label NAME` clause, parallel to `as |…|`* —
+  `{{#each users as |user uidx| label outer}}`. `label` is parsed as structure and is
+  single-sourced in the surface desugar beside `extractBlockParams` (it adds `NAME` to `scope` and has
+  `each` bind the frame-object). Rejected alternatives: a static `loop="outer"` hash (a hash
+  value is a runtime expression, but a label is a *static* scope fact — special-casing a string-literal
+  hash is magic); an `as |user ^outer|` sigil (MaxBars deliberately dropped sigils, ADR-006).
+. *The frame-object field set is normative* —
+  `{ this, index0, index1, rindex0, rindex1, first, last, length, key }`, reusing ADR-006's fixed
+  arithmetic (`rindex0 = length − 1 − index0`, `first = index0 == 0`, …). It is an **immutable
+  per-iteration snapshot**: `outer.index0` is the enclosing loop's index at the moment the inner body
+  renders. Because the field set and arithmetic are fixed, the compiler emits the label object into the
+  `each` frame exactly as the interpreter's `iterate` does, and the equality is gated by `test:compile`
+  (interpreter ≡ compiled), like block params.
+. *Shadowing is contained by extending the warn-always lint* ([adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables](/adr/adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables/)
+  §4): warn when a label shadows a likely data field, and *hard-warn* when a label name is itself a bare
+  loop-variable name (`label index0` must not silently re-open the §4 footgun). The risk is lower than
+  for bare loop variables, since a label is an explicit author-chosen name rather than an implicit
+  vocabulary word.
+. *Available in both surface dialects (FullBars + MaxBars)* — *revised at implementation* from the
+  proposed "MaxBars-only". The `label NAME` recognizer lives in the *shared* surface desugar and is gated
+  on the `each` head, not the dialect, so FullBars accepts it too. This is safe because — unlike the bare
+  loop variables, which change bare-name *resolution* and so are MaxBars-only — a label is purely
+  additive new syntax with no Handlebars equivalent: a template that does not write `label NAME` is
+  unaffected, so there is no semantic divergence to contain. Gating it MaxBars-only would have meant
+  threading a flag through the whole desugar/render/compile chain for no behavioural benefit. RawBars,
+  having no surface desugar, has no labels. (The shadow lint below is MaxBars-only, since it reads the
+  bare loop-variable vocabulary.)
+. *No transitive frame-climbing in v1* — one label names *one* enclosing frame. The label object exposes
+  that loop's own state (`this` is its element); it carries *no* `parent` field, so it cannot be used to
+  climb further out. To reach two enclosing loops, label both. This is the guardrail that stops the
+  feature from quietly becoming the `../` stack ADR-001 §4 dropped.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* removes the documented v1 limit; composes with the existing normative loop-variable arithmetic
+  rather than replacing it; reuses the block-param scope-and-bind machinery wholesale, so the engine
+  delta is "reify the frame as an object and bind it" plus one desugar recognizer.
+* *Pro:* no new resolution machinery — `outer.length` is the proven scoped-helper-returning-object +
+  path-lookup pattern (the same shape block params already use).
+* *Con:* a new surface keyword (`label`) and a new immutable-snapshot object; the shadowing surface
+  grows by one lint case. All contained in the MaxBars dialect layer.
+
+## Resolved questions
+
+* *Label syntax* — the `label NAME` clause (Decision §2); available in both surface dialects (Decision §5).
+* *Depth interaction with the recursion budget* ([adr-0012-recursion-budget](/adr/adr-0012-recursion-budget/)) — *none by
+  construction*: a label is one scoped helper, so nesting N labelled loops installs N scoped helpers
+  (ordinary block nesting), not recursion. The budget guards self-inclusion (a partial including
+  itself), which labels do not touch.
+
+## Implementation
+
+Shipped across the five expected phases:
+
+. *Desugar* — `FullBars.Surface.extractLabel` strips a trailing `label NAME` off an `each` head, adds
+  `NAME` to `scope`, and `blockHeadArgs` emits a reserved `@label` marker. `core` `splitBlockArgs` lifts
+  it into a new `label` field (dropped from the positional list) and the engine seam carries it as
+  `Ctl.loopLabel`.
+. *Interpreter* — `Kernel.Prelude.iterate` reifies the frame as a `VObject` (`frameObject`) under the
+  label name, added last to the frame map.
+. *Compiler* — `frameBlock` emits the label to `rt.each`, which binds `frame.binds[label]` to the same
+  field set. *One design refinement surfaced here:* the runtime's `childFrame` now *inherits* its
+  parent's `binds` (an `Object.create` chain), so an outer label — and outer block params — stay visible
+  in a nested block, matching the interpreter's pushed-frame stack. This also fixed a latent, previously
+  untested divergence for nested block-param access. Gated by `test:compile` (`mx:label-*` and
+  `mx:blockparams-nested-outer`, interpreter ≡ compiled).
+. *Lint* — `MaxBars.Lint.labelShadowWarnings` warns when a label name is a bare loop variable.
+. *Docs + tutorial* — this ADR, the MaxBars page's *Labelled loops* section, and a runnable example.
+
+The normative field set shipped as decided — `{ this, index0, index1, rindex0, rindex1, first, last,
+length, key }` — with *no* `parent` (see Decision §6).

+---
+title: "ADR-014: Syntax highlighting derives from the engine lexer"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-014 Highlighting from the lexer
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01. Companion to [ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/)
+(one structural parser) — this record extends the same "one grammar, derived downstream" principle to
+syntax highlighting. Implementation plan: `highlighting-spec.md`.
+
+## Context
+
+FlatBars renders template syntax in (at least) two front-ends — the FlatBars Lab editor (CodeMirror 6,
+a hand-written `StreamLanguage`) and the tutorials site (a regex overlay behind the runnable-example
+card). Each grew its own tokenizer. Together with the engine's own lexer that makes *three* definitions
+of FlatBars surface syntax:
+
+. the authoritative one — `FlatBars.Lexer` + `FlatBars.Token` (`tokenizeInterior`), the meaning-free
+  structural tokenizer ADR-001 rests on, dialect-scoped through `LexOptions` / the `parseExpr` seam;
+. the Lab's template highlighter — a CodeMirror `ViewPlugin` over a hand-written tag regex
+  (`HB_TAG_RE` + `hbMarkFor`); *not* the engine, and a separate regex from (3);
+. the tutorials' regex highlighter (`tutorials/src/lib/highlight.mjs`).
+
+(2) and (3) are *separate* regex approximations of (1) — they drift from the engine and from each
+other (e.g. the Lab's `hbMarkFor` mis-classifies `{{<p}}`/`{{$b}}` inheritance as plain
+expressions; neither handles set delimiters or MaxBars operators). A fourth and fifth definition exist
+for the host *data* format: the tutorials hand-roll a line-regex YAML highlighter, while the Lab uses a
+real `lang-yaml` grammar plus a bespoke value decorator (see `highlighting-spec.md` §1 for the full
+audit). Two template bugs shipped from this:
+
+* *Exhibit A* — `Hello, {{!-- name --}}!` highlighted the comment as closing at the inner
+  `}}`, leaving `--}}!` as plain text. The regex did not know the `{{!-- … --}}`
+  long-comment form, which the engine's `RComment` / `openerLiteralAt` handles.
+* *Exhibit B* — the regex painted an unterminated `{{!--` as a closed comment plus a separate
+  raw tag, while the engine swallowed everything to the next `--}}`. *The highlighter and the
+  engine disagreed about where a tag begins and ends* — i.e. the highlighter lied about what the engine
+  would parse.
+
+This is precisely the class of drift ADR-001 and the project's "one source of truth, derived
+downstream" gates (`check:catalog`, `test:compile`, `examples:verify`) exist to prevent. Highlighting
+had no such gate, so the drift was silent.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *Highlighting is a structural concern and MUST derive from the engine lexer.* Tokenizing template
+  source for display is the same job the meaning-free lexer already does. Front-ends MUST NOT fork the
+  grammar. The engine exposes a tokenization API (`highlightSpans(template, dialect)` →
+  positioned whole-tag spans; a thin `FlatBars.Highlight` core module over the lexer; see
+  `highlighting-spec.md`), shipped in the same `flatbars-js` bundle the Lab and
+  tutorials already load. A single `kind → CSS-class` map is shared; presenters differ (a CodeMirror
+  `ViewPlugin` for the Lab, a highlight-layer overlay for the tutorials) but the *grammar is one*.
+
+. *Per-dialect by construction.* Because the source is the dialect-scoped lexer (`LexConfig`,
+  `LexOptions`, `parseExpr`), each dialect's tag boundaries and roles are coloured correctly without
+  per-dialect highlighter code: set delimiters (the stateful `mustacheDelims` pair) on RawBars/MaxBars/
+  MinBars, the inheritance sigils `{{<}}`/`{{$}}`, and — critically — the clause
+  separators `{{else}}` / `{{elif …}}`, which paint as *statements* only when the head is
+  one the dialect treats as a separator. That set is the parser's own `standaloneSeps`
+  (`["else","elif"]` for the kernel dialects, *empty* for MinBars, where `else` is just a variable) —
+  IoC, the same seam `trimStandalone` consults, never a hardcoded keyword list. A regex cannot even
+  *tokenize* MaxBars (operator chars vs path chars) nor know a dialect's separator set, which is
+  decisive against the regex as a permanent solution. *A tag is coloured as one span by its meaning* —
+  the structural role of its head (interpolation, block, partial, comment, …). Interior tokens
+  (operators, string and number literals) are *not* singled out: a literal carries no meaning of its
+  own beyond "an argument to this tag", so painting it a second colour competes with the tag's role
+  rather than clarifying it. (An earlier iteration tiled each tag with `operator` / `string` / `number`
+  sub-spans; it was removed in favour of this one-colour-per-meaning rule. The per-token `end` offset
+  that enabled it stays in `FlatBars.Token.PosToken`, and now *is* the substrate for the editor token
+  vocabulary's interior axis — `tokenize` ([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/), implemented)
+  carves those interior spans for the LSP/TextMate layer, while `highlightSpans` stays one-colour-per-tag.)
+
+. *A drift gate is mandatory* (`check:highlight`, mirroring `check:catalog`), wired into `npm test`.
+  Highlighting joins "measured, not asserted": a lexer change not reflected in highlighting fails the
+  build.
+
+. *Implemented (the stopgap is retired for template syntax).* The engine API landed as
+  `highlightSpans` (`FlatBars.Highlight`, on the `flatbars-js` facade). Both front-ends now paint
+  template syntax from it — the Lab via the shared `lab/cm-flatbars.mjs` CodeMirror plugin, the
+  tutorials via `highlightTemplate(src, dialect)` rewritten over `highlightSpans`. The template regexes
+  (the Lab's `HB_TAG_RE`/`hbMarkFor`, the tutorials' `TAG_RE`/`highlightTemplate` body) are *gone*.
+  `check:highlight` is now engine-derived (golden = `highlightSpans`), so a lexer change unreflected in
+  highlighting fails the build. An interior-token pass was tried and *reverted*: a tag is coloured as one
+  span by its head's meaning (§2), so operators/strings/numbers inside a tag get *no* span of their own.
+  The enabling substrate stays — `FlatBars.Token.PosToken` carries an `end` offset — and is now consumed
+  by the opt-in LSP/TextMate vocabulary's `tokenize` ([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/),
+  implemented), not by `highlightSpans`. One follow-up
+  remains, an *enhancement, not the bug class this ADR closes*: full CodeMirror 6 adoption in the
+  tutorials (real `lang-yaml`, a single presenter with the Lab), deferred for bundle weight. Host-*data*
+  (YAML) highlighting — the Lab's `yamlDecorator`, the tutorials' `highlightYaml` — is a separate concern
+  and is unchanged. See `highlighting-spec.md`.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): the highlighter shares the parser's tokenizer
+
+This ADR's principle — highlighting derives from the engine lexer — is now
+literal: `tokenizeSpans` no longer re-runs `tokenizeInterior` itself. It scans
+via `tokenizeTemplate` (which now lexes each tag's interior at scan time) and
+carves interior spans from the tag's *pre-lexed* interior — the same `RawTok`
+stream the parser consumes
+([ADR-004](/adr/adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams/) amendment). The
+highlighter and the parser therefore read every interior off the *same* token and
+cannot drift on how it is lexed. Byte-identical: the `check:highlight` golden was
+unchanged by the migration.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* The Lab's and the tutorials' template regexes are retired: both now paint from the shared
+  `highlightSpans`. The `check:highlight` corpus was the acceptance set that the engine-driven
+  highlighter kept green, so the migration was verifiable rather than a leap.
+* `flatbars-js` gained a public, stable tokenization surface (`highlightSpans`) — also useful for future
+  editor features (semantic colouring of known vs unknown helpers via the schema/catalog, error
+  squiggles from the lexer's `ParseError` spans).
+* The golden gate (`scripts/gen-highlight.mjs`) is now an *engine-equivalence* oracle: its golden is
+  `highlightSpans(src, dialect)` from the committed bundle, covering the set-delimiter, per-dialect, and
+  clause-keyword cases a regex cannot. Long `{{!-- … --}}` comments are coloured as one span: the
+  lexer emits them as a span-only `RLongComment` under `keepLongComments` (a flag only the highlighter
+  sets, so the render/compile token stream is unchanged), bounded exactly as the engine parses them —
+  which is what the regex got wrong in Exhibits A/B.

+---
+title: "ADR-015: Mustache set delimiters via a gated lexer mode"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-015 Set delimiters
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-01; narrowed to MinBars-exclusive 2026-06-04
+(see "Scope narrowing" below). MinBars passes 14/14 on the mustache/spec
+`delimiters` module. Lifts the set-delimiters deferral recorded in
+[ADR-007](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/); constrained by
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/) (one structural lexer)
+and [ADR-014](/adr/adr-0014-highlighting-derives-from-lexer/) (no forked
+grammar).
+
+## Context
+
+Mustache lets a template change its own tag delimiters mid-stream:
+`{{=<% %>=}}` switches `{{ }}` to `<% %>` until a later
+`<%={{ }}=%>` switches back. ADR-007 deferred it ("no customer corpus to
+audit"); the tutorial showed it as a static `spec-only` block. It is the last
+unimplemented *core* `mustache/spec` module (delimiters is core, not a
+`~optional` module like inheritance / dynamic-names), so MinBars's
+"Mustache-conformant" claim was previously "conformant except the one module
+we skip."
+
+The decisive constraint, found in the code: **MinBars lexes through the
+*shared* core lexer** — `FlatBars.Lexer.tokenizeTemplate`, the same lexer the
+RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars ladder uses, whose `openerLiteralAt` hardcodes
+`{{` / `{{{` / `{{!--` … via `matchAt cs i "{{"`. Set
+delimiters makes the open/close pair **mutable mid-parse**. So this is a
+shared-lexer question, not a MinBars-local one, and Handlebars (hence
+FullBars / MaxBars) has no `{{=...=}}` — the feature is Mustache-only.
+
+## Decision
+
+Implement set delimiters as a **flag-gated mode of the one core lexer**,
+following the `LexOptions { infixArith }` precedent (the established
+dialect-scoping seam):
+
+. Add `mustacheDelims :: Boolean` to `LexConfig`. When **false** (the default
+  for every dialect except MinBars), the lexer behaves byte-identically to
+  today — the meaning-free core and the Handlebars-family dialects are
+  untouched, and the index-slicing hot path is unaffected.
+. When **true**, the lexer carries a *current* `{ open, close }` pair,
+  initialised to `{{` / `}}`. On encountering a
+  `<open>=A B=<close>` tag it swaps the pair and emits a new
+  `RSetDelim` `RawTok`. Single pass, O(n); spans stay correct because the
+  lexer already threads a `base` offset. No re-lex, no source rewrite, no
+  second lexer. Per the Mustache manual, the new open/close are
+  whitespace-separated and **may not contain whitespace or `=`** — which also
+  makes a space-separated directive value unambiguous to parse.
+
+*Per-dialect flag values:* set-delimiter is a *Mustache* feature, not a
+"non-Handlebars" feature. Only MinBars enables it; the rest of the ladder
+keeps the flag off so the dialect ladder has a single consistent answer to
+"does delimiter switching work here?" — yes only on the Mustache surface.
+
+* *MinBars* — `mustacheDelims = true`. Inline `{{=...=}}` switches the
+  active pair mid-stream; the `{{! @delimiters: <% %> }}` long-comment
+  directive seeds the file's initial pair.
+* *RawBars*, *MaxBars*, *FullBars* — `mustacheDelims = false`. The inline form
+  is rejected at the parser (a `LexError: unexpected character` from the
+  recovering parser, refined into the actionable LSP diagnostic below). The
+  `{{! @delimiters: …}}` long-comment form parses as a normal comment, and the
+  directive inside is silently ignored — the `@`-prefixed directive convention
+  has no meaning outside the Mustache surface.
+
+The off-by-default invariant is the contract: *with the flag off, every
+non-MinBars dialect lexes exactly as before* (byte-identical). This keeps **one
+grammar** (ADR-001 / ADR-014) and confines the stateful behaviour behind a
+single flag whose default preserves today's behaviour everywhere outside
+MinBars.
+
+### Normative rulings (the spec-suite traps)
+
+* *Rebasing scope.* Under custom delimiters, only the **2-char pair + the
+  Mustache sigils** (`# / ^ & > ! =`) rebase. The FlatBars / Handlebars
+  extensions `{{{` (triple), `{{!--` (long comment),
+  `{{{{` (raw block), and `{{<` / `{{$` (inheritance) do
+  **not** rebase — their behaviour under custom delimiters is undefined by the
+  spec. (Unescaped output under custom delimiters is the ampersand form
+  `<%& name %>`.)
+* *Standalone whitespace.* A set-delimiter tag alone on a line is
+  **standalone**: the line is stripped. `RSetDelim` is standalone-eligible in
+  `MinBars.Standalone`.
+* *Partial-boundary reset.* Delimiter changes are **template-scoped** — a
+  partial begins with the default `{{ }}` regardless of the caller's
+  current delimiters.
+* *Highlighting.* `RSetDelim` carries a token kind so `<%=...=%>` and
+  custom-delimited tags colour in both front-ends — folds into the ADR-014
+  Tier-1 `tokenizeTemplate` span work, so the highlighter never disagrees with
+  the engine.
+
+### Editor diagnostic on non-MinBars use
+
+The LSP (`editors/lsp/src/tokens.mjs` `dialectDiagnostics`) surfaces a clear,
+actionable message in every non-MinBars dialect, at the `{{=` offset:
+
+____
+Set-delimiter directives `{{=A B=}}` are not valid in *<Dialect>* —
+they're a Mustache feature reserved for MinBars. Switch the file to MinBars to
+use them (Cmd-Shift-P → Change Language Mode).
+____
+
+This replaces the generic `LexError: unexpected character` the recovering
+parser otherwise emits — users get a remediation instead of a cryptic lexer
+error.
+
+### Measured, not asserted
+
+Corpus-first, per the project's gate culture (`examples:verify`,
+`test:compile`): the `mustache/spec` `delimiters.json` corpus is vendored,
+gated, and currently 14/14 (`test:minbars-spec`). No conformance claim
+precedes a passing fixture.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+* *(A) Mutable delimiters in the core lexer for every dialect* — puts
+  Mustache-only stateful behaviour into the meaning-free core and onto the
+  ladder, which has no such feature. Rejected.
+* *(B) RawBars + MaxBars opt-in via config / runtime / CLI / directive* —
+  shipped in the original 2026-06-01 decision, withdrawn in the 2026-06-04
+  scope narrowing (see "Scope narrowing"). Producing three yeses and one no
+  for the same feature added complexity without a use case; the editor-side
+  diagnostic now explains the MinBars-exclusive policy.
+* *(C) MinBars source-rewrite pre-pass* (normalise `<% %>` →
+  `{{ }}` before lexing) — the rewriter must tokenize with dynamic
+  delimiters anyway (same hard problem), and rewriting **destroys source
+  offsets**, breaking error spans and ADR-014 highlighting. Rejected.
+* *(D) MinBars forks its own Mustache lexer* — a second lexer (ADR-014
+  anti-pattern); duplicates standalone / whitespace logic and will drift.
+  Rejected.
+* *(E) Stay deferred* (status quo) — honest, zero-risk, but leaves MinBars one
+  core module short of the conformance it advertises. Superseded by this ADR
+  once the corpus confirmed there is something to pass.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* `flatbars-js` / the core lexer gain a small, principled config knob and one
+  new `RawTok` (`RSetDelim`); the ladder is provably unaffected (flag off ⇒
+  identical lexing).
+* The conformance table claims delimiters — `test:minbars-spec` confirms
+  14/14.
+* ADR-007's deferral is lifted; the tutorial's static set-delimiters block is
+  a live runnable card.
+* FullBars stays Handlebars-faithful (no set delimiters). The off-by-default
+  invariant keeps existing RawBars / MaxBars / FullBars templates
+  byte-identical.
+
+## Scope narrowing (2026-06-04)
+
+The 2026-06-01 decision enabled `mustacheDelims` on RawBars and MaxBars (via
+the four opt-in mechanisms in alternative (B)) on the rationale that they're
+"non-Handlebars dialects". That rationale was wrong: set-delimiter is a
+*Mustache* feature, not a "non-Handlebars" feature. RawBars (the desugared core
+surface) and MaxBars (the operators + pipes flagship) have no semantic reason to
+ship a Mustache lexer mode; carrying it produced three yeses and one no where
+the dialect ladder benefits from one consistent answer.
+
+The Decision section above is the binding policy as of 2026-06-04. The
+implementation collapsed accordingly:
+
+* `RawBars.coreOptions.lexConfig` and `MaxBars.maxOptions.lexConfig` revert to
+  `defaultLexConfig` (no `mustacheDelims`).
+* `packages/js/src/FullBars/JS.purs` `highlightConfig` matches at the
+  highlight layer for `rawbars`, so highlighting agrees with parsing.
+* The rawbars and maxbars test suites flip from "asserts switching works" to
+  "asserts the inline form is rejected and the long-comment form is ignored".
+* `dialectDiagnostics` (`editors/lsp/src/tokens.mjs`) emits the actionable
+  message described in "Editor diagnostic" above for FullBars / RawBars /
+  MaxBars; MinBars silent.
+
+The four opt-in mechanisms (config / runtime / CLI / directive) listed in
+alternative (B) above are withdrawn — they're no longer reachable from any
+shipped dialect. If a future use case demands cross-dialect support, this
+section becomes the next ADR's "Context".

+---
+title: "ADR-016: MinBars compile-to-JS"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-016 MinBars compile
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted (complete — slices 1–3: interpolation, sections, inverted, partials, inheritance).
+*Date:* 2026-06-01. Revisits the interpret-only decision in [ADR-007](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/); an
+instance of the compile IoC pattern ([ADR-011](/adr/adr-0011-compile-to-js/)).
+
+## Context
+
+The dialect-agnostic compiler (`FlatBars.Compile` = emit driver + an `Emit` record + the
+`flatbars-runtime.mjs` runtime) already serves the whole *ladder*: RawBars (`compileJs`), FullBars
+(`compileSurface`), and MaxBars (`compileMaxJs`, which literally reuses the FullBars surface compiler).
+They share one compiler because they are *one engine* (RefEnv + the reference prelude) differing only in
+surface syntax, so they desugar to one core AST and run on one runtime.
+
+The lone holdout is *MinBars*, deferred to interpret-only by ADR-007. MinBars is a *peer* engine: its
+own `MinEnv` context stack (Mustache walks a stack of frames with parent fallback), polymorphic
+sections (`{{#x}}` = iterate-array / render-once-truthy / skip-falsy), the mustache falsy-set,
+context-inheriting partials, and inheritance — none of which match the RefEnv model the shared runtime
+assumes.
+
+The lever: `MinBars.Surface.desugar` is already a `Template → Template` rewrite into *core helper
+applications* (`mlookup` / `escape` / `section` / `inverted` / `partial` / `parent` / `block`). So
+MinBars already produces the exact core `Template` the emit driver walks — what was missing is a
+*runtime target* for those helpers, not a new AST.
+
+## Decision
+
+Give MinBars a compile path the same way it has an interpret path: plug its *own* `Emit` rules + runtime
+ops into the *reused* emit driver (the IoC move, mirroring its own `Engine m MinEnv`).
+
+* *Emit* (`MinBars.Compile`): the baseline tier (no FullBars `if`/`each` optimiser — MinBars's heads are
+  `section`/`inverted`/…). `escape e` → `rt.esc`, raw output → `rt.out` (both reused: the runtime's
+  `escapeHtml`/`stringify` already match the kernel's, gated by the existing compile conformance);
+  `(mlookup "name")` → `rt.mlookup(env, name)`; `section` → `rt.msection(value, env, fn)` pushing a
+  frame per item; `inverted` → an inline `if (rt.mfalsy(env, value)) { … }`.
+* *Runtime* (`flatbars-runtime.mjs`, `m*` ops): the MinBars "scope" is `{ stack, truthy }`; `mseed`
+  builds the root stack, `mlookup` is `MinBars.Context.mresolve` (implicit-iterator `.`, dotted-name
+  descent, parent-fallback stack walk), `msection` is the polymorphic coercion + push, `mfalsy` is the
+  rule test. The scope is seeded with MinBars' truthiness *callback* (`rt.truthyMustache`; ADR-022
+  replaced the old `$falsy` const), so truthiness is correct for free.
+* *Seam*: `FullBars.JS` exposes `compileMinbars`/`renderMinbars`; the compile-conformance harness
+  (`packages/compile/conformance.mjs`) dispatches the `minbars` dialect and asserts *compiled ≡
+  interpreter* byte-for-byte — the contract that forces the runtime to replicate `MinEnv` exactly.
+
+*Packaging (slice 1):* the `m*` ops live in the shared `flatbars-runtime.mjs` (namespaced) rather than a
+separate `minbars-runtime.mjs`; `MinBars.Compile` lives in the `minbars` package (a new `flatbars-compile`
+dependency, allowed by the isolation invariants — only `rawbars` edges are forbidden). A dedicated
+`minbars-compile` package is the cleaner long-term home and can be split out later.
+
+## Phasing
+
+. *Slice 1:* interpolation (escaped/raw/dotted/implicit/missing), polymorphic sections, inverted
+  sections.
+. *Slice 2 (shipped):* partials, by *inlining* — `compileMinJsWith` splices each static `{{> p}}`
+  into the call site, with `indentTemplate indent` applied to the partial's desugared template (the
+  standalone indent is a compile-time literal). Because the splice lands in the caller's scope, context
+  inheritance is automatic, and because `indentTemplate` runs on the *template* (not the rendered
+  string), a newline produced by an interpolated value is not indented — byte-identical to the
+  interpreter, which renders the same `indentTemplate indent tmpl` under the caller's env (proven by
+  the mustache standalone-indentation case in the corpus). Inlining cannot express a *cycle*, so a
+  *recursive* partial is rejected with a `DisallowedShape` (the interpreter bounds recursion at run
+  time with the recursion budget); a *dynamic-name* partial `{{>* name}}` is rejected too (the name is
+  unknown until run time). Both are loud failures, never a silent miscompile. No runtime/driver change
+  was needed — the slice-1 `m*` ops suffice.
+. *Slice 3 (shipped):* inheritance — also by inlining, since block resolution never consults data, so
+  the whole override structure is static. The inliner threads an *override map* (outer-wins via a
+  left-biased union: the more-derived/inherited override wins) and a *parent depth* (bounded by the
+  recursion budget). `{{<p}}` harvests its body's `{{$b}}` overrides, layers them, and inlines the
+  parent template (`indentTemplate` for a standalone parent — template-level). `{{$b}}` emits the
+  active override (or the default body). §4.6.2 reindentation: a standalone override is dedented at its
+  definition (compile-time, `harvestBlocks`) and re-indented at the expansion site (runtime
+  `rt.mindentOverride` — output-level, so it indents value newlines too, unlike partial indentation);
+  the expansion indent is the tag's own indent, or the default's intrinsic indent computed at compile
+  time from its leading static content. Inheritance "recursion" that terminates via an override (the
+  spec's *Recursion* case) inlines fine; a true cycle is bounded by the budget. A *dynamic-name* parent
+  `{{<* …}}` is rejected (loud).
+
+Each slice is gated by compile conformance before it lands.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* The Lab's "Compiled JS" panel can light up for MinBars (it already gates on `compileToJs` existing) —
+  a follow-up once the bundle re-exports `compileMinJs`.
+* A Mustache template can ship as a standalone JS module (no engine bundle at runtime) — the one real
+  payoff, since Mustache is logic-less (no helpers to inline, unlike Handlebars `if`/`each`).
+* The compile-conformance gate now spans all four engines; a MinBars semantics change that isn't
+  mirrored in the runtime fails the build.
