+---
+title: "ADR-017: Editor support via an engine-backed LSP, with a mandatory TextMate fallback"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-017 Editor support (LSP + TextMate)
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted; the highlighting foundation is *implemented*. *Date:* 2026-06-02. Builds on
+[ADR-014](/adr/adr-0014-highlighting-derives-from-lexer/) (highlighting derives from the lexer) and
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/) (one structural parser); the stateful driver is
+[ADR-015](/adr/adr-0015-set-delimiters/) (set delimiters). This record extends "one grammar, derived
+downstream" from our own front-ends (the Lab, the tutorials) to *third-party editors* — VS Code and
+JetBrains — for production use.
+
+:::note
+*Implemented (semantic-token highlighting + diagnostics).* The token vocabulary, the
+engine-backed language server, the TextMate fallback, and both editor plugins
+landed; *diagnostics* followed via the recovering parser
+([ADR-023](/adr/adr-0023-recovering-parser/)). Only hover/completion and
+Marketplace publishing remain. What shipped:
+
+* `editors/token-vocabulary.json` — the single source of truth the three consumers
+  share (engine `tokenize` kinds, LSP legend, TextMate scopes).
+* `tokenize(template, dialect)` on the `flatbars-js` bundle — the tag-role *and*
+  interior-role (`string`/`number`/`operator`) token stream; `highlightSpans` is
+  now its tag-role projection. Gated by `check:highlight` (pins both views).
+* `editors/flatbars.tmLanguage.json` — the fallback: the well-known Handlebars
+  grammar re-identified as `source.flatbars` and extended for all four dialects
+  (inverse sections, Mustache inheritance, set delimiters, MaxBars operators),
+  keeping its standard scope names so themes colour FlatBars familiarly. Gated by
+  `check:tmgrammar` (per dialect: tag-boundary + literal agreement with the engine).
+* `editors/lsp` — `flatbars-lsp`, the semantic-tokens server (`test:lsp`).
+* `editors/vscode` — the extension bundling the client + grammar (`test:vscode`).
+* `editors/jetbrains` — the Gradle/Kotlin plugin: the TextMate grammar via a
+  `TextMateBundleProvider` (all IDEs), plus the LSP path on Ultimate (`-PwithLsp`;
+  the platform LSP API is Ultimate-only and absent from the open SDK, so the LSP
+  layer is an opt-in build). `test:jetbrains` is the offline gate.
+:::
+
+## Context
+
+Production use needs VS Code and JetBrains plugins with first-class DX. ADR-014 already decided that
+highlighting must derive from the engine lexer rather than a forked grammar, but it spoke to our
+in-process JS front-ends (the Lab's CodeMirror plugin, the tutorials' overlay). Real editors need a
+*delivery mechanism*, and that forces a sharper question than "which grammar format."
+
+The decisive constraint is that highlighting FlatBars is *stateful and content-dependent*:
+
+* *Set delimiters* (ADR-015): after `{{=<% %>=}}` every later tag uses the new pair until
+  `<%={{ }}=%>`. A correct highlighter must carry the *active delimiter pair* as state across the
+  document.
+* *Per-dialect grammar*: the `parseExpr` / `parseHead` seam and `LexOptions` make tag interiors and the
+  legal shape set differ across RawBars / FullBars / MaxBars / MinBars; the separator set that paints as
+  a statement is the parser's own `standaloneSeps` (empty for MinBars), never a fixed keyword list.
+* Raw blocks `{{{{ … }}}}`, long comments `{{!-- … --}}`, the inheritance sigils
+  `{{<}}` / `{{$}}`.
+
+Stateless mechanisms cannot express this. A *TextMate* grammar has a scope stack (begin/end) but no data
+state — it cannot capture "the delimiters are now `<% %>`" and use it later. A *tree-sitter* grammar is
+context-free for the same reason; its only escape hatch is a hand-written C *external scanner*, i.e. a
+second copy of the delimiter logic. So a grammar-format highlighter is *structurally incapable* of being
+correct for FlatBars, and — per ADR-014's Exhibits A & B and the tutorials' YAML `111` bug — any second
+definition of the grammar drifts from the engine.
+
+The engine lexer already implements the state (it threads `mustacheDelims`), is dialect-scoped, and is
+*already JavaScript* (the `flatbars-js` bundle the Lab and tutorials load). The way to highlight
+correctly in any editor is therefore to *run the engine lexer*, not to approximate it.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *Editor support derives from the engine; the authoritative highlighter is the engine lexer delivered
+  as LSP semantic tokens.* A single language server (`flatbars-lsp`, Node, embedding the `flatbars-js`
+  bundle and its `tokenize(template, dialect)` API — the interior-aware superset of ADR-014's
+  `highlightSpans`) computes positioned token kinds for the
+  document — stateful by construction, so set delimiters, dialects, raw blocks and separators are all
+  correct because there is no second grammar to be wrong. Both VS Code (semantic-tokens LSP client) and
+  JetBrains (LSP API, 2023.2+) consume *the same server*; one implementation, all editors. (The JetBrains
+  platform LSP API has historically been Ultimate-only; Community-edition IDEs do not attach the server
+  and see only the TextMate fallback below — which is exactly why that fallback is mandatory, not a reason
+  against the LSP.) The server is
+  also the substrate for the rest of DX — diagnostics from the recovering parser
+  ([ADR-023](/adr/adr-0023-recovering-parser/): ONE parser that recovers, of which the canonical
+  fail-fast `parse` is a projection — not a second engine), helper hover/completion from `preludeSchema`
+  and the catalog, and go-to-partial. Highlighting was the first feature on this substrate, needing *none*
+  of the recovering parser, so it shipped first; diagnostics followed once ADR-023 landed.
+
+. *A shared `flatbars.tmLanguage.json` is a mandatory, committed fallback — not optional.* Every plugin
+  ships it. The LSP is not always present or instant, and some contexts have *no* language server at
+  all, where the TextMate grammar is the only highlighting the user ever sees:
++
+--
+* first paint, before the server activates / attaches;
+* environments with no LSP: code review on GitHub/Gitea, diffs, `bat`/`less`/`cat` previews, marketplace
+  screenshots, documentation code blocks;
+* JetBrains' TextMate-bundle path for files before (or without) the plugin;
+* a degraded/crashed or still-starting server — DX must never fall to *no* colour.
+--
++
+Because those contexts are real and unavoidable, shipping the grammar is non-negotiable. We use the
+*well-known Handlebars TextMate grammar*, re-identified as `source.flatbars` and extended for all four
+dialects (inverse sections, Mustache inheritance `{{<}}`/`{{$}}`, set delimiters, and
+MaxBars operators), keeping its standard scope names (`keyword.control.*`, `support.function.*`,
+`string.quoted.*`, …) *on purpose* — themes already colour them, so FlatBars looks like the Handlebars
+developers know. It colours *only* the template syntax and a leading YAML front-matter block: a FlatBars
+template's output is not necessarily HTML (it may be JSON, SQL, Markdown, plain text), so the grammar's
+HTML/CSS/JS embedding is removed and host text is left plain. It is explicitly *best-effort and
+non-authoritative*: being stateless it cannot follow a
+set-delimiter *switch* (the tags past `{{=A B=}}`) and is FullBars-flavoured (it paints
+`else`/`each` as keywords even in MinBars, and paints RawBars/MaxBars's `extras`-off shapes as valid).
+When the LSP is attached, its semantic tokens are *sparse corrections*, not a blanket re-colour: because
+the floor is now a rich, familiar grammar, the LSP emits a token ONLY where it knows something the
+stateless grammar cannot — dialect-scoped interior operators/literals, set delimiters, and
+dialect-disallowed errors (the vocabulary's `lspEmitKinds`). The structural tags (interpolation, raw,
+blocks, partials, comments) are left to the grammar, so `{{{x}}}` keeps its braces-vs-name colour
+instead of being flattened to one whole-tag semantic token. The grammar is the floor; the engine is the
+ceiling *only where the engine knows more*.
+
+. *The fallback is a derived artifact and MUST be drift-bounded, like every other.* But it is *richer*
+  than the engine — it splits a tag into sigil / name / args / literals, where the engine paints one kind
+  per tag (ADR-014) — so a scope-to-kind bijection does not fit, and we do not force one. `check:tmgrammar`
+  instead pins, *for each dialect*, the two things the engine defines and a stateless grammar can be held
+  to: (a) *tag boundaries* — exactly the characters the engine marks as inside a FlatBars tag are the
+  characters the grammar scopes as a tag (every tag scope ends in `.flatbars`; host text and the YAML
+  front-matter block never do), which catches the Exhibit-A/B begin/end drift across all four dialects; and
+  (b) *literals* — wherever the engine carves a `string`/`number`, the grammar scopes it as one. Everything
+  else (which helper is a keyword, argument and operator colouring) is allowed *enrichment*. Dialect-error
+  shapes and set-delimiter switches are out of scope (the LSP owns them). The gate is wired into `npm
+  test`; ADR-014's stopgap was *time-boxed*, but this fallback is *permanent* (it serves the no-LSP
+  contexts forever), so its gate is permanent too. The token vocabulary (`editors/token-vocabulary.json`)
+  is still the one place the kinds, the LSP legend, and the grammar's literal scopes are defined together.
+
+. *Reject tree-sitter as the FlatBars parser/highlighter.* A tree-sitter grammar is a second source of
+  truth (the drift ADR-001 and ADR-014 exist to prevent); it cannot track the dialect seam without N
+  grammars; its statefulness requires a hand-written C external scanner duplicating set-delimiter logic;
+  and it is not JetBrains' highlighting path, so it would not unify editors. If Zed / Neovim / GitHub
+  tree-sitter highlighting later becomes a goal, a tree-sitter grammar may be added as *another
+  non-authoritative fallback* under the same drift gate — never as the engine's parser.
+
+. *Reject native per-editor lexers* (a JFlex/Kotlin lexer for JetBrains plus a separate VS Code
+  tokenizer). That is two more grammar copies, maximal drift, and double maintenance — the opposite of
+  one source of truth, for no benefit the LSP does not already give.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* One server, two (and more) plugins. The `flatbars-js` bundle runs inside `flatbars-lsp`; the existing
+  `check:bundle` gate keeps the editor's engine from going stale against the PureScript source.
+* The highlighting *layering* — TextMate first-paint, then semantic tokens as authority — is the standard
+  industry pattern (TypeScript, rust-analyzer). At template sizes the semantic round-trip is
+  imperceptible.
+* *Two highlighting representations exist by design* (the engine and the TextMate fallback). Unlike the
+  drift ADR-014 fought, the authority is unambiguous (the engine always wins where it runs), and the
+  fallback is gated, scoped to default delimiters, and labelled — *bounded* drift, not silent drift.
+* The in-process front-ends keep painting from `highlightSpans` (the tag-role projection, ADR-014, one
+  colour per tag); the richer interior axis lives only in `tokenize`, which the editor layer consumes. The
+  TextMate grammar is for *external / no-LSP* contexts, not for our own front-ends.
+* Set-delimiter and MaxBars-operator regions are *knowingly* approximate without a server — documented,
+  and corrected the instant one attaches. That is the honest limit of any stateless fallback, and the
+  reason the fallback is a floor rather than the design.
+
+## Resolved
+
+* *Token vocabulary (resolved — implemented).* The stable kind set (tag-role × interior-role) is
+  `editors/token-vocabulary.json`, the single contract the three consumers share. `highlightSpans` still
+  emits only the tag-role kinds — each tag painted once, by the meaning of its head (ADR-014) — and the
+  interior-role axis (`operator` / `string` / `number`) is carved by the superset `tokenize`, recovered
+  from `FlatBars.Token.PosToken`'s `end` offset exactly as anticipated. The *operation*-kind axis
+  (value / inline / block / operator) it pairs with is owned by
+  [ADR-019](/adr/adr-0019-operation-vocabulary/); completion labels (when they land) should reference
+  that taxonomy rather than coin their own.
+* *Grammar provenance (resolved — adopt the Handlebars grammar + conformance gate).* The fallback is the
+  established Handlebars TextMate grammar, re-identified as `source.flatbars` and extended for the four
+  dialects, kept honest by `check:tmgrammar` (see Decision 3). This was chosen over both a from-scratch
+  hand-authored grammar and generation from token boundaries: reusing the grammar developers' themes
+  already target is what makes FlatBars *look familiar*, which is the fallback's whole job.
+* *Recovering parser (resolved — implemented, [ADR-023](/adr/adr-0023-recovering-parser/)).* The
+  diagnostics layer's prerequisite turned out NOT to be a second parser: there is one recovering parser,
+  and the total fail-fast `parse` is its projection. Diagnostics ship from it (`diagnostics(template,
+  dialect)` → `publishDiagnostics`); hover/completion remain the open follow-on.
+
+## Open questions
+
+* *Incremental semantic tokens.* Whole-document retokenization is fine at current sizes; add range
+  requests / deltas only if a profile shows it (ties to the deferred incremental-parse trigger noted in
+  the parser review).
+* *Hover / completion.* _Resolved — implemented; see the 2026-06-04 amendment below._
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): interior token offsets come from the one tokenizer
+
+The interior-role spans `tokenizeSpans` emits (the `PosToken.end` substrate this
+ADR's semantic-token layer recovers) now come off each `RawTok`'s interior —
+populated by `tokenizeTemplate`, the same tokens the parser consumes — rather than
+a highlighter-private `tokenizeInterior` re-lex
+([ADR-014](/adr/adr-0014-highlighting-derives-from-lexer/) amendment). Offsets
+and the token vocabulary are unchanged — the `check:highlight` golden and the
+`flatbars-lsp` token tests were byte-identical across the migration.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): three release-blockers gate marketplace publishing
+
+A team review of the three integrations (`flatbars-lsp`, the VS Code extension,
+the JetBrains plugin) confirmed the two-layer design of this ADR but found the
+*release readiness* is gated on process and seam gaps, not features. Until the
+three blockers below are closed, the extensions are **not** to be published to the
+VS Code Marketplace / Open VSX / JetBrains Marketplace. The decisions:
+
+. *Activation is unverified end-to-end, so it is release-blocking (VS Code).* The
+  review's first framing was that `activationEvents: []`
+  (`editors/vscode/package.json`) left the language client — and thus the whole LSP
+  ceiling (semantic tokens + diagnostics) — without a trigger. *That framing was
+  wrong, and the manifest validator caught it:* since VS Code 1.74 the `onLanguage`
+  events are *generated* from `contributes.languages`, and `engines.vscode` is
+  `^1.75`, so the extension auto-activates on opening a FlatBars file — declaring
+  the events explicitly is redundant (and now flagged as removable). The real gap
+  is that *nothing proves it*: the smoke test spawns the server over a pipe,
+  bypassing activation entirely, so a regression (a broken client, a dropped
+  language contribution) would ship silently. *Decision (implemented):* keep
+  `activationEvents: []` (rely on the generated events); assert the
+  auto-activation precondition offline in the smoke test (`engines.vscode >= 1.74`
+  and `contributes.languages` ≡ the shared dialect set); and add a *real-IDE* test
+  (`editors/vscode/test/ide`, `npm run test:vscode:ide`) that opens a `.maxbars`
+  fixture in a downloaded VS Code and asserts the extension auto-activates and that
+  a semantic token *and* a published diagnostic actually surface. It is heavy (a VS
+  Code download + a windowed run), so it runs in CI (blocker 2), not in `npm test`.
+
+. *The JVM/LSP path compiles on no CI machine, so it is release-blocking
+  (JetBrains).* `test:jetbrains` validates the bundled JS transport (descriptors,
+  grammar canonicality, an LSP round-trip) but never compiles Kotlin; the
+  Ultimate-only LSP layer (`-PwithLsp`, the platform LSP API absent from the open
+  SDK) is built nowhere we control. *Decision (implemented):* a path-filtered
+  workflow, `.github/workflows/editors.yml`, with two jobs — a `gates` job
+  (the editor node gates + the real-IDE VS Code test under `xvfb`) and a
+  `jetbrains-build` job that provisions JDK 17 + Gradle (there is no wrapper in the
+  repo) and runs `gradle buildPlugin -PwithLsp`, downloading the IntelliJ IDEA
+  Ultimate SDK so the Ultimate-only LSP layer compiles. Neither client now ships
+  code that has only ever been type-checked by hand.
+
+. *The "one vocabulary, three consumers" seams are ungated, so they are
+  release-blocking (shared).* The contract this ADR rests on has unchecked joints:
+  `lspEmitKinds` (`editors/token-vocabulary.json`) drives the sparse-correction
+  design but is pinned by no test — adding `expr` to it would silently flatten
+  `{{{x}}}` to one colour, the exact failure Decision 1's floor design
+  guards against, with every gate green; `check:tmgrammar` asserts tag boundaries
+  and literals but *not* that the grammar's scope names still match the vocabulary's
+  `tmScopes`; and the embedded engine bundle (`lab/vendor/flatbars-engine.mjs`,
+  re-exported by `editors/lsp/src/engine.mjs`) carries no API-version the server can
+  assert. Packaging compounds it: the two `sync-assets.mjs` scripts call `esbuild`
+  *unpinned* and duplicate the dialect list by hand, undercutting the
+  byte-reproducibility `check:bundle` enforces (it pins `esbuild@0.23.0`).
+  *Decision (implemented):* add a vocabulary-integrity gate, `check:vocab`
+  (`scripts/check-vocab.mjs`, in `npm test`), asserting engine kinds ≡ vocabulary
+  kinds — witnessed by the `check:highlight` corpus, so there is no second corpus —
+  the *pinned* `lspEmitKinds` set, the LSP legend derivation, and grammar scope
+  names ⊇ vocabulary `tmScopes`; and pin + centralise the packaging `esbuild` in
+  `editors/shared/sync.mjs` (the shared bundle step + single-sourced language set,
+  pinned to the `esbuild@0.23.0` `gen:bundle` already uses). The "engine-shape
+  compatibility" the bundle API-version idea targeted is met by this gate (kinds ≡
+  vocabulary ≡ legend) together with `check:bundle`'s existing byte-identical
+  freshness guarantee, rather than a runtime version constant — no change to the
+  generated engine bundle, and the contract is checked in CI rather than asserted
+  at startup.
+
+*Rejected at the same review:* making the LSP emit *full* semantic tokens (instead
+of sparse corrections over the TextMate floor). It contradicts Decision 2 of this
+ADR — the floor must stand alone in no-LSP contexts (GitHub, `bat`, diffs) and full
+emission flattens the braces-vs-name distinction. The sparse split is kept; only
+its seam is gated (blocker 3).
+
+*Unchanged / still deferred:* the TextMate floor remains the guaranteed baseline
+(Community / no-LSP users are first-class); incremental `semanticTokens/range` is
+tracked but non-blocking. (Process note: the review's draft flagged a committed
+`editors/vscode/dist/` as a high risk; `git ls-files` shows it untracked —
+`.gitignore` covers `dist/` — so that finding was withdrawn.)
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): hover + completion
+
+The third capability on this substrate (after highlighting and diagnostics) is
+hover + completion, the open question above. They are *not* keyed to the recovering
+parser's `NodeError` nodes after all — the operation set is static, so a per-edit
+parse buys nothing. Instead:
+
+* `FullBars.Catalog.operations` projects `preludeSchema` (the same single source the
+  helper catalog renders) to each operation's name, its ADR-019 kind
+  ([ADR-019](/adr/adr-0019-operation-vocabulary/); `value`/`inline`/`block`,
+  derived structurally — `operator` is a MaxBars surface form, not a runtime kind),
+  arity, source (`registered`/`scoped`/`alias`/`synonym`), and any alias/synonym
+  target. `scripts/gen-operations.mjs` writes that to `editors/operations.json`,
+  gated by `check:operations` (in `npm test`) exactly like the catalog — so the
+  editor can never offer an operation the engine does not know. The server inlines
+  it like the token vocabulary.
+* The server gates hover and completion on being *inside a tag*, decided by the
+  engine's own `tokenize` (not a re-implemented lexer) — the offset must fall in a
+  `tag` span and not in an interior `string`/`number` literal. *Hover* on a known
+  operation reports its kind, arity, alias/synonym relationship, a signature
+  *synthesised from the kind*, and its one-line prose doc. *Completion* inside a tag
+  offers the operations, excluding deprecated aliases (they still hover, so existing
+  code is explained) and sorting scoped variables after helpers.
+
+The prose comes from a **required `doc` field on `OperationDef`** (a follow-up to
+this amendment): the single source, populated for every operation and
+compiler-enforced by the `valDef`/`gen` smart constructors, so an operation cannot
+ship undocumented and there is no parallel doc table to drift. (This supersedes
+this amendment's first cut, which deliberately carried *no* doc string for exactly
+the drift fear — solved instead by making the prelude itself the one source.)
+Scoped variables live outside `operationDefs` and carry no doc, so hover simply
+omits the line. The long-form reference prose stays in `prelude.adoc`; `doc` is the
+one-line summary. Covered by `test:lsp` (unit + protocol) and the real-IDE path.
+
+A `codeAction` quick-fix completes the loop: on a deprecated alias or a
+non-canonical scoped variable the server offers a one-click *rewrite to the
+canonical form* (`downcase`→`lowercase`, `index`→`index0`, `partial-block`→`yield`).
+The replacement is the `canonical` field already in `operations.json` — aliases from
+`preludeAliases`, scoped from `Kernel.Prelude.scopedCanonical` (the shared table the
+`Linter.Aliases` lint and the `flatbars lint` CLI also read; *not* `synonymOf` —
+synonyms are endorsed and never offered). It is dialect-scoped: alias rewrites apply
+anywhere, the scoped rewrite only in RawBars/MaxBars (FullBars/MinBars keep
+Handlebars' `@index`/`@partial-block`). So the same single source drives the lint
+(report), the CLI (`flatbars lint`), and the editor (one-click fix).
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): support matrix locked in
+
+The JetBrains side now formally targets **all JetBrains IDEs (TextMate floor)
++ IDEA Ultimate (LSP ceiling)**. The default Gradle build (`buildPlugin`)
+produces a TextMate-only plugin compatible with every Community + Ultimate
+IDE; the `-PwithLsp` build adds the `flatbars-lsp` server consumed via the
+Ultimate-only platform LSP API. `runPluginVerifier` is wired against the
+since-build range so any compatibility regression fails before publish.
+
+Community-edition users see an `EditorNotificationProvider` banner on first
+opening a FlatBars file, linking to the Ultimate upgrade path so the missing
+LSP capabilities never surface as a silent gap.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): editor floor refined to ERB-canonical scopes
+
+The TextMate floor switched from FlatBars-bespoke `meta.function.*` /
+`meta.variable.unescaped.*` scopes to the canonical ERB/PHP/EJS pattern:
+every brace cluster carries `punctuation.section.embedded.{begin,end}`,
+every tag region carries `meta.embedded.{line,block}`, and control-tag
+sigils split out as `keyword.control.{section,inheritance,import}`. Themes
+that style ERB braces now style FlatBars braces identically with zero
+hardcoded colour in either editor manifest.
+
+`#tag_interior` patterns added on every expression-bearing tag rule paint
+the body's literals (`string.quoted.*`, `constant.numeric.*`,
+`constant.language.*` for `true`/`false`/`null`), operators
+(`keyword.operator.*`), subexpression parens (`punctuation.section.parens`),
+list-literal brackets (`punctuation.section.brackets`), and path separators
+(`punctuation.accessor`).
+
+LSP `shrinkToInner` trims `{`/`}`/`~`/whitespace off every tag-level
+semantic-token span before emission, so the `keyword`/`set-delimiter`/`error`
+spans cover only the inner body and leave the braces to the grammar's
+embedded scope. `paintOperations` adds a new `operation` semantic kind that
+paints helper names from `operations.json` in head / subexpression-head /
+pipe-target positions; gated by the catalogue so plain variables stay
+default-coloured.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): short-form dialect extensions + hybrid templates
+
+Each dialect now ships two equivalent native extensions — the long form
+(`.rawbars`/`.minbars`/`.fullbars`/`.maxbars`) and a short alias
+(`.rbars`/`.mbars`/`.fbars`/`.xbars`). Both resolve to the same language id;
+both are listed in every consumer (`shared/sync.mjs`, VS Code's
+`package.json`, JetBrains's TextMate bundle, the grammar's `fileTypes`,
+LSP's `dialectForUri`). The packagers' language tables are now codegenerated
+from the single `LANGUAGES` source so adding an extension touches one place.
+
+`editors/flatbars-injection.tmLanguage.json` is an injection grammar with
+`injectTo` covering 26 common host scopes (`source.java`, `source.ruby`,
+`source.python`, …, `text.html.basic`). Paired with `files.associations`
+(`*.java.xbars` → `java`), the host paints its native syntax and the
+injection layers `{{…}}` tag highlighting on top. The LSP attaches to the
+host — hybrid templates are syntax-only for tag intelligence; users wanting
+full IntelliSense open with the dialect's language id.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): capability matrix split into ADR-026
+
+The full list of LSP capabilities we ship vs deliberately omit (the latter
+being principled design decisions tied to the engine's deliberately
+absent cross-template scope graph) lives in
+[ADR-026](/adr/adr-0026-editor-capability-matrix/).

+---
+title: "ADR-018: User-defined helpers (JS `registerHelper`), inline-only and dual-mode"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-018 User-defined helpers
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted. *Date:* 2026-06-02. Builds on
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/) (helpers are the meaning plug-in) and
+[ADR-011](/adr/adr-0011-compile-to-js/) (compile ≡ interpret). Extends the FullBars
+Handlebars-faithfulness claim ([fullbars-compat](/engine/fullbars-compat/)) from syntax/semantics to the one piece of the
+Handlebars *workflow* that was missing: `Handlebars.registerHelper(name, fn)`.
+
+## Context
+
+A JS host can render and compile FullBars, but cannot supply its own helper:
+`Handlebars.registerHelper('loud', s => s.toUpperCase())` has no equivalent. Helpers are the IoC
+plug-in (ADR-001) — but the plug-in language has been PureScript (`Kernel.Prelude`), and the JS facade
+ships only that curated prelude. For real Handlebars users, registering a helper is the *single most
+common* extension, so "Handlebars-faithful" without it is faithful to the grammar and unfaithful to the
+workflow. The feature is genuinely *cross-cutting* — four seams move together:
+
+. *Two execution modes.* FlatBars runs templates two ways and gates that they agree byte-for-byte
+  (`test:compile`, ADR-011). A user helper must work in *both* the interpreter and the compiled module,
+  or be explicitly mode-limited. The compiled runtime already has a closed helper registry
+  (`flatbars-runtime.mjs`: `const helpers = {…}` + `rt.call` → `UnknownHelper`); the interpreter
+  (PureScript) has an extensible env (`Kernel.Env.registerAll`) but *no* FFI to adopt a JS function as a
+  `Helper` over the `Value` type.
+. *Escaping.* The reference engine never auto-escapes raw output and escapes `Value` strings in
+  `{{ }}`. A JS helper returns a string; that must land as an *escaped* `VString` in
+  `{{ }}` (raw in `{{{ }}}`), with a `SafeString`-equivalent escape hatch.
+. *Validation.* Unknown helpers are a schema error (`Kernel.Walk`, `allowUnknown`) and a runtime
+  `UnknownHelper`. A registered helper must extend the schema or it is rejected before it runs.
+. *Security.* In a *library* host, a helper is the host's own JS — no new risk. In the *Lab*, the user
+  types both template and helper into one page, and workspaces are shareable by URL: helper *source*
+  riding along in a link would let a shared link execute attacker JS in the victim's origin. FlatBars's
+  deliberate "no template `eval` / no render `policy`" stance is about *template* eval; host-registered
+  helpers are a different axis — but the Lab blurs host and template.
+
+A block helper (`{{#my}}…{{/my}}`) is a fifth seam this ADR deliberately did *not* open: at the
+time, the compiled runtime's `rt.block` refused every block helper except the internal `apply`, so a
+custom block helper could not satisfy compile ≡ interpret without generic block emission the emitter
+lacked.
+
+:::note
+*Superseded for block helpers by [ADR-020](/adr/adr-0020-user-block-helpers/).* The
+:::
+`blockHelperMissing` work gave the emitter exactly that generic block path (`rt.block` now carries the
+body as a callback), so user-defined block helpers are now supported on FullBars (one `registerHelper`,
+usage-decided `options.fn`/`inverse`). The "inline-only" limit below describes this ADR's v1, not the
+current state.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *User-defined helpers are inline-only, dual-mode, and escaped-by-default.* A host registers
+  `name → (args…) → value` functions; they are usable in both the interpreter and the compiled module,
+  and produce escaped output in `{{ }}` unless the value is marked safe.
+
+. *One registration feeds both modes.* The facade marshals each JS helper into (a) a PureScript
+  `Helper` over `Value` (via an FFI call site) registered into the render env, and (b) the compiled
+  runtime registry (`rt.register`). Both paths therefore execute *the same* JS function with *the same*
+  marshalling, so `test:compile` stays byte-identical — and the equivalence is gated with custom-helper
+  cases.
+
+. *The marshalling contract.* Arguments marshal `Value → JS` (string/number/boolean/null/array/object);
+  surface hash args (`key=value`) arrive as a trailing plain-object argument (the engine already
+  desugars them to a dict). The return marshals `JS → Value`: a string ⇒ `VString` (escaped in
+  `{{ }}`); `safe(string)` — a sentinel from the bundle's exported `safe` — ⇒ `VSafe` (raw),
+  the `SafeString` equivalent. A thrown JS error becomes a located render/compile error, never an
+  uncaught throw.
+
+. *Registered names extend the schema.* Helpers registered for a run are added to the validation schema
+  (known name, inline kind, `AnyArity` unless declared), so they neither trip "unknown helper" nor lose
+  the arity diagnostics the prelude gets.
+
+. *An explicit per-call bag; no global registry.* The one facade primitive is
+  `renderWith(helpers, partials, template, data)` (plus `safe`) — a helpers *bag* `{ name: fn }` passed
+  per call, with *no* global mutable registry (clean for tests and for a shared Lab). There is
+  deliberately *no* `compileWith`: compilation emits `rt.call(name, …)` for any non-built-in head
+  regardless of helpers, and the host binds them at run time via `rt.register` — so the bag is a
+  *render-time* concern, not a compile-time one. The familiar `Handlebars.registerHelper(name, fn[,
+  arity])` spelling is a *source-level* affordance, not a stateful facade global: the Lab and tutorials
+  inject a `registerHelper` function into the user's helper source (`lab/helpers.mjs` `buildHelpers`),
+  which accumulates the bag they then pass to `renderWith`. This keeps the migrator's spelling while
+  honouring "no global mutable registry" — the global shim an earlier draft proposed is exactly the
+  hidden state that line rejects.
+
+. *The Lab runs helpers in a Worker.* Custom helper JS is evaluated and executed in a *Worker*
+  (`lab/helpers-worker.mjs`), never on the main thread — a Worker has no DOM and no `window`, so a
+  shared workspace's helper code cannot read or deface the playground page. This *isolation* is the
+  mechanism (it supersedes the earlier confirm-prompt: even auto-run shared code can't touch the page).
+  Because the render then crosses a thread boundary while the Lab's `run()` is synchronous, the Worker
+  renders *out of band* — its result is cached by input key and painted when fresh; a miss kicks off the
+  async render, which re-runs once it lands. A Worker is not a full capability jail (it still has
+  `fetch`); it removes the page-takeover surface, which is the threat a shared "playground link" poses.
+  The Lab surfaces helpers as a *separate* `helpers.js` editor (its own explorer group / tab / share
+  field `h`), FullBars-only — distinct from the JSONata data `transform`, because helpers extend the
+  *engine* while the transform pre-processes the *data*. (RawBars/MaxBars helper terminology is
+  [ADR-019](/adr/adr-0019-operation-vocabulary/)'s concern, not this one.)
+
+## Consequences
+
+* `flatbars-js` gains a public helper API — `renderWith(helpers, partials, template, data)` and `safe` —
+  and the compiled runtime gains `rt.register`/`rt.safe` and a host-registry fallback in `rt.call`. (The
+  Handlebars-style `registerHelper` is a source-level affordance the Lab/tutorials inject, per Decision 5,
+  not a facade export.) The existing `check:bundle` gate keeps the editor engine in step.
+* The interpreter gains a small, contained FFI surface (a marshaller calling a JS function over JSON);
+  the canonical PureScript `prelude`/`render` are unchanged — the FFI lives at the facade boundary.
+* `test:compile` is extended with custom-helper cases; the equivalence invariant now also covers
+  host-supplied meaning.
+* Two new honest limits, documented in-source: *block* custom helpers are unsupported (compile can't
+  express them), and the Lab's helper sandbox is a Worker, not a full capability jail — adequate for a
+  playground, called out as such.
+
+## Alternatives rejected
+
+* *Global mutable `registerHelper` as the primitive* (Handlebars-style). Hidden state poisons a shared
+  Lab and test isolation; the bag-per-call primitive, with `registerHelper` injected at the *source*
+  level (not a facade global), gives the familiar spelling without the global.
+* *Compile-only or interpret-only helpers.* Either breaks `test:compile` or breaks the Lab's live
+  render. Dual-mode through one registration is the only option that preserves both.
+* *Custom block helpers in v1.* No compiled equivalent (`rt.block`), so they cannot be made
+  mode-equivalent; deferred until/unless the emitter gains generic block emission.
+* *Running Lab helpers on the main thread.* Shared-link code execution in the victim's origin; Worker
+  isolation (no DOM/page access) is the floor, and supersedes the earlier confirm-prompt.
+
+## Open questions
+
+* *Declared helper arities* — *done.* `registerHelper(name, fn, arity)` accepts an optional arity (a
+  number ⇒ exactly N, `[min, max]` ⇒ a range / at-least when `max` is `null`/`Infinity`, omitted ⇒
+  any). A mismatch reports the *same* `ArityError` text the prelude's arity-checked helpers produce, in
+  both the interpreter and the compiled runtime. A declared *kind* (value / inline / block / operator)
+  follows [ADR-019](/adr/adr-0019-operation-vocabulary/)'s owned taxonomy; editor completion from a
+  declared kind/arity (ADR-017) remains future work.
+* *Capability scoping in the Lab.* The Worker removes DOM/ambient authority but not all of a Worker's
+  own globals; a tighter capability jail is future work if abuse appears.

+---
+title: "ADR-019: The operation model — \"operation\" / \"definition\" natively, \"helper\" at the host boundary"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-019 Operation vocabulary
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted — *implemented*. The `Helper` → `Operation` rename landed in one gated commit
+(build + `test:compile` byte-identical + `check:catalog` + `check:bundle`); the `concepts` §1 reframe and
+`#glossary` are in place; the host API keeps the frozen `helper` word; and `check:glossary` gates the two
+registers' agreement. The conditions below (frozen boundary, single gated rename, owned kind taxonomy)
+are met. *Date:* 2026-06-02. Builds on
+[the core model](/concepts/) §1–4 (everything is an application; there are *no variables*; the head
+is always a name; scope is install/remove of names) and
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/) (the meaning plug-in). Constrains, but does not
+revert, [ADR-018](/adr/adr-0018-user-defined-helpers/) (`registerHelper`). This record is about
+*naming*, not mechanism: the mechanism is fixed; what we *call* it in the native dialects has been wrong.
+
+## Context
+
+FlatBars inherited the word *helper* from *Handlebars* — not Mustache. Mustache has no helpers: it is
+"logic-less," and its only extension point is an in-data *lambda*. *Helper* is a Handlebars coinage —
+`Handlebars.registerHelper`, and the built-ins `if` / `each` / `with` / `unless` / `lookup` that
+Handlebars itself calls helpers. In Handlebars the word is honest: it has real variables (a
+`{{name}}` is a path lookup), and a *helper* is the bolt-on for when a path is not enough — the
+auxiliary that *helps* the real content. That is the sense the team objects to: helper as *subordinate*.
+
+In FlatBars that sense is a falsehood. [concepts](/concepts/) §1 is explicit: there are *no
+variables*; `{{{city}}}` *calls* the operation `city`. The thing the `{{ }}` family treats as an
+afterthought is, here, the entire language. Keeping "helper" as the native noun imports an ideology
+(logic-less-template-plus-escape-hatch) that §5 ("no keywords — not even `else`") already rejects, and it
+*hides the one genuinely new thing the model says*.
+
+That new thing is a dissolution. The `{{ }}` family splits its extension story across *two*
+languages and *two* mechanisms:
+
+* a *lambda* (Mustache), a function placed *in the data*, invoked when its name resolves at a leaf;
+* a *helper* (Handlebars), a function registered *on the side*, applied to a block or an interpolation.
+
+This is a *binding-site* distinction: in-data vs registered. FlatBars has *one* binding site — the
+operation environment (§4). A Mustache lambda-at-a-leaf is just a *nullary operation installed in scope*
+(by a block or the host); a Handlebars block helper is just a *block operation*. One axis, not two.
+"Helper" buried this; a truer noun should advertise it.
+
+The countervailing force is migration. [host-api](/engine/host-api/) §7.4 is a deliberate
+Handlebars→FlatBars dictionary, and ADR-018 *just* shipped `registerHelper` because "Handlebars-faithful
+without it is faithful to the grammar and unfaithful to the workflow." Renaming the word a migrator types
+spends the adoption capital ADR-018 was paid to build.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *Two registers, split by audience.*
++
+** *Native conceptual register* — [concepts](/concepts/) and the RawBars / MaxBars dialect docs,
+   *and the internal code identifiers*. The primary noun is *operation* (the thing a name invokes at a
+   call site); the thing *installed in the environment* is a *definition*. A name *resolves* to a
+   definition in the current *scope*; applying it is an *operation*.
+** *Boundary / compatibility register* — the JS host facade. `renderWith` and the source-level
+   `registerHelper` affordance (ADR-018) and the §7.4 migration table *keep the word "helper,"*
+   documented as: a *helper is how a host registers an operation*. The migrator never loses the term;
+   the newcomer never inherits the lie. *This boundary word is frozen* — `helper` is the permanent
+   migration anchor ADR-018 paid for, and is never renamed even as the internals become `Operation`;
+   that frozen boundary is what makes the rename below safe. (There is no `compileWith`: compilation is
+   helper-agnostic — it emits `rt.call`, bound at run time — see ADR-018.)
+
+. *Operations have two kinds, the contract already forces them.* The type
+  `Ctl m env -> Array Value -> m Value` ([host-api](/engine/host-api/) §7.3) distinguishes *inline*
+  operations (ignore the control handle) from *block* operations (use it). *Values* are not a third kind:
+  a value is a *nullary inline operation* — there being no variables, that is the only way a value appears.
+
+. *Rename the internal type `Helper` → `Operation`.* The kernel/fullbars/compile `Helper` type, the
+  prelude table, and the schema's kind language (`inline` / `block`, arity) read as operations and
+  definitions. The JS-facing `registerHelper` and the rest of the `flatbars-js` facade are the *explicit
+  exception* — they stay, by Decision 1.
+
+. *MaxBars gets a surface gloss, not a new model.* The infix symbols `+ >= |` are *operators* (surface
+  sugar); prefix heads and pipe stages are *operations*. We keep the entrenched word "operator" rather
+  than coin a replacement — but because *operator* and *operation* differ by one letter, every use must
+  carry the contrast: an **operator is surface sugar that desugars to an operation** (never standalone).
+  The glossary pairs them on one line for exactly this reason. There is *no "function"* —
+  [concepts](/concepts/) §3 forbids callable values, so "function" would promise first-class
+  functions the language does not have. Both desugar to the same core `App`
+  ([concepts](/concepts/) §8), so the two surface words sit over one core, exactly as "one parser,
+  four languages / one compiler" already claims.
+
+. *Say the dissolution out loud.* [concepts](/concepts/) §1 gains one sentence: FlatBars has no
+  logic-less core for an operation to be an *escape hatch from* — application *is* the language, so an
+  operation is not a "helper" in the subordinate sense; and a glossary records
+  *operation / definition / scope / inline / block / operator* each with its host-API synonym.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *A deliberate, documented asymmetry*: the internal type is `Operation`, the host registrar is
+  `registerHelper`. This is the cost of keeping ADR-018's migration value while telling the native model's
+  truth. It is ratified here so a contributor meeting `registerHelper : … -> Operation` reads it as intent,
+  not drift.
+* *A new normative glossary* ([concepts](/concepts/) or a `glossary.adoc`) becomes the single
+  teachable artifact for the two registers — and it is *gated*, not prose-on-trust: a `check:` (mirroring
+  `check:catalog`) asserts that every native term carries its host-API synonym and that the
+  [host-api](/engine/host-api/) §7.4 migration table and the glossary agree on the
+  operation↔helper / definition / scope / inline / block / operator mapping. A drift in either fails the
+  build, so the two registers cannot silently diverge. The gate checks *terms*, not prose, to avoid a
+  maintenance tax.
+* *This ADR owns the kind taxonomy.* The single, shared set of operation kinds is *value* (a nullary
+  inline operation), *inline* (n-ary), *block*, and *operator* (the MaxBars surface form). ADR-018's
+  declared arities and [ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/)'s catalog-driven completion both
+  *reference* this taxonomy rather than coining their own labels. (Note: the kind is *inline*, not
+  "transform" — "transform" is the Lab's JSONata data-preprocess and must not be overloaded as a kind.)
+* *The `Helper` → `Operation` rename is wide and mechanical* across kernel / fullbars / compile and the
+  schema language, and lands in *one* commit gated by a hard checklist, all green:
++
+--
+  . `npm run build` — every package compiles under the new type name;
+  . `npm test` — full suite, including `npm run check:catalog` (the catalog prose shifts with the prelude
+    vocabulary, so `npm run gen:catalog` is regenerated in the same commit);
+  . `npm run test:compile` — *byte-identical* compiled-vs-interpreted output, proving the rename is purely
+    nominal (no semantics change);
+  . `npm run check:bundle` — the editor bundle tracks the renamed source.
+--
++
+The boundary word `helper` (Decision 1) does *not* move in this commit — only the internal `Operation`
+type, the prelude/schema kind language, and `concepts`/dialect prose.
+
+## Alternatives rejected
+
+* *Keep "helper" everywhere.* Maximizes familiarity, but cements the falsehood in the native model and
+  leaves the lambda/helper dissolution unsaid — the very insight that distinguishes FlatBars from the
+  family it parses.
+* *Rename to "function."* Vetoed by [concepts](/concepts/) §3: nothing produces a callable value and
+  `Value` is free of functions. "Function" would set an expectation the language exists to deny.
+* *"Word" / Forth dictionary framing.* Most honest to the model (scope *is* a dictionary, §4), but opaque
+  to the `{{ }}`-family audience the dialects are for. Retained as *explanatory* framing in prose, not as
+  the surface noun.
+* *Docs-only reframe (leave code as `Helper`).* Considered and rejected by the team: a `concepts`/dialect
+  vocabulary that the type names contradict trains contributors back into "helper." The rename is the
+  cost of coherence.
+* *Open custom block operations to make the model fully uniform.* Out of scope and orthogonal —
+  ADR-018 defers custom *block* helpers for a compile-equivalence reason; this ADR only renames what
+  exists.
+
+## Open questions
+
+* *Schema kind labels* — *resolved* (see Consequences): the taxonomy is *value* / *inline* / *block* /
+  *operator*, with `value` derived from `inline` + arity 0 internally and surfaced as its own label to
+  the catalog/LSP. "transform" is explicitly *not* a kind (it is the Lab's data-preprocess).
+* *Naming `definition` vs `binding` for the environment entry.* "Definition" reads well in prose;
+  "binding" is more precise about the name↔meaning pairing. This ADR picks *definition*; revisit if the
+  glossary proves it ambiguous against block-installed scope.
+
+## Addendum: host-registered block operations for RawBars and MaxBars (design)
+
+*Status:* Accepted (team-reviewed). Reopens the *"open custom block operations"* alternative this ADR
+deferred — now unblocked, because [ADR-020](/adr/adr-0020-user-block-helpers/) built the block-operation
+machinery (the `Engine.blockArgs` seam, `Ctl.hash`/`blockParams`, the `rt.block` channel, and a JS
+marshaller) and proved it byte-identical across interpreter and compiler. Only one dialect (FullBars) wired
+a host registrar to it. This addendum extends host registration to *RawBars* and *MaxBars*, and settles
+what they expose and what they call it.
+
+The review's conditions, folded in: the registrars use *operation* (never `helper`) for the native
+dialects (Dana); there is *no* `compileWithOperations` — compilation stays operation-agnostic, emitting
+`rt.call` bound at run time, exactly as ADR-018 set up (Lena); and the `test:compile` harness must register
+operations through each dialect's compile + render path so the new cases gate *both* paths (Priya).
+
+### The vocabulary fork (resolved)
+
+ADR-018 shipped `renderWith` / `registerHelper` for FullBars; Decision 1 above froze *helper* as that
+facade's boundary word — the *Handlebars-migration anchor*. The fork: when RawBars and MaxBars gain a
+registrar, is the boundary word still *helper*, or *operation*?
+
+*Decision: the boundary word is dialect-scoped, not global.* FullBars keeps `renderWith` / `registerHelper`
+— it is the Handlebars-faithful surface, and "helper" is the migrator's term it was paid to keep. RawBars
+and MaxBars are *native* dialects with no Handlebars-migration debt — RawBars is the very dialect that
+*rejects* the helper framing (concepts §1) — so their registrars use the native noun: a host registers an
+*operation*. The frozen "helper" of Decision 1 is thereby scoped to *FullBars' facade* (the anchor it was
+created for), not imposed on dialects that never had it. This keeps each facade honest to its own dialect's
+register and is exactly the two-register model applied at the boundary, not just in the docs.
+
+### What each dialect exposes
+
+* *RawBars* — `renderWithOperations(operations, partials, template, data)` (and the source-level
+  `registerOperation(name, fn[, arity])` affordance, mirroring `registerHelper`). RawBars is the
+  desugared core surface: it has *no surface sugar*, so a block head emits no `@hash`/`@param` markers — a
+  RawBars block operation therefore gets `options.fn`/`options.inverse` (and `options.fn(ctx, { data })`
+  for scoped vars) but *no* `options.hash` and no `as |…|` block params (there is no surface to write
+  them). Resolution stays *strict* — an unknown operation is `UnknownHelper`, never `blockHelperMissing`
+  (RawBars has no implicit-section policy; ADR-020's lenient resolve is FullBars/MaxBars only).
+* *MaxBars* — `renderWithOperations(...)` over the MaxBars surface (infix/pipes/loop vars). It desugars the
+  same `@hash`/`@param` markers, so a MaxBars block operation gets the *full* surface: `fn`/`inverse`/`hash`
+  + `options.fn(ctx, { data, blockParams })`, and the lenient `blockHelperMissing` resolve it inherits.
+  Block params (`as |a b|`) parse because the MaxBars head grammar omits its top-level *pipe* rung, leaving
+  a bar in head position to serve as the block-parameter delimiter — exactly as FullBars and the core
+  parser already treat it. The only head-position consequence: to *pipe* a block argument, parenthesise it
+  (`{{#each (xs | f) as |x|}}`), which re-enters the full expression grammar.
+
+### Mechanism — reuse, do not rebuild
+
+The kernel already supports all of this; the work is two thin facades plus marshalling, no new engine
+machinery:
+
+* The JS marshaller that turns a host function into an `Operation` (inline *or* block, usage-decided, with
+  `options.hash`/`fn`/`inverse` + the `{ data, blockParams }` frame) is *dialect-agnostic* — `FullBars.JS`'s
+  `mk` is lifted to a shared helper and reused by all three registrars.
+* RawBars renders through the *strict* `runResolved` (registering the operations into the env via
+  `registerAll`); MaxBars through the *lenient* `runResolvedLenient` with `maxOptions` + `maxLoopVars`, the
+  same path `renderMax` already uses. Each gets a `…WithOperations` entry in its package, surfaced on the
+  `flatbars-js` facade.
+* `Ctl.hash`/`blockParams` are populated by the shared `blockArgs` seam regardless of dialect; RawBars sees
+  `Nothing`/`[]` (no markers), MaxBars sees both — so the *same* marshaller yields the per-dialect surface
+  above with no per-dialect branching. (MaxBars producing `@param` markers required one dialect-local parser
+  change — the head ladder dropping its pipe rung so `as |…|` survives as structure; see
+  [the MaxBars page](/engine/maxbars/). No core or desugar change: `as` stays single-sourced in the surface
+  desugar's `extractBlockParams`.)
+
+### Gating
+
+* `test:compile` gains RawBars and MaxBars block-operation cases (interpreter ≡ compiled), mirroring the
+  FullBars `block:*` cases — RawBars covering `fn`/`inverse`/`data`, MaxBars also `hash` and block params
+  (`op:max-params`, plus `op:max-paren-pipe-params` pinning the parenthesise-to-pipe rule).
+* `check:glossary` extends to record the second boundary spelling: *operation* is the RawBars/MaxBars host
+  registrar's word, *helper* the FullBars one — both naming the same `Operation`. The gate keeps the
+  glossary and the facade in step (a registrar named against the wrong register fails the build).
+* Docs: the RawBars and MaxBars dialect pages document `renderWithOperations`; the FullBars ADR-020 line
+  that read "RawBars/MaxBars use the operation vocabulary, not `registerHelper`" is now precise — they use
+  `registerOperation`, the native-boundary twin.
+
+### Out of scope (this addendum)
+
+* A *new MaxBars-native block spelling* (a pipe/infix block form) — operators stay surface sugar over the
+  same `App`; `{{#op …}}` is the block form for every dialect.
+* `options.ids` / source locations — still throw by design (ADR-020), in every dialect.

+---
+title: "ADR-021: The MaxBars/RawBars variable model — `this` / `loop` / `root` / `parent` / `outer`"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-021 MaxBars variable model
+---
+
+*Status:* Proposed. *Date:* 2026-06-03. *Supersedes* [ADR-006](/adr/adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables/)
+Decision §1–2 (the bare loop-variable vocabulary) and §5 (its v1 outer-loop limit). *Extends*
+[ADR-013](/adr/adr-0013-labelled-loops/) (labelled loops → `outer`). Applies to *MaxBars and RawBars*
+only; FullBars is unchanged (Handlebars-faithful).
+
+## Context
+
+Three things converged to make the loop/context vocabulary worth redesigning:
+
+* *ADR-006 bare loop variables* gave MaxBars `{{index0}}`, `{{first}}`, `{{length}}`,
+  `{{key}}`, … as *bare* scoped names. They silently shadow data fields — the schema-less
+  *warn-always* lint (`loopVarShadowWarnings`) exists *only* to paper over that footgun — and they reach
+  just the *current* loop.
+* *ADR-013 labelled loops* added `label NAME` → the loop frame reified as an object
+  (`{{outer.index1}}`). It proved the mechanism: *a dotted head resolves against a binding only
+  when the name is scope-declared* (`{{c.deep.n}}` works because `c` is a block param;
+  `{{root.title}}` / `{{parent.title}}` render *empty* because `root`/`parent` are frame
+  helpers but **not** scope-declared, so they parse as data paths).
+* *Reaching the enclosing / root context* still relied on Handlebars' `@root` and `../` — the
+  `@` namespace the non-Handlebars dialects want to drop.
+
+The decision: replace the bare magic vocabulary with a small set of **reserved, namespaced, chainable**
+scoped names, and drop `@`/`../` in MaxBars and RawBars.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *The model is `this` / `loop` / `root` / `parent` / `outer`* — five reserved scoped names, available in
+  *MaxBars and RawBars*. FullBars is untouched: it keeps `@index`/`@root`/`../` (Handlebars
+  fidelity) and does *not* get these names. The set is *complete*: current context (`this`), current-loop
+  metadata (`loop`), a named enclosing loop's metadata (`outer`/labels), enclosing context (`parent`),
+  root context (`root`).
+
+. *Frames chain.* Every frame-shifting block (`each`, `with`) pushes a frame linked to its parent frame
+  and the root. The reserved names resolve against this chain, and **chain from day one**:
++
+| Name | Resolves to |
+| --- | --- |
+| `this` | the current context (raw data). Unchanged. |
+| `loop` | the *current loop's metadata object* (`each` only) — see the loop-object shape below. Chains over enclosing *loops*: `{{loop.parent.index0}}`, `{{loop.parent.parent.length}}`, `{{loop.root.length}}`. |
+| `outer` | a *named* enclosing loop's metadata object (any `label NAME`, ADR-013) — same shape as `loop`. |
+| `parent` | the *enclosing context* object. Chains over enclosing *contexts*: `{{parent.name}}`, `{{parent.parent.name}}`. |
+| `root` | the *root context* object (outermost context). |
++
+`loop`/`outer` are *loop metadata* (chain over enclosing **loops**); `parent`/`root` are *contexts*
+(chain over enclosing **contexts**). They are complementary, not redundant: `{{loop.parent.index0}}`
+is the enclosing loop's index; `{{parent.name}}` is a field on the enclosing context.
+
+. *Object shapes (normative).*
++
+* *loop-object* (`loop`, `outer`, any label): `{ index0, index1, rindex0, rindex1, first, last, length,
+  key, this, parent, root }`. The index/`first`/`last`/`length` arithmetic is ADR-006's (`rindex0 =
+  length − 1 − index0`, `first = index0 == 0`, …); `this` is the element; `parent` is the nearest
+  *enclosing loop*'s loop-object (or `null`); `root` is the *outermost loop*'s loop-object (or itself).
+  An **immutable per-iteration snapshot**.
+* *context-object* (`parent`, `root`): the context's *own* fields, plus the reserved links
+  `{ this, parent, root }` (reserved names win on collision). `parent` is the enclosing context-object
+  (or `null` at the top level); `root` is the root context-object.
+
+. *Reserved-name resolution (the mechanism).* The reserved names are **scope-declared** so a dotted head
+  resolves the binding, not a data path — the ADR-013 mechanism, generalized.
++
+* *MaxBars* — the surface desugar **seeds** the reserved names into `scope` (so `{{loop.first}}`
+  desugars to `(lookup (loop) "first")`, not a data lookup). This seeding is *MaxBars-only*: it rides the
+  same dialect hook that already distinguishes MaxBars from FullBars (which seeds nothing). This is "the
+  MaxBars-only scoped-name seeding."
+* *RawBars* — has no surface desugar, so the names are reached as ordinary *operations* the frame
+  installs, in RawBars' explicit style: `{{{loop}}}`, `{{{lookup loop "first"}}}`,
+  `{{{lookup (lookup loop "parent") "index0"}}}`.
+* The *engine* installs the same frame bindings for both dialects; FullBars' surface routes bare names to
+  data lookups, so it never reaches them — no gating of the bindings is required.
+
+. *`@` and `../` are removed in MaxBars* — at the parser seam (`parseMaxExpr`/`parseMaxHead`): an
+  `@`-prefixed name or a `../` run is a *located parse error* that points the author at `root` /
+  `parent` / `loop`. MaxBars-local; FullBars' default parser keeps both. RawBars never had `@`/`../`
+  (no surface), so there is nothing to remove there.
+
+. *The bare loop-variable vocabulary is removed* (supersedes ADR-006 §1–2). MaxBars passes
+  `noLoopVars`, so bare `{{first}}` / `{{index0}}` / `{{length}}` / `{{key}}`
+  are ordinary *data fields*; their values live as fields of `loop`. The frame no longer installs the
+  standalone `index0`/`first`/… operations, so RawBars' `{{{index}}}` / `{{{first}}}` /
+  `{{{parent-index}}}` are likewise replaced by `loop.*`.
+
+. *The block-partial body is the reserved name `yield`.* Handlebars' `{{> @partial-block}}`
+  yield is unwritable in the non-Handlebars dialects — `@` is reserved (§5), and a bare `partial-block`
+  lexes as the subtraction `partial - block` under MaxBars' infix arithmetic. `yield` is added as a
+  hyphen-free *synonym* of the `partial-block` scoped operation, installed under both names in the
+  partial block frame, so the one yield is spelled `{{yield}}` (MaxBars), `{{{yield}}}`
+  (RawBars), and `{{> @partial-block}}` (FullBars, unchanged). It is reserved like the other
+  roots: a same-named data field is shadowed (read it with an explicit `{{lookup this "yield"}}`),
+  and a `label yield` is flagged by the label-shadow lint. The yield is escape-safe (`VSafe`), so
+  MaxBars' `{{ }}` form does not re-escape it.
+
+. *The warn-always shadow lint is retired.* The footgun was "any field-like bare name silently shadows a
+  field"; with the metadata behind `loop.`, the reserved roots are `this`/`loop`/`root`/`parent`/`outer`
+  (and `yield` inside a block partial) — explicit, and rarely data fields except `yield`, whose escape
+  hatch is the explicit lookup above. ADR-006's `loopVarShadowWarnings` is deleted. The
+  ADR-013 `labelShadowWarnings` (a `label NAME` colliding with a reserved root — `this`/`loop`/`root`/
+  `parent`/`yield`) stays; a lighter optional lint may warn when a data field named one of the roots is
+  shadowed in a block body. NOTE: a reserved root shadows a field *everywhere*, even through an explicit
+  `{{this.NAME}}` (the path reduces to the segment `NAME`), so the explicit `lookup` is the only
+  field escape.
+
+. *Compiler parity.* The frame chain + reserved-name objects are emitted by the compiler exactly as the
+  interpreter builds them — the ADR-013 `rt.each`/`childFrame` `binds` chain extends to carry `loop` /
+  `parent` / `root` and the parent links — gated by `test:compile` (interpreter ≡ compiled).
+
+## Examples
+
+```handlebars
+{{!-- MaxBars --}}
+{{#each rows as |row| label outer}}
+  {{#each row.cells}}
+    {{loop.index1}}/{{loop.length}}       {{!-- this (inner) loop --}}
+    {{outer.index0}} of {{outer.length}}  {{!-- the named enclosing loop --}}
+    {{loop.parent.first}}                 {{!-- the enclosing loop, unnamed --}}
+    {{parent.heading}}                    {{!-- the enclosing context (a row) --}}
+    {{parent.parent.title}}               {{!-- two contexts up --}}
+    {{root.report.id}}                    {{!-- the root context --}}
+  {{/each}}
+{{/each}}
+```
+
+## Alternatives considered (team debate)
+
+* *Flat names, no chaining* (`loop`/`outer`/`parent`/`root` but no `parent.parent`/`loop.parent`) —
+  rejected: developers expect chaining from day one.
+* *Hierarchy only* (`this`/`loop`/`outer`, fold `root`/`parent` under `loop`) — rejected: `root`/`parent`
+  are not conceptually under `loop`, and the folding breaks in `{{#with}}` bodies (no `loop`).
+* *Keep `@`/`../` alongside the new names* — rejected: the goal is to *drop* `@` in the
+  non-Handlebars dialects; coexistence defeats it.
+* *MaxBars-only (exclude RawBars)* — rejected by requirement: the model is for both non-Handlebars
+  dialects. The asymmetry is only in *reach* (MaxBars: dotted paths via seeding; RawBars: explicit
+  operations), not in the underlying bindings.
+* *Keep the bare vocabulary for backward compatibility* — rejected: repo policy is no compat shims; the
+  bare vars become data fields and templates migrate (below).
+
+## Migration
+
+* *MaxBars:* bare `{{index0}}`/`{{first}}`/… → `{{loop.index0}}`/`{{loop.first}}`;
+  `{{@root.x}}` → `{{root.x}}`; `{{../x}}` → `{{parent.x}}`. Touches the
+  `mx:loopvars-*` conformance cases, the `loopVars`/`loopObject` tutorial examples, the MaxBars
+  interpreter `loopvars-*` tests, and `maxbars.adoc`.
+* *RawBars / core corpus:* `{{{index}}}` / `{{{key}}}` / `first` / `last` /
+  `{{{parent-index}}}` (the `each-array`, `each-first-last`, `each-array-key-null`,
+  `each-object-*`, `each-parent-index` cases) → the `loop.*` forms.
+* *Lint:* delete `MaxBars.Lint.loopVarShadowWarnings` + its tests; keep `labelShadowWarnings`.
+* *Docs:* this ADR; supersession note on ADR-006 §1–2 + its §5 v1 outer-loop limit; extended-by note on
+  ADR-013; `nav.adoc` registration; `maxbars.adoc` and the RawBars page.
+* *Build:* regenerate the Lab bundle; `test:compile` and full `npm test` green.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *Pro:* one coherent, chainable, namespaced model; the shadow footgun is essentially gone (metadata is
+  behind `loop.`); `@`/`../` are dropped from the non-Handlebars dialects as intended; reuses the
+  ADR-013 frame mechanism.
+* *Con:* a *breaking change* to every MaxBars/RawBars template using bare loop vars or `@`/`../`
+  (no compat shim); a non-trivial migration; the reserved roots now shadow same-named fields inside a
+  block body — `yield` most notably, a common data field (bond/crop yield), whose only escape is the
+  explicit `{{lookup this "yield"}}`; building the frame *chain* (`parent`/`root` links,
+  multi-level) is more engine/compiler work than ADR-013's single frame.
+
+## Open questions
+
+* Exact error text for `@` / `../` in MaxBars (point at `root`/`parent`/`loop`).
+* `parent` at the *top level* (no enclosing context): propose `null`; `root` is always available.
+* Whether to expose `loop.depth` (nesting depth) — *defer* to a follow-up.

+---
+title: "ADR-023: One recovering parser; fail-fast `parse` is its projection"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-023 Recovering parser
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted; *implemented*. *Date:* 2026-06-03. Builds on
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/) (one structural parser) and unblocks the
+editor diagnostics deferred by [ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/).
+
+## Context
+
+ADR-017 shipped engine-backed *highlighting*, but left editor *diagnostics* (the red squiggle for a
+malformed tag) deferred behind a "recovering parser" it called a prerequisite. The naïve reading is that
+an IDE needs a second, error-tolerant parser alongside the engine's total, fail-fast `parse`. That is the
+exact *drift trap* this project fights everywhere else (ADR-001/014): two definitions of the grammar that
+must be kept in lock-step, and an IDE that can disagree with the compiler about what is even valid.
+
+The core also distinguishes a *fail-fast* contract the compiler genuinely needs — you cannot codegen a
+syntactically invalid template, so `parse` must be total and reject bad input — from the *implementation*
+that delivers it. The question is whether fail-fast must be dropped, kept as a second engine, or
+re-expressed.
+
+A template language makes recovery unusually tractable: the lexer (`tokenizeTemplate`) already delimits
+tags into a flat `RawTok` stream, so *tag boundaries are natural synchronization points*. An error in one
+tag's interior need not blank the rest of the document.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *There is ONE parser, and it recovers.* `parseSeq` (the tree builder over the `RawTok` stream) no
+  longer returns `Either`: it always produces a best-effort tree plus *every* error in source order. The
+  recovery is local and bounded, anchored at tag boundaries:
++
+--
+* a tag with a bad interior drops a `NodeError Span String` marker and the scan continues;
+* a *block* opener with a salvageable head (a leading identifier — `{{#if a == 1}}` yields name
+  `if` even though the args won't parse) still nests, so its body and close parse and only the bad args
+  are flagged — no cascade of spurious errors;
+* a missing or mismatched `{{/x}}` builds the block anyway and records the mismatch; a stray
+  top-level close is reported and recovered past.
+--
+
+. *Fail-fast is kept, but re-expressed as a PROJECTION over the recovering parser — not dropped, not a
+  second engine.* `parse` / `parseWith` run `parseRecovering` and return `Right tree` iff no error was
+  recovered, else `Left` the first error in source order — byte-for-byte the result the total parser
+  always gave. The compiler/render path keeps its total, fail-fast contract; it simply gets the verdict
+  from the one parser. Editor tooling calls `parseRecovering` directly. *One grammar, two views — drift
+  is impossible by construction*, which is ADR-001's principle, now fulfilled more truly (a fail-fast-only
+  parser is exactly what would have forced a second one).
++
+The cost on a *valid* template is zero: recovery only triggers on an error, and on the error path the
+compiler rejects the file anyway, so the extra work is never wasted on output.
+
+. *`NodeError` is a first-class AST node.* It carries the offending span and a message and appears *only*
+  in a `parseRecovering` tree. Because `parse` projects any recovered error to `Left`, the render /
+  compile / lower / desugar paths never receive one; each consumer's `NodeError` arm is a total,
+  unreachable-in-practice neutral (the foldTemplate algebra gained a `nodeError` case). Tooling folds
+  (diagnostics, pretty-print) handle it meaningfully. We chose an in-tree node over a sidecar error list
+  so a later phase (hover, selection ranges) can attach to the error's position in the tree.
+
+. *Diagnostics are derived, not heuristic.* `flatbars-js` exposes `diagnostics(template, dialect)` —
+  `parseRecovering` with that dialect's `ParseOptions`, each error located via `parseErrorAt`. The same
+  dialect seam that makes `==` an operator in MaxBars makes `{{#if a == 1}}` an error in every
+  other surface — so the editor flags exactly what the dialect rejects. `flatbars-lsp` publishes these as
+  `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` on open and every edit.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* Editor diagnostics work, four dialects, with no second parser and no change to the fail-fast contract.
+  ADR-017's "recovering parser (prerequisite)" open question is resolved by this record.
+* `parse`/`parseWith` stay byte-compatible — every spago suite passes and `test:compile` is 296/296
+  (compiled ≡ interpreter). The recovering behaviour has its own tests (`parseRecovering`).
+* `NodeError` widens the `Node` sum, so every match on it is total by construction; a new consumer of the
+  skeleton AST must add a `nodeError` arm (a one-line neutral unless it is tooling).
+* *Deferred, not blocked:* richer recovery for an unsalvageable block head (currently a `NodeError` plus a
+  flat tail), and hover/completion built on the in-tree error nodes. Diagnostic *ranges* currently cover
+  the offending tag (start → its `}}`); finer spans can come from `NodeError`'s span when needed.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-04): recovery over pre-lexed interiors
+
+`headedRecovering`/`salvageName` now consume each tag's *pre-lexed* interior,
+carried on the `RawTok` itself and populated by `tokenizeTemplate`
+([ADR-004](/adr/adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams/) amendment), instead of
+re-lexing it. Per-tag recovery is preserved precisely because that interior is the
+*deferred* `Either ParseError (Array PosToken)`: a malformed interior is a `Left`
+that rides inside its own tag and is handled exactly where `tokenizeInterior` used
+to fail, so one bad tag never breaks the structural scan or the rest of the
+document. Behaviour is unchanged (`parseRecovering` tests + `test:compile` 300/300).
