+---
+title: "ADR-024: Block-scoped `let` and the dict literal — MaxBars surface, FullBars unchanged"
+sidebar:
+  label: "ADR-024 `let` & dict literal"
+---
+
+*Status:* Proposed (revised 2026-06-04 after team review — see *Resolved during review* below; the list
+literal was split out to [ADR-025](/adr/adr-0025-list-literal/)).
+*Date:* 2026-06-04. Applies to *MaxBars and RawBars* only; *FullBars is unchanged*
+(Handlebars-faithful — see [ADR-009](/adr/adr-0009-fullbars/) and the conformance line at
+[ADR-005](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/)). Sits alongside
+[ADR-021](/adr/adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model/) (the MaxBars/RawBars variable model) as the
+expression-sugar half of the same dialect carve-out.
+
+This ADR covers the two constructs that need *no shared-prelude change*: block-scoped `{{#let}}` and the
+dict literal (which reuses the existing `dict` helper). The *list literal* needs a new `list` constructor
+in the shared prelude, a different blast radius, so it is its own decision —
+[ADR-025](/adr/adr-0025-list-literal/). The two ADRs share this Context and the lexing/dialect model.
+
+## Context
+
+Template authors recurringly need *template-local constants* — a forge-name → URL lookup table, a
+status → label enum, an alias for a deep path used many times — that are intrinsic to the template,
+identical on every render, and have no business in the host data. Today the only spelling is to pass
+them in through the render context on every call, which is friction for what is effectively a `const`
+inside the template.
+
+Three things make this a design problem, not a one-helper fix:
+
+* *No variables.* The [concepts](/concepts/) thesis is strict — *"the only compound expression is
+  an application of a name."* Any new construct must either *be* an application or *desugar* to one. A
+  literal expression class (`Lit`-typed nodes for `{…}`/`[…]`) cannot live in the kernel AST.
+* *No host-format dependency in core.* [ADR-003](/adr/adr-0003-strict-layering/) keeps `JSON` ⇆ `Value`
+  out of the core (*"JSON-ness is a host concern"*). YAML / JSON-style literal collections in *tag*
+  bodies would re-import the same dependency under a different name.
+* *Dialect carve-out is the established lever.* [ADR-005](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/) gives MaxBars
+  the room for surface additions FullBars cannot have, by reuse-by-dependency: MaxBars depends on
+  `fullbars`, swaps the interior expression grammar, and FullBars's Handlebars conformance
+  (`49/50` byte-identical, gated by `check:hbs-conformance`) is untouched. [ADR-006](/adr/adr-0006-maxbars-loop-variables/)
+  /[ADR-021](/adr/adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model/) use this for the variable model; this ADR uses it
+  for `let` and the dict literal.
+
+The space of candidates was enumerated in the design debate. The salient negative results — captured
+here so future revivals don't relitigate, and shared with [ADR-025](/adr/adr-0025-list-literal/) —
+were:
+
+* *JSON-style literals* (`{"b":1,"c":2}`, `[1,2,3]`) — imported `:` and `,` as new tag-body tokens with
+  no FlatBars precedent, broke whitespace-separated args, doubled the editor-tooling contract
+  ([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) token-vocabulary).
+* *Unified `[…]` for both dicts and lists*, content-disambiguated (all-`name=value` ⇒ dict, otherwise
+  list). Killed by the empty-collection case: `[]` cannot mean both, leaving no literal spelling for
+  the empty dict — and discarded the universal `{} / []` shape convention every comparable language
+  (including Lua's tables) honours. This is *why* the dict literal is `{…}` (here) and the list literal
+  is `[…]` (ADR-025), as two distinct shapes.
+* *Dict sugar at the helper level only* (e.g. renaming `dict` → `obj`). One character saved per call,
+  capped by name quality; not worth a prelude churn on a well-established helper.
+* *Dropping `{{#with}}` in favour of `{{#let}}`*. `with` does two jobs (re-root context + optional alias);
+  `let` does one (alias only). The aliases are equivalent only when the body never uses bare names. `with`
+  also lives in the shared prelude, so removing it requires either splitting the prelude or adding a
+  surface-level rejection — both heavier than the saving. See *Relationship to `{{#with}}`* below.
+
+## Decision
+
+Two constructs ship here, scoped to *MaxBars only*, *surface-stage* desugared, with *no shared-prelude
+change*: block-scoped `{{#let}}` and the dict literal. (The list literal and its required `list` helper
+are [ADR-025](/adr/adr-0025-list-literal/).)
+
+### 1. Block-scoped `{{#let}}` — alias only, never re-root
+
+`{{#let}}` installs *nullary operations* at the block's lexical scope; they vanish at `{{/let}}`. It is
+the operation model applied to template-local *constants* — no new concept, just a new way to write one.
+
+```handlebars
+{{#let n=expr [n=expr …]}}
+  … body where each n is a nullary operation that returns expr …
+{{/let}}
+```
+
+Semantics:
+
+* *Bindings* evaluate left-to-right, each in the scope *extended by the bindings to its left*: in
+  `{{#let a=1 b=(add a 1)}}`, `b` sees `a`. A binding sees neither itself nor any binding to its
+  right, so there is no self-reference and no fixpoint — this is a *sequential* `let`, not a `letrec`,
+  and it remains a single total walk (no second pass). The sequential form removes the nesting tax the
+  earlier parallel design imposed (which forced `{{#let a=1}}{{#let b=(add a 1)}} … {{/let}}{{/let}}`
+  for what is the common case).
+* *Scope* is block-scoped lexically: names exist between `{{#let}}` and `{{/let}}`. Inner blocks inherit;
+  partials called inside inherit (the standing scope-chain rule).
+* *Shadowing.* A `let` name that collides with an in-scope helper shadows it inside the body, then the
+  original is unshadowed at `{{/let}}`. A collision with a `{{#each xs as |x|}}` block param of the same
+  name in the *same* scope is a parse error.
+* *Does not re-root context.* `{{#let u=user}}{{name}}{{/let}}` resolves `name` against the *root*, not
+  against `user`. To re-root, use `{{#with}}` (which stays — see below).
+
+### 2. Dict literal `{name=expr name=expr …}` — MaxBars expression sugar
+
+A brace-delimited list of hash-arg pairs in expression position is sugar for `(dict …)`. The interior
+syntax is FlatBars-native — *bare* keys, `=` separator, *whitespace*-separated pairs — no JSON
+conventions are imported.
+
+```handlebars
+{{#let forges={codeberg="…" github="…" gitlab="…"}}}
+  …
+{{/let}}
+```
+
+Desugars at the MaxBars parser stage to `(dict codeberg="…" github="…" gitlab="…")`. The `dict`
+helper already lives in the shared prelude ([prelude](/engine/prelude/)); *no kernel or prelude change* — this is
+the property that lets the dict literal ship ahead of the list literal.
+
+Empty: `{}` is the empty dict — clean, unambiguous, lowers to `(dict)`.
+
+### 3. Lexing: desugar at the MaxBars expression stage, structure lexer untouched
+
+The dict literal is resolved entirely in the MaxBars interior grammar (`MaxBars.Expr`, plugged in
+through the `ParseOptions.parseExpr` seam). The *structure* lexer (`tokenizeTemplate`) never gains `{` or
+`}` as structural tokens, and tag-boundary detection is unchanged. This is what keeps the three
+delimiter widths (`{{ }}` / `{{{ }}}` / `{{{{ }}}}`) intact: width detection runs *first* and fixes the
+tag span; only then does the interior tokenizer see the literal braces. (ADR-025 extends the same
+principle to `[`/`]`; the rule is identical.)
+
+The one consequence for the surface: inside an already-delimited tag, the interior tokenizer matches `{`
+against its closing `}` by nesting depth, so a literal collection's own closing brace is consumed before
+the tag close. `{{#let x={a=1}}}` therefore reads as `#let x=` · `{a=1}` · `}}` (dict-close, then
+tag-close), and the nested `{{#let x={a={b=1}}}}}` as `{a={b=1}}` · `}}` — no ambiguity, because
+the tag span was settled by width detection before the interior is scanned. *Authors never insert a
+disambiguating space.* This is the load-bearing lexing claim, so it is gated by a dedicated tokenizer
+corpus (see *Gates*).
+
+### 4. Dialect scope
+
+| Surface | `{{#let}}` | `{…}` dict literal | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| *RawBars* | ✓ (explicit form: `{{#let (bind a x)}}…{{/let}}`) | ✗ (no sugar at all by design) | Writes the kernel form directly. |
+| *FullBars* | *✗* | *✗* | Handlebars-faithful. Authors use `{{#with x as \|n\|}}` for aliasing and `(dict …)` for collections. |
+| *MaxBars* | ✓ (with `n=expr` surface sugar) | ✓ (`{name=expr …}`) | The flagship; the list literal is added by ADR-025. |
+
+This is the same asymmetry already enforced for MaxBars operators (`>=` is MaxBars-only sugar that
+lowers to `(gte …)`; `gte` is a shared-prelude helper).
+
+### 5. Kernel footprint
+
+One addition, small and decided here (not deferred):
+
+* *A dedicated `Let [(name, expr)] body` AST node* (resolved during review — see below). It pushes a
+  helpers-only frame onto the env stack at `{{#let}}` and pops it at `{{/let}}`. The env stack already
+  exists — `pushFrame` (`Kernel.Env`) is what block params and `{{#with}}` use — but note `pushFrame`
+  bundles *helpers + context*; `let` pushes the binding helpers while *passing the current context
+  through unchanged* (that is the "never re-root" guarantee of §1, expressed mechanically). No new
+  `Value` shape.
+
+The dict literal adds *nothing* to the kernel: `{…}` desugars before the AST is built, so the kernel sees
+an ordinary `Application` node — `(dict …)` — and `dict` is already in the prelude. (The list literal of
+ADR-025 is the one construct that *does* touch the shared prelude.)
+
+### 6. Relationship to `{{#with}}`
+
+`{{#with}}` stays in *every* dialect. `let` and `with` are complements, not competitors:
+
+| Operation | Alias | Re-root `this` / bare names |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `{{#let n=x}}` | ✓ | ✗ |
+| `{{#with x}}` | ✗ | ✓ |
+| `{{#with x as \|n\|}}` | ✓ | ✓ |
+
+The identity worth recording: `{{#with x as |n|}}` ≡ `{{#with x}}{{#let n=x}} … {{/let}}{{/with}}`.
+`let` desugars *part* of `with`, not the whole thing.
+
+## Consequences
+
+### Gates
+
+* *Tokenizer corpus (precondition — must land before implementation).* A golden corpus in the
+  `check:highlight` style that pins the lexing claim of §3 over the adjacent-brace cases: `{{#let x={a=1}}}`,
+  `{{#let x={}}}`, and the nested `{{#let x={a={b=1}}}}}` (five trailing braces). Each must
+  tokenize with the tag span fixed by width detection *before* the interior is scanned. No corpus, no
+  merge — this is the construct's highest-risk surface. (ADR-025 adds the bracket cases.)
+* *`check:hbs-conformance`* — already in `npm test`. Catches any FullBars regression from the `49/50`
+  byte-identical line. If `let`/`{…}` ever bleed into the FullBars surface parser, the next run of this
+  gate flags it. (Unlike ADR-025, this ADR adds no prelude helper, so there is no catalog/conformance
+  churn here.)
+* *`check:isolation`* — extended with one MaxBars-only-surface assertion per construct, source-pinned in
+  the style of `check:a11y`: a FullBars template containing `{{#let …}}` or `{name=expr}` in
+  expression position must produce a surface diagnostic, not silent acceptance.
+* *Linter round-trip* (`Linter.Lower`) — pins that `{{#let a=1}}` lowers to
+  `{{#let (bind a 1)}}` and `{b=1 c=2}` lowers to `(dict b=1 c=2)`. One canonical RawBars
+  form per construct — no AST drift, no two-way sugar.
+
+### Linter
+
+* New hint *`prefer-let-over-with-as`* (MaxBars only): suggest `{{#let n=x}}…{{/let}}` when the
+  body of a `{{#with x as |n|}}…{{/with}}` never uses bare names — the exact case where the
+  forms are equivalent. *Soundness boundary:* the scope-chain rule (§1) means a partial invoked in the
+  body inherits the re-rooted context and may consume bare names *invisibly* — and a host-supplied
+  partial cannot be analysed at all. So the hint fires *only when the body invokes no partial*
+  (`{{> …}}`, `{{#> …}}`, `{{yield}}`); a body that calls a partial is left alone
+  rather than risk a rewrite that changes rendering. The genuine `with` use-cases (re-root with no
+  alias, or re-root + alias with a bare-name body) are untouched.
+
+### Editor tooling (ADR-017 contract)
+
+The token vocabulary gains two new tag-body tokens, scoped to the MaxBars grammar variant: `{` and `}`
+(the dict literal's delimiters). The LSP semantic-token emitter, the TextMate fallback grammar, and the
+VS Code / JetBrains extension grammars each receive a one-time update; the *contract source*
+([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) token-vocabulary.json) is the single edit point. (ADR-025
+adds the `[`/`]` tokens, including the `[` dual-context disambiguation.)
+
+### Documentation
+
+* `maxbars.adoc` gains a `Let` section and a `Dict literal` section.
+* `rawbars.adoc` adds one paragraph: the explicit `(bind …)` form is the desugared canonical;
+  surface sugar lives in MaxBars.
+* `fullbars.adoc` is *not* modified. The existing convention rule in `tutorials/src/fullbars.mjs`
+  (*"No MaxBars operators"*) gains a parallel line: *"No MaxBars block-scoped bindings, no MaxBars dict
+  literals."*
+
+### Non-goals (deliberately deferred)
+
+* *File-level front matter* (template-scoped data via a `---` YAML header). A host-layer concern (see
+  the front-matter debate notes); `let` is the engine-side, lexically-scoped answer. If a front-matter
+  adapter ships later it should *desugar at the host* into a top-level `let` — keeping one canonical
+  binding mechanism.
+* *Dropping `{{#with}}`* in MaxBars/RawBars. Considered and rejected — the carve-out cost exceeds the
+  gain, and the philosophical objection (`with` re-roots ⇒ "hidden variable") already coexists with
+  `{{#each}}`'s identical re-rooting. The linter hint covers the cases where `let` would actually
+  read more clearly.
+
+## Resolved during review
+
+The team review of 2026-06-04 closed the questions that were previously left open or mis-scoped:
+
+* *The list literal was split out to [ADR-025](/adr/adr-0025-list-literal/).* It alone needs a new
+  `list` constructor in the *shared* prelude (the prelude has no list constructor today), so it carries a
+  catalog + conformance blast radius that `let` and the dict literal do not. Keeping them in one ADR
+  conflated "pure MaxBars surface" with "shared-prelude change"; the split makes each decision honest and
+  lets `let` + dict ship first.
+* *Kernel primitive: a dedicated `Let [(name, expr)] body` AST node*, not a sugar that lowers to a chain
+  of single-binding scope-frame ops. The runtime behaviour is identical, but the `Linter.Lower`
+  round-trip is a *stated gate* (see *Consequences*), and it cannot be specified without fixing the
+  canonical form: a dedicated node round-trips one-to-one, whereas the sugar-chain lowers
+  `{{#let a=1 b=2}}` to *nested* `(bind)` blocks — two-way drift, the exact failure the gate
+  exists to prevent. So the node is the canonical form.
+* *Binding semantics are sequential* (§1), not parallel-in-the-enclosing-scope. The dedicated node makes
+  forward reference (`b` sees `a`) free, and it matches every author's mental model of `let` while
+  staying a single total walk.

+---
+title: "ADR-025: The list literal `[…]` and the `list` prelude helper — MaxBars surface + shared prelude"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-025 list literal
+---
+
+*Status:* Proposed. *Date:* 2026-06-04. The list-literal half of the collection-literal design,
+*split from* [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/) during the 2026-06-04 team review.
+Applies to *MaxBars* (surface sugar) and the *shared prelude* (a new constructor). FullBars's surface is
+*unchanged*; the prelude addition is value-only and Handlebars-compatible (gated by
+`check:hbs-conformance`).
+
+This is a separate ADR from [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/) for one reason: the
+list literal is *not* pure MaxBars surface. Its desugar target does not exist, so it ships a new helper
+into the *shared* prelude — a different blast radius (catalog regen, conformance re-run, presence in
+every dialect) than `let` and the dict literal, both of which reuse what is already there. Conflating the
+two understated this cost; separating them keeps each decision honest and lets ADR-024 ship first.
+
+## Context
+
+Shared with the *Context* of [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/) — the
+template-local-constants motivation, the *no variables* / *no host-format-in-core* constraints, the
+dialect carve-out lever, and the enumerated negative results (JSON-style literals; the unified-`[…]`
+dead-end that forces distinct `{…}`/`[…]` shapes). Not repeated here.
+
+One fact specific to lists drives this ADR:
+
+* *There is no list constructor today.* The shared prelude ([prelude](/engine/prelude/)) has list-_consuming_
+  helpers — `join`, `count`, `size`, `at`, `take`, `reverse`, `unique`, `pluck` — but nothing that
+  *builds* a list. The only way to obtain one is `split` (from a string). So a template author cannot
+  write a literal sequence at all. This is a genuine capability gap, not a convenience over an existing
+  helper (contrast `dict`, which `(dict …)` has always provided). The list literal closes it, and that
+  is why it is worth a prelude addition.
+
+## Decision
+
+Two things ship together, because the surface sugar is inert without its target:
+
+### 1. A new `list` prelude helper
+
+A variadic value helper `(list e …)` that returns the array of its evaluated arguments. It lives
+in the *shared* prelude next to `dict`, so it is available in every dialect's expression position
+(RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars/MinBars), exactly as `dict` is. It adds no new `Value` shape (arrays already
+exist) and no kernel change — it is an ordinary value-producing operation, the list analogue of `dict`.
+
+This is the one piece that distinguishes this ADR from [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/):
+a *shared-prelude* change, with the catalog + conformance consequences in *Gates* below.
+
+### 2. List literal `[expr expr …]` — MaxBars expression sugar
+
+A bracket-delimited list of positional expressions in expression position is sugar for `(list …)`.
+
+```handlebars
+{{#let langs=["PureScript" "TypeScript" "Rust"]}}
+  {{#each langs}} — {{this}}{{/each}}
+{{/let}}
+```
+
+Desugars at the MaxBars parser stage to `(list "PureScript" "TypeScript" "Rust")`. Empty: `[]` is
+the empty list, lowers to `(list)`. The sugar is MaxBars-only; RawBars writes `(list …)` directly;
+FullBars has neither the sugar nor (by convention) uses it, though the `list` helper is *present* in its
+prelude.
+
+### 3. Lexing and the `[` / `.[` disambiguation
+
+Lexing follows the *Lexing* section of [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/)
+verbatim, extended from `{`/`}` to `[`/`]`: desugar happens in the MaxBars interior grammar
+(`MaxBars.Expr` via the `ParseOptions.parseExpr` seam); the *structure* lexer never gains `[`/`]` as
+structural tokens; width detection fixes the tag span before the interior is scanned, so a literal's own
+`]` is consumed by nesting depth before the tag close. `{{#let xs=[1 2}}}]`… reads cleanly, and no
+disambiguating space is ever required.
+
+The one list-specific hazard is the existing path-index form `{{a.[i}}]`. The disambiguation is
+*not* by look-behind — that is unsound under the recovering parser
+([ADR-023](/adr/adr-0023-recovering-parser/)), where the preceding token may be a `NodeError`. Instead,
+in the MaxBars interior grammar *`.[` is the only path-index form*; a `[` in any other position is
+unconditionally a list-open. The two productions never compete for the same token, so error recovery on a
+malformed tag cannot flip one into the other. (This is the one claim flagged for a confirming tokenizer
+spike — see *Open question*.)
+
+### 4. Dialect scope
+
+| Surface | `[…]` list literal | `(list …)` helper |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| *RawBars* | ✗ (no sugar by design) | ✓ (write it directly) |
+| *FullBars* | ✗ (Handlebars-faithful surface) | ✓ (present in the shared prelude; convention says don't use it) |
+| *MaxBars* | ✓ (`[expr …]`) | ✓ |
+
+The helper is shared (a value-policy-free constructor, like `dict`); only the *sugar* is MaxBars-scoped —
+the same asymmetry as `>=` → `(gte …)`.
+
+## Consequences
+
+### Gates
+
+* *`check:catalog`* — the new `list` helper makes the generated helper catalog stale; run
+  `npm run gen:catalog` and the gate keeps the docs partial in step with `FullBars.preludeSchema`. *This
+  gate is the headline difference from [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/)*, which
+  adds no helper.
+* *`check:hbs-conformance`* — already in `npm test`. Re-run after adding `list` to confirm the `49/50`
+  byte-identical FullBars line is unmoved (a value-producing helper should be inert to it, but the gate
+  proves it). Also catches any `[…]` bleed into the FullBars surface parser.
+* *Tokenizer corpus (precondition — must land before implementation).* Extends the ADR-024 corpus with
+  the bracket cases: `{{#let xs=[}}]`, `{{#let xs=[1 2 3}}]`, the mixed
+  `{{#let x={a=[1 2}}}}]` (four trailing braces), and the path-index control `{{a.[0}}]` to
+  pin that `.[` is *not* read as a list-open. No corpus, no merge.
+* *`check:isolation`* — one MaxBars-only-surface assertion: a FullBars template with `[expr …]` in
+  expression position produces a surface diagnostic, not silent acceptance. (Note the `list` *helper* is
+  legal everywhere; only the bracket *sugar* is gated.)
+* *Linter round-trip* (`Linter.Lower`) — pins that `[1 2 3]` lowers to `(list 1 2 3)`. One
+  canonical RawBars form, no two-way sugar.
+
+### Editor tooling (ADR-017 contract)
+
+The token vocabulary gains two new tag-body tokens, scoped to the MaxBars grammar variant: `[` and `]`.
+The `[` token has two lexical contexts within tags — path-index in `.[` (existing) and list-literal
+elsewhere (new); §3 fixes the disambiguation to be position-based, not look-behind-based, so it is robust
+under the recovering parser. The LSP semantic-token emitter, the TextMate fallback grammar, and the VS
+Code / JetBrains grammars each receive a one-time update; the contract source
+([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) token-vocabulary.json) is the single edit point.
+
+### Documentation
+
+* `maxbars.adoc` gains a `List literal` subsection (alongside the `Dict literal` section added by
+  [ADR-024](/adr/adr-0024-let-and-dict-literal/)).
+* `prelude.adoc` / the generated helper catalog gain the `list` entry (via `gen:catalog`).
+* `rawbars.adoc` notes `(list …)` as the canonical form behind the MaxBars `[…]` sugar.
+* `fullbars.adoc` convention line (`tutorials/src/fullbars.mjs`) extends to *"no MaxBars list literals"*
+  (the `list` helper itself stays available, like any prelude value helper).
+
+### Non-goals (deliberately deferred)
+
+* *Bracket literals outside `{{#let}}`*. A natural future extension is `{{#each [1 2 3}}…{{/each}}]`
+  and `(map [1 2 3 …)]` — admissible because, once this ADR lands, `(list …)` is a
+  first-class expression. Out of scope here; opens cleanly if pressure shows up.
+* *A `map`/`filter`/`fold` family over lists.* The list literal makes such helpers *useful*, but each is
+  its own prelude decision; this ADR ships only the constructor.
+
+## Open question
+
+The §3 claim that *`.[` is the only path-index form and every other `[` is a list-open* is the one piece
+not yet proven against the recovering parser. Before the four editor grammars
+([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/)) are touched, a small tokenizer spike should confirm that
+malformed-tag recovery never reclassifies a path-index `[` as a list-open (and vice versa). The
+implementation is otherwise straightforward; this is the only residual risk, and it is contained to the
+MaxBars interior tokenizer.

+---
+title: ADR-026 — Editor capability matrix
+---
+
+## Context
+
+ADR-017 set the two-layer model — TextMate grammar (the floor) plus
+`flatbars-lsp` semantic tokens (the ceiling) — and shipped the minimum LSP
+surface needed to demonstrate it: `semanticTokens/full`, `publishDiagnostics`,
+`textDocument/hover`, `textDocument/completion`, and a `codeAction`
+canonicalisation quick-fix.
+
+The June 2026 editor-plugin review surfaced a follow-up question: what is the
+*complete* set of LSP capabilities the editors advertise, and which IDE-native
+features (Find Usages, Rename, Reformat, Structure View, Folding, Breadcrumbs,
+Go to Definition) is the plugin expected to provide? The platform LSP client in
+JetBrains does not auto-wire most of those; the server must both advertise the
+capability and the editor side must opt in.
+
+This ADR fixes the matrix.
+
+## Decision
+
+The editors ship the following LSP capabilities, gated on what the engine can
+honestly compute from a *single* template document (the FlatBars engine does
+not maintain a cross-template scope graph, by design — partials are looked up
+by name in a host-supplied registry, see ADR-003):
+
+|  |  |  |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Capability | Status | Source |
+| `semanticTokens/full` | Ship | ADR-017 — engine `tokenize` + vocab-driven legend. The legend is augmented with one *custom* semantic-token type — `embeddedDelimiter` — declared in `editors/token-vocabulary.json` under `customSemanticTypes` and codegenned into the VS Code manifest's `contributes.semanticTokenTypes` + `semanticTokenScopes` so the LSP-emitted brace pair under a switched delimiter (`{{=<% %>=}}` → subsequent `<% … %>`) themes identically to the grammar's `punctuation.section.embedded.flatbars` floor without per-theme work. `check:vocab` enforces parity between the kind's `lsp.type` and the custom-type declaration. |
+| `publishDiagnostics` | Ship | ADR-023 — recovering parser → `NodeError` ranges. The LSP layers a second diagnostic source on top — `dialectDiagnostics` in `editors/lsp/src/tokens.mjs` — a small finder array that flags surface constructs the *engine* accepts but the *dialect* does not (e.g. set-delim outside MinBars, MaxBars `??` in any other dialect, subexpressions / block params / partial-hash-args / helper invocations in MinBars). Each finder produces an actionable, dialect-named message instead of leaving the user with an opaque parse failure. The rule inventory is pinned by `check:dialect-diagnostics` so refactoring the finders array cannot silently drop a rule. |
+| `textDocument/hover` | Ship | `operations.json` derived from `FullBars.preludeSchema`. |
+| `textDocument/completion` | Ship | Same source as hover, gated on `inTagContext`. |
+| `textDocument/codeAction` | Ship | Canonicalisation rewrites (`index` → `index0`, `partial-block` → `yield`). |
+| `textDocument/foldingRange` | Ship (new) | Every block-open / block-close pair is a fold region; raw-block regions fold. Single-document, structurally trivial from the engine tokens. |
+| `textDocument/documentSymbol` | Ship (new) | The block nesting hierarchy projected as a symbol tree — feeds IntelliJ Structure View and VS Code outline. |
+| `textDocument/formatting` | Ship (new) | Canonical-spacing inside `{{ … }}` (one space after the opener, one before the closer, normalised internal whitespace). Single-document, deterministic. |
+| Bold tag emphasis ("isle in the ocean") | Ship (new) | The whole tag — braces + interior — renders bold. VS Code: vocab-driven `configurationDefaults` (overridable), bold on every theme + injected hosts. JetBrains: bold on the LSP ceiling only (`lspCustomization` semantic-token attributes); the TextMate floor stays theme-controlled (no plugin hook to force a scope's font weight) — the same Ultimate-vs-Community asymmetry as LSP. |
+| `textDocument/definition` | Do not ship | Would require a cross-template scope graph (which partial defines which identifier, where a `{{> partial}}` resolves). FlatBars uses a runtime partial registry the engine never indexes; building an editor-time index duplicates the host's data and would drift. Out of scope for the editor. |
+| `textDocument/references` | Do not ship | Same reason as definition: no global identifier graph. |
+| `textDocument/rename` | Do not ship | Same reason; refactoring partial names would have to coordinate with the host application's partial registry. |
+| `textDocument/documentHighlight` | Do not ship | Without a scope graph, single-buffer "highlight uses of `name`" devolves to string search — strictly worse than the editor's built-in word highlight. |
+
+The "do not ship" decisions are *principled*, not deferred: the engine model
+deliberately keeps partials and helpers as host-registry lookups, so the
+editor has no honest source of truth for those refactorings. Documenting that
+here turns the absence into a feature.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* **VS Code**: All "ship" capabilities surface through `vscode-languageclient`
+  with no additional wiring — VS Code consumes advertised server capabilities
+  automatically.
+* **JetBrains**: The platform LSP client auto-consumes hover/completion/
+  diagnostics/codeAction. The new capabilities (`foldingRange`,
+  `documentSymbol`, `formatting`) require an `LspCustomization` opt-in or the
+  corresponding `Lsp4j*` extension in the descriptor; ADR-017's editor-side
+  amendment tracks the JetBrains-specific wiring as a maintenance item.
+* **Verifier**: `check:operations-paint` (added alongside this ADR) keeps the
+  catalog / painter parity honest, so the helper-name highlighting stays
+  trustworthy even as the prelude grows.
+* **Future**: Adding a cross-template scope graph would unlock `definition`,
+  `references`, `rename`, and `documentHighlight`. Designed in
+  [ADR-027](/adr/adr-0027-cross-template-scope-graph/) as an editor-side
+  workspace indexer over the engine's `tokenize`, no language-level changes
+  needed. Adding full LSP intelligence inside hybrid host+FlatBars templates
+  (`*.java.xbars` and friends) is designed in
+  [ADR-028](/adr/adr-0028-hybrid-template-lsp/) via VS Code's
+  `EmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider` API plus a virtual-document shim.
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted 2026-06-04. Effective immediately.

+---
+title: ADR-027 — Cross-template scope graph for the LSP
+---
+
+## Context
+
+[ADR-026](/adr/adr-0026-editor-capability-matrix/) fixed the LSP capability
+matrix and listed four capabilities the server deliberately does NOT ship —
+`textDocument/definition`, `textDocument/references`, `textDocument/rename`,
+`textDocument/documentHighlight` — on the grounds that the engine has no
+cross-template scope graph: partials and helpers are looked up at runtime
+through a host-supplied registry the engine never indexes. Without an editor-
+side index, those four capabilities would either return nothing or fall back
+to text-shaped string search (strictly worse than the editor's built-in word
+highlight).
+
+This record proposes the missing scope graph as a *separate, future work
+item* outside the editor surface — an engine-level addition that, once
+shipped, would unlock the four LSP capabilities almost mechanically.
+
+## Decision
+
+A cross-template scope graph is a workspace-scoped index built and maintained
+by the language server, structured around the two named references FlatBars
+templates actually carry:
+
+* **Partial names** — every `{{> name}}` (and `{{#> name}}`) is a reference;
+  every `{{#*inline "name"}} … {{/inline}}` block (FullBars) is a definition.
+* **Helper / operation names** — every identifier the painter resolves
+  through `editors/operations.json` is a reference to the catalogue entry;
+  user-defined helpers registered via `registerHelper` (ADR-018) are
+  definitions only the host knows about (out of editor scope until the
+  registry abstraction lands).
+
+The index is workspace-rooted: the LSP scans every file whose URI extension
+maps to a dialect (`dialectForUri` returns non-null), parses each into the
+token stream, and records `(name, defLocation)` and `(name, refLocation)`
+tuples. Two collections per workspace:
+
+* `partialDefinitions: Map<name, Location[]>` — the locations of inline
+  declarations.
+* `partialReferences: Map<name, Location[]>` — the locations of `{{> name}}`
+  invocations.
+
+Capability wiring:
+
+* `textDocument/definition` on a partial-name token (in either an inline
+  declaration or an invocation) returns the matching definitions.
+* `textDocument/references` returns all matching invocations (plus the
+  definition when `includeDeclaration` is set).
+* `textDocument/rename` proposes a `WorkspaceEdit` rewriting both the
+  definition and every invocation.
+* `textDocument/documentHighlight` (the in-file slice) returns the
+  definitions and references that share the file with the cursor.
+
+The index is *eventually consistent*: built on `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles`,
+re-indexed per-file on `textDocument/didChange`, garbage-collected on
+`textDocument/didClose` when the URI leaves the workspace. The LSP serves
+stale answers between batches rather than blocking on a full re-scan — the
+worst stale answer is "no result" which the four capabilities tolerate.
+
+## Phased plan
+
+. **Phase 1 — read-only scanner.** Add `editors/lsp/src/index.mjs` that
+  consumes the engine's `tokenize` over every workspace file and builds the
+  two maps. No LSP wiring yet; expose `definitionsOf(name)` /
+  `referencesOf(name)` for tests.
+. **Phase 2 — `textDocument/definition` + `documentHighlight`.** Wire the
+  first two capabilities into `server.mjs`; advertise both in the
+  `InitializeResult`. The single-buffer documentHighlight degrades to the
+  word-bounded set of references in the active file when the index is cold.
+. **Phase 3 — `textDocument/references`.** Same shape as definition; honours
+  `includeDeclaration`.
+. **Phase 4 — `textDocument/rename`.** Returns a `WorkspaceEdit` with one
+  `TextEdit` per occurrence. A pre-check rejects renames whose target collides
+  with an existing partial name.
+. **Phase 5 — helper / operation references.** Treat catalogue identifiers as
+  references too; the catalogue entries themselves are the definitions
+  (synthetic locations into `operations.json`).
+
+Tests at each phase: per-fixture corpus under `editors/lsp/test/fixtures/`
+asserting the index's contents, the capability's response, and at least one
+multi-file scenario.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* Unblocks the four ADR-026 omissions without requiring a language-level
+  module system. The engine itself stays unchanged — the LSP owns the index.
+* Adds workspace scanning to server startup; on large workspaces (10K+
+  templates) the initial scan needs streaming and progress notifications.
+  Implement with `workspace/configuration` so users can cap the scope.
+* `registerHelper`-style host-defined helpers remain unreachable until the
+  registry abstraction in ADR-018 grows an editor-visible projection.
+* User-defined inline partials in non-FullBars dialects are unreachable as
+  written — RawBars/MaxBars do not have `{{#*inline}}`. Either the partial
+  registry is host-provided (unindexable today) or partials become a
+  filesystem convention (one `.fullbars` file per partial name).
+
+## Status
+
+Proposed 2026-06-04. Implementation is gated on a small `tokenize`-based
+scanner; no language-level changes are required.

+---
+title: ADR-028 — Full LSP intelligence in hybrid host+FlatBars templates
+---
+
+## Context
+
+[ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) amended on 2026-06-04 added an
+injection grammar (`editors/flatbars-injection.tmLanguage.json`) so a hybrid
+file like `test.java.xbars` — opened as `java` via `files.associations` —
+gets Java syntax highlighting from the host grammar AND FlatBars tag
+highlighting layered on top via the injection. Hybrid templates work for
+*syntax highlighting* immediately, with zero per-file setup beyond the file
+association.
+
+What hybrid templates do NOT get is LSP intelligence on the FlatBars regions:
+the LSP attaches to the *host* language (Java's LSP), not to FlatBars. Hover,
+completion, diagnostics, the canonicalisation quick-fix, the new
+documentSymbol / foldingRange / formatting capabilities — none of these fire
+on `{{ … }}` tags in a hybrid file.
+
+The path forward is VS Code's `vscode.languages.registerEmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider`
+API (introduced 1.86) plus an `EmbeddedDocumentProvider` style scheme: extract
+the embedded FlatBars regions into a synthetic virtual document, forward LSP
+requests across the two languages, and map positions back through the
+extraction. This record proposes the design.
+
+## Decision
+
+The VS Code extension adds an `EmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider` for every host
+language listed in `editors/flatbars-injection.tmLanguage.json` `injectTo`
+(currently 26 hosts). For each FlatBars region in a hybrid file the provider
+exposes a *virtual document* the FlatBars LSP attaches to; the extension
+shims LSP requests between the user's editor (which targets the physical
+file) and the LSP (which sees the virtual file).
+
+Concretely:
+
+* **Region extraction.** A new helper in `editors/vscode/src/embedded.js`
+  scans the physical document for `{{ … }}` runs (the same regex the
+  injection grammar uses, in a JS port to keep them in lock-step). For each
+  run it records `(physicalRange, virtualOffset)`.
+* **Virtual document.** The hybrid document is reflected at a `flatbars-embedded:`
+  URI; its content is ` `-padded host text with the FlatBars tags spliced
+  in at their original offsets so column numbers match the physical document
+  exactly. The padding glyph is a non-breaking space that the FlatBars
+  tokenizer treats as content (never a tag).
+* **Request forwarding.** The extension intercepts every LSP request on the
+  physical document whose position falls inside an extracted region and
+  re-issues it against the virtual URI, then translates result ranges back.
+  Capabilities forwarded: hover, completion, codeAction, foldingRange,
+  documentSymbol, formatting. Diagnostics flow the other way — the LSP
+  publishes onto the virtual URI and the extension forwards them onto the
+  physical URI with translated ranges.
+* **Capability gating.** Requests whose position falls OUTSIDE every region
+  pass through to the host language unchanged. This is what makes "Java
+  intelligence on Java code, FlatBars intelligence on `{{ … }}` tags"
+  work simultaneously in one buffer.
+
+JetBrains follow-up: IntelliJ has an analogous concept (the LSP customization
+hook plus the `MultiHostLanguage` API). Wiring it is a separate ticket
+because the JetBrains Marketplace plugin currently consumes the LSP through
+the platform's stock client, which does not expose the multi-host hook.
+
+## Phased plan
+
+. **Phase 1 — extraction + virtual document.** Land `embedded.js` with a
+  unit test exercising every host's region extraction. No LSP wiring.
+. **Phase 2 — hover + diagnostics on virtual.** Wire the smallest pair to
+  prove the round-trip; gate behind a `flatbars.experimental.hybridLsp`
+  setting until the rough edges shake out.
+. **Phase 3 — completion + codeAction.** Adds the request types that mutate
+  the document (codeAction's `WorkspaceEdit` needs physical-URI ranges).
+. **Phase 4 — foldingRange + documentSymbol + formatting.** Same wiring as
+  Phase 3; documentSymbol's nested children need physical ranges.
+. **Phase 5 — drop the experimental gate.** Flip the default; document in
+  the editor README.
+
+Tests per phase: hybrid fixture corpus under `editors/vscode/test/embedded/`,
+one per host language, asserting position mapping in both directions
+(physical → virtual and virtual → physical).
+
+## Consequences
+
+* Unlocks every LSP capability inside hybrid templates without changing the
+  injection grammar or the LSP server. The complexity is purely
+  client-side wiring.
+* Performance: a hybrid file holds two LSP sessions simultaneously. The
+  virtual-document representation should be ephemeral (live in extension
+  memory, not the workspace) to keep watchers and indexers from doubling.
+* The padding strategy means line numbers in the virtual document always
+  match the physical document, which the LSP can stay oblivious to —
+  position translation is identity on column except across newlines. We
+  accept the small wasted bytes (` ` per host character) as the price
+  of zero column-math edge cases.
+* JetBrains side stays syntax-only until the multi-host hook ships there or
+  we add a custom integration. Communicate this in the JetBrains README so
+  Ultimate users aren't surprised.
+
+## Status
+
+Proposed 2026-06-04. Implementation gated on
+`vscode.languages.registerEmbeddedLanguageInfoProvider` (1.86+) and a small
+client-side region extractor; no engine or LSP server changes are required.

+---
+title: "ADR-0029: i18n via a host-plugged `t` (translate) operation, not bundled CLDR"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-029 i18n helper
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted — *implemented* 2026-06-05 (the blessed `t` prelude operation, interpreter +
+compiled runtime; the FlatBars Lab demonstrates the seam via native `Intl` — see the amendments). *Date:*
+2026-06-05. Builds on
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/) (helpers are the meaning plug-in; the core stays
+meaning-free), reuses the IoC callback shape of
+[ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/) (truthiness is a per-engine lambda the host plugs in, seeded into
+both interpreter and compiled runtime, *no per-file config, no baked data*), extends the user-extension
+path of [ADR-018](/adr/adr-0018-user-defined-helpers/) (`registerHelper`), and is gated by the
+compile ≡ interpret invariant of [ADR-011](/adr/adr-0011-compile-to-js/). It respects the dialect-purity
+boundaries of [ADR-007](/adr/adr-0007-minbars/) (MinBars is *Mustache*) and
+[ADR-009](/adr/adr-0009-fullbars/) (FullBars is *Handlebars-faithful*), using the engine-level opt-in
+precedent of [ADR-015](/adr/adr-0015-set-delimiters/) (set-delimiters is a MinBars-only knob, not a
+global). Escaping follows [ADR-002](/adr/adr-0002-escaping-and-value-policy/).
+
+## Context
+
+The https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparison_of_web_template_engines[Wikipedia comparison of web template
+engines] scores FlatBars *i18n: No*. The evidence is direct: the 90-operation prelude
+(`FullBars.preludeSchema`) ships no `t` / `translate` / `gettext`. Two facts frame the decision:
+
+* *This is the company we keep.* Handlebars and Mustache *also* have no built-in i18n — their ecosystems do it
+  with userland helpers/lambdas (i18next, `handlebars-i18n`, Mustache lambdas). So "absent from the core"
+  is not anomalous; the gap is a *workflow/DX* gap, not a correctness gap.
+* *i18n is meaning, and meaning is plugged in, not built in (ADR-001).* Real localization is not string
+  substitution: it needs *pluralization* (CLDR gives Polish/Arabic/Russian 3–6 plural categories),
+  *gender/select*, and locale-aware *number/date* formatting (ICU MessageFormat is the de-facto standard).
+  A naive key-lookup `t` produces grammatically wrong output for most languages — *worse* than nothing,
+  because it looks finished.
+
+Three hard constraints fell out of team review (debate recorded against this ADR):
+
+. *No CLDR/ICU data in our core or runtime.* The compiled runtime (`flatbars-runtime.mjs`) and the
+  committed Lab bundle are size-gated; CLDR plural data is tens of KB and would tax *every* compiled
+  template, including the majority that never localize.
+. *The prelude is one shared schema across all four dialects.* Adding `t` to the base prelude adds it to
+  *MinBars* (breaking the "pure Mustache" claim, ADR-007) and *FullBars* (Handlebars ships no `t`,
+  ADR-009) — a faithfulness regression even though byte-identical conformance would stay green (the spec
+  corpora never call `t`).
+. *Whatever ships must satisfy compile ≡ interpret (ADR-011)* or `test:compile` goes red.
+
+## Decision
+
+Adopt the truthiness pattern (ADR-022) for localization: *FlatBars supplies the call site; the host
+supplies the brain; we never bundle CLDR.*
+
+. *`t` is a blessed operation in the shared kernel prelude* (`Kernel.Prelude`), reserved for the
+  *core-surface family* — *RawBars, FullBars, and MaxBars* — and *absent from MinBars* (the separate
+  Mustache peer engine has its own closed prelude, so adding to the kernel prelude never touches it; ADR-007
+  stays intact). *RawBars is included precisely because it is the desugared core surface* (not a
+  meaning-free substrate): FullBars's `{{t …}}` desugars to a core `t` operation, so the operation
+  *must* exist at the RawBars level for the desugar target to be complete, and RawBars runs the same
+  prelude/engine. As implemented, the prelude `t` ships only the *fallback* (return the key unchanged); it
+  carries no locale or CLDR data. Because — like every prelude operation — `t` only fires when applied with
+  arguments (`{{t "k"}}`), a bare `{{t}}` still reads the data field `t`, so nothing is
+  shadowed.
+
+. *The host supplies the brain by registering `t`* (the IoC seam of ADR-018), not via a separate callback
+  parameter: the interpreter's `renderWith` helper bag and the compiled runtime's `rt.register("t", fn)`
+  both shadow the prelude fallback. The registered function receives the *message key* and the *named
+  arguments* (the `key=value` hash as a trailing dict) and closes over the locale (e.g.
+  `(key, args) => translate(locale, key, args)`). The host owns the catalog, locale resolution, and
+  all CLDR/ICU behaviour (plurals, select, gender, number/date) — typically its existing i18n library, or
+  the browser's native `Intl` (see the 2026-06-05 amendment). *FlatBars ships no plural rules and no CLDR
+  data.* Conceptually this is the truthiness pattern (ADR-022) — a host-plugged rule, the same on both
+  interpreter and compiled paths — reusing the registration seam rather than a bespoke env field.
+
+. *Surface.* The head is `t`, the first argument is the message key, the rest are named arguments:
++
+```handlebars
+{{t "cart.summary" count=cart.size name=user.name}}
+```
++
+In MaxBars this also composes with pipes (`cart.size | t "cart.summary"` is *not* the shape; the key is
+the head argument — pipe sugar applies to value-producing operations, see [maxbars](/engine/maxbars/)).
++
+*Name: lowercase `t`, not `T`.* An uppercase `T` was considered for ergonomics — it reads more like a
+sigil and is harder to overlook in a dense template — and rejected. `t` is the universal i18n function
+name (i18next, gettext, Rails, Vue, react-i18next), so it is recognized on sight and lets ported templates
+work unchanged; the prelude is case-sensitive, so `T` would silently break `{{t …}}`. It would also
+be the *only* uppercase operation among the 90 lowercase ones. Most importantly, `t` is an *operation
+name*, not a sigil (FlatBars has no keywords — "the head of an application is always a name", ADR-001);
+making it look like grammar would miscategorize it. The "don't overlook it" need is met in the *editor*
+layer instead — bold tag emphasis (ADR-026) and operation-name painting both already make `{{t …}}`
+stand out — which is the correct place for visual salience. No `translate` alias ships (canonical-only;
+legacy spellings are a lint concern, ADR-019).
+
+. *Escaping is unchanged (ADR-002).* The callback returns a `String`; it lands *escaped* in
+  `{{t …}}` and *raw* in `{{{t …}}}`, exactly like every other helper, with `safe` as the
+  SafeString escape hatch. Messages that intentionally carry markup use the triple-stache. *No new
+  escaping axis is introduced.*
+
+. *Missing-key policy: fallback-and-flag, never throw.* With no `t` registered the prelude fallback renders
+  the key unchanged (a host that returns a marker for a missing key gets that instead), and *analyse mode*
+  (ADR-022 Part B) / the linter can flag it. A strict mode that errors on a missing key is opt-in (for CI,
+  not render). Production renders never hard-fail on one missing translation.
+
+. *compile ≡ interpret.* The prelude fallback is *pure* (return the key), so a template using `t` with no
+  host registration renders byte-identically interpreted and compiled. With a host `t`, the same registered
+  function runs on both paths (`renderWith` for the interpreter, `rt.register` for the compiled runtime).
+  `test:compile` gates the no-host case; the with-host parity is verified directly.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* The Wikipedia *i18n: No* becomes *Yes (host-plugged)* for RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars, with the honest
+  footnote that the plural/format brain is the host's — which is exactly how i18next-backed Handlebars works.
+* The catalog gains a `t` entry (`FullBars.Catalog`, the LSP `operations.json`); `npm run gen:catalog` and
+  `npm run gen:operations` regenerate them and `check:catalog` / `check:operations` gate the drift. `t` is
+  now hover-documented and operation-painted in the editors.
+* *Only MinBars is unaffected* — its separate closed prelude does not gain `t`, so ADR-007 purity and the
+  Mustache conformance claim are untouched. RawBars *does* gain `t` (ADR-008's `nonEmpty` truthiness is
+  orthogonal and unchanged); this is required, not incidental — it is the desugar target FullBars/MaxBars
+  lower to. FullBars's `t` is an *extension* beyond Handlebars (faithful to the workflow, not a Handlebars
+  built-in); `hbs-conformance` is unaffected because the corpus never calls `t`.
+* Zero bundle-size impact and no behavioural change for templates that don't localize: no CLDR ships, and a
+  bare `{{t}}` still resolves to the data field.
+
+### What we explicitly do NOT do
+
+* *No ICU MessageFormat engine in-core, no CLDR plural rules in our runtime* (rejected option D in the
+  debate): heavy data, violates meaning-free + the bundle gates. Plurals are the host's job.
+* *No per-file `@locale` directive.* Locale is the host's, closed over by the registered `t` — mirroring
+  ADR-022's rejection of per-file `@truthiness`.
+* *No `t` in MinBars.* It lives in the *kernel* prelude (shared by RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars), never in
+  MinBars's separate Mustache prelude — so the Mustache-purity claim stays clean without a conditional
+  mechanism (rejected option B was forcing it onto *every* engine, which would have hit MinBars).
+* *No dedicated translate-callback parameter or new env field.* The host plugs in through the existing
+  ADR-018 registration seam (`renderWith` / `rt.register`), which already marshals a host function and
+  shadows the prelude fallback — no second mechanism.
+
+## Alternatives considered (debate ratings)
+
+|  |  |  |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Option | Summary | Verdict |
+| A — recipe only | Document `registerHelper('t', …)` + i18next; ship no engine surface. The honest "you can already do this today" answer, and how Handlebars/Mustache users localize. | *Adopt as the interim*, but it documents a workaround rather than closing the gap. |
+| B — `t` in the base prelude | Simplest, but adds `t` to MinBars + FullBars schemas. | Rejected — pollutes Mustache/Handlebars faithfulness. |
+| C — opt-in module + host `translate` callback | This ADR. Truthiness pattern applied to localization; no CLDR shipped; dialect-gated. | *Accepted (proposed).* |
+| D — full ICU/CLDR in-core | Correct plurals out of the box, but tens of KB of data in core/runtime. | Rejected — violates meaning-free + bundle gates. |
+| E — `number` / `date` / `selectPlural` (+ `relative`) helpers | A locale-aware formatting helper set, same host-register discipline. | *Adopted* — all are blessed prelude operations alongside `t` (pure fallbacks: plain text; the English one/other rule; "N units ago"). All four accept an Intl options hash — the trailing dict passes through with no arity change (the fallbacks ignore it; the host reads it). |
+
+## Follow-ups
+
+. ✅ *Done — the interim recipe and Lab demo:* the `/localize` guide renders `{{t …}}` live via the
+  host-register seam, on the browser's native `Intl` (see the 2026-06-05 amendment), gated by `check:i18n`.
+. ✅ *Done — this ADR (C):* the `t` prelude operation (RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars; not MinBars), the host
+  brain via the ADR-018 registration seam (interpreter + compiled runtime), the pure key-returning
+  fallback, catalog/operations generation, and `test:compile` parity.
+. ✅ *Done — the E formatting set:* `number` / `date` / `selectPlural` / `relative` are blessed prelude
+  operations alongside `t` (pure fallbacks — plain text, the English one/other rule, and "N units ago" —
+  overridden by the host's native `Intl`). All four read an Intl options hash
+  (`{{number n style="currency" currency="EUR"}}`, `{{selectPlural n type="ordinal"}}`,
+  `{{relative v u numeric="always"}}`), which the trailing dict delivers without an arity change.
+. *Conformance note:* add an `i18n` row to [fullbars-compat](/engine/fullbars-compat/) documenting that the `t` operation
+  (shared by RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars) is an *extension* beyond Handlebars (faithful to the workflow, not a
+  Handlebars built-in), the same framing ADR-018 used for `registerHelper`.
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-05): the Lab demonstrates the seam via native `Intl` — i18next is not vendored
+
+The question arose of whether to vendor *i18next* into the FlatBars Lab and build an i18n guide around
+it, the way the Lab vendors `jsonata` (`lab/vendor/jsonata.mjs`, ~78 KB) for the data-shaping guide. Team
+review (debate recorded against this ADR) rejected vendoring and adopted *option C+*: the Lab demonstrates
+the i18n integration *seam* using the browser's native `Intl`, with i18next available only as an
+*unbundled* documented escape hatch.
+
+Decision and rationale:
+
+. *No i18next in the bundle.* The browser already ships the CLDR brain — `Intl.PluralRules` (every
+  language's plural categories), `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat` — at *zero* bytes. JSONata
+  earned its vendor because data-shaping-before-render has no platform equivalent; i18n's plural/format
+  machinery *is* the platform, so vendoring i18next would be redundant weight plus a version/CVE pin and an
+  ecosystem blessing. The Lab vendors a library only when the platform can't already do the job.
+
+. *Demonstrate the seam, framed as Lab-as-host.* A live card (`tutorials/src/components/TryI18n.jsx`,
+  sibling of `TryJsonata.jsx`) and a `/localize` guide wire a `t` helper to native `Intl` via the existing
+  `registerHelper` / `renderWith` path (ADR-018) — *not* a new engine feature. This *reinforces* the
+  ADR's "i18n is the host's job" thesis (the Lab is acting as the host) rather than implying FlatBars does
+  i18n; the page says so explicitly.
+
+. *No dependency on the unimplemented `t` operation.* Riding the ADR-018 `registerHelper`/`renderWith`
+  seam, the demo ships today as the living proof of follow-up 1 (the interim recipe) and migrates to the
+  blessed `t` (follow-up 2) when the module lands.
+
+. *Cheap gate.* `scripts/check-i18n.mjs` (mirroring `check:jsonata`) renders the `{{t …}}` cells
+  across locales — including one with non-trivial plurals (Polish: one/few/many/other) and per-locale
+  number grouping — and asserts the output. There is no vendored dependency to pin.
+
+. *Escape hatch, unbundled.* The guide shows a one-paragraph stub for swapping the `Intl` wrapper for
+  i18next or ICU MessageFormat (`@formatjs`) in a real host — fidelity without the bytes.
+
+Future option (non-blocking): if users ask to demo *their* i18next setup, load it lazily via dynamic
+`import()` on demand, never in the base bundle, keeping the 0-byte default.
+
+### Lab integration (2026-06-05): first-class catalog.yaml + config.yaml views
+
+The Lab exposes the seam as two dedicated sidebar *views* (not partial tabs), mirroring the engine's
+data/config split: a *LOCALIZATION* section with *`catalog.yaml`* (the message DATA, locale-keyed; shown
+on every surface except MinBars) and a generalized *`config.yaml`* (the former Stem-only `stem.config.yaml`)
+that now also carries `i18n.locale` on the t-surfaces and `minbars.truthiness` on MinBars — the latter
+replacing the old mustache.js-truthiness UI toggle. The render routes RawBars/FullBars/MaxBars through the
+helper Worker (`lab/i18n.mjs` `buildI18nHelpers`), so
+`{{t …}}`/`number`/`date`/`selectPlural`/`relative` resolve from `catalog.yaml` bound to the locale
+the Lab parses from `config.yaml` (its inline `parseConfigYaml`). One shared catalog/config (the groups are
+surface-scoped), not per-surface storage.
+The `/localize` *Open in Lab* round-trips the catalog + locale into those views (`cat`/`loc` workspace
+fields). The data pane is shared by data/config/catalog, so a `dataPaneMode` flag routes edits by what the
+pane displays — config/catalog keystrokes never fall through to `data.yaml`.
+
+#### The Lab's MinBars truthiness default is `mustacheJs`, by design
+
+The engine, CLI, and JS facade default MinBars to the *language-agnostic spec* rule (`0`/`""`/`{}` truthy,
+as in Ruby/Python Mustache); `mustacheJs` (`0`/`""` falsy) is the opt-in (`renderMinbars({compat})`,
+`flatbars --mustache-js`). The *Lab* deliberately inverts that default: `config.yaml`'s
+`minbars.truthiness` starts at *`mustacheJs`*, not `spec`.
+
+The reason is the Lab's audience and habitat. It runs in the browser, where `mustache.js` is *the* Mustache
+people have used — so its truthiness (`0`/`""` falsy) is what a JS author already expects. Defaulting the
+playground to the rule its visitors carry in their heads minimises surprising "why did my `0` render?"
+moments, especially for beginners meeting Mustache through the Lab. The spec rule stays one keystroke away
+(`minbars.truthiness: spec`); the engine's own default is unchanged, so nothing downstream of the Lab
+shifts. This is a *presentation* choice scoped to the playground, not an engine policy change (ADR-022).
+
+Consistent with that default, the share link omits the truthiness field for `mustacheJs` and records only
+the spec opt-out (`mj=0`), keeping the common link compact. (One consequence: a pre-2026-06-05 MinBars link
+that relied on the *old* default-`spec` — no `mj` field — now renders under `mustacheJs`; such links predate
+the i18n/config work and are vanishingly rare. Add `minbars.truthiness: spec` to restore the old reading.)
+
+## Amendment (2026-06-05): i18n is a first-class host seam, not a `registerHelper` shadow
+
+The original Decision wired the host's brain by *registering* `t`/`number`/`date` as a user operation
+(the `renderWith` bag / `rt.register`) that *shadows* the prelude fallback. That worked, but it left the
+engine unable to distinguish "a translator is wired" from "nobody wired one" — so the promised *flag*
+("fallback-and-flag") could not be made precise, and the claim to "adopt the truthiness pattern (ADR-022)"
+was aspirational. The implementation is now the *first-class seam* the Decision described:
+
+* *The seam.* `Kernel.Value.Translator` (`String -> Array Value -> Maybe String`) is seeded
+  per-engine — `RefEnv.translator` via `withTranslator` (interpreter, the i18n analogue of `withTruthy`),
+  and `rt.registerTranslator` (compiled runtime). `Nothing` means "no host", which the engine *knows*.
+* *All five blessed ops are seam-driven* (`t`/`number`/`date`/`selectPlural`/`relative`): a `seamed name
+  fallback` wrapper consults the translator and runs the op's pure fallback when it is absent or declines.
+  So the *seam*, not the op identity, decides translated-vs-fallback, and interpreter ≡ compiled (the
+  fallback path is gated by `test:compile`; the wired path by `check:i18n`).
+* *The flag is now precise (ADR-029 #2).* Analyse renders with no translator seeded, so it reports every
+  i18n op that fell back ("no translator wired — register one or ship keys") as an *awareness note* — never
+  a CI-gating lint, so it cannot false-positive a wired project.
+* *Consumers use the seam.* The `flatbars-js` facade exposes `renderSurfaceI18n` (host translator as a JS
+  `(name, args) => string | null`); the Lab's `TryI18n` island, `check:i18n`, and the `/localize`
+  host recipe all seed a translator (`registerTranslator`), not `registerHelper`. FullBars carrying these
+  ops is recorded as an explicit exception in [ADR-009](/adr/adr-0009-fullbars/) (no faithfulness-by-omission).
+
+The Lab worker (`helpers-worker.mjs`) renders pure i18n (no custom helpers, FullBars — the common
+localization case) through the seam (`renderSurfaceI18n`); the *combined* i18n+custom-helpers render (and
+RawBars/MaxBars i18n) still merges the i18n bag with the custom helpers, where a registered i18n op shadows
+the seamed prelude op (identical output). The wired-translator `test:compile` case now gates the
+compiled≡interpret wired path too (the fallback path was already gated).
+
+Remaining (tracked, non-blocking): a combined translator+helpers render entry across all three core-surface
+dialects, which would let the worker's combined/RawBars/MaxBars i18n use the seam directly rather than the
+shadowing bag.

+---
+title: "ADR-0030: symbolic analyse mode, coverage honesty, and the host `PathSchema` seam"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-030 symbolic analyse
+---
+
+*Status:* Accepted — *implemented* 2026-06-06. Extends [ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/) (analyse
+mode, the data-driven truthiness portability check): same `Decision` trace, same named-rule menu, same
+`reportMarkdown`/`findings`/`jsonataScaffold` outputs. Reuses the host-pluggable-callback pattern of
+[ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/) (`Truthy`) and [ADR-029](/adr/adr-0029-i18n-helper/)
+(`Translator`) for the new `PathSchema` seam. Respects the meaning-free thesis of
+[ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/): no schema is baked; the host plugs it in.
+
+## Context
+
+Analyse mode (ADR-022 Part B) renders a template against *real data* and observes every truthiness
+decision the engine made, flagging the ambiguous four (`0` `""` `[]` `{}`) when a named rule would branch
+the other way. It is genuinely useful — but it has one structural weakness that a team review surfaced:
+
+* *It only sees what the sample data exercises.* The report literally says "_no portability findings — for
+  that data_". A green run on `{ "count": 5 }` says nothing about `count: 0`. "No findings" reads as "safe"
+  but proves only "safe for this one sample" — a footgun.
+* *The fix can't be "provide better data".* Hand-crafting adversarial data for every path does not scale, and
+  the engine has no schema to reason about which values a path can hold (ADR-001: types are a host concern).
+
+The goal is to decouple *coverage* from the data sample without baking a type system into the meaning-free
+core, and to make "no findings" honest about its scope.
+
+## Decision
+
+. *Symbolic what-if (potential findings).* For every condition whose *observed* value is **not** one of the
+  ambiguous four and not always-falsy (`false`/`null`), derive the *same-type* ambiguous value — a number ⇒
+  `0`, a non-empty string ⇒ `""`, a non-empty array ⇒ `[]`, a non-empty object ⇒ `{}` — and emit a
+  **potential finding** ("`count` (observed `5`) would diverge if it ever holds `0`"). This is a pure
+  post-process over the recorded `Decision`s — no extra render, no new wrapper — so its output is a function
+  of the *template*, not the sample, which is what CI wants to gate. A *bare-path* condition carries its
+  data path and JSONata fix; a *computed* condition (`{{#if (and a b)}}`) gets the same type-based
+  potential finding without a targetable path (the generation half of the review's #1/#5, unified).
+
+. *Coverage honesty.* Every `Finding` gains a `kind` (`"observed"` vs `"potential"`), and `reportMarkdown`
+  states what it checked: _N conditions evaluated · M observed · K potential_, with potential findings in
+  their own clearly-hypothetical section ("_would diverge if …_"). "No observed findings" can no longer be
+  misread as "portable for all data".
+
+. *Optional host `PathSchema` seam.* A host may plug in `PathSchema = String -> Value -> Boolean`
+  ("could this path hold this value?") — seeded exactly like `Truthy` (ADR-022) and `Translator`
+  (ADR-029), **not** baked. A potential finding for path `p` and ambiguous value `av` is suppressed when
+  `schema p av == false` (the host's types rule it out: "`count` is always a present positive number").
+  Default is `\_ _ -> true` (no schema ⇒ every what-if stands), so it costs nothing when unused and never
+  violates the meaning-free core.
+
+. *Data-access misses as an advisory finding.* Analyse also wraps `lookup`, recording bare paths that
+  resolve to absent/`null`. These surface as `kind: "miss"` findings ("`user.naem` resolved to null for this
+  data — likely a typo"), the highest-signal typo catcher we have. Like every data-observed signal they are
+  *advisory* and carry the same coverage caveat ("for this data").
+
+. *Lint stays static; analyse owns data + symbolic.* The split from the review holds: `flatbars lint`
+  remains static, value-free, and CI-gating (aliases, scoped variables, i18n usage); analyse owns everything
+  data- or symbolic-driven and stays *advisory* — observed/miss findings depend on the sample, and only the
+  symbolic *potential* findings (a function of the template) are stable enough to gate. They cross-link, they
+  do not merge.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* The facade `analyze(template, data)` returns observed **and** potential **and** miss findings (each tagged
+  `kind`), and the report leads with the coverage line. `analyzeWith(schema, template, data)` adds the host
+  `PathSchema`. The Lab Truthiness panel groups by `kind`; `/analyse` teaches "observed vs potential".
+* The named-rule machinery, the `recoverPath`/`fixFor`/`describe` helpers, and `jsonataScaffold` are reused
+  unchanged — potential findings emit the same JSONata cleanup for their (hypothetical) path.
+* No new render pass: symbolic findings are derived from the existing `Decision` trace, so analyse stays a
+  single pure render (`WriterT (Array Decision) (Either Error)`), no `Effect`/`Aff`.
+* The `PathSchema` seam is the third instance of the same pattern (truthiness, i18n, now schema) — the host
+  supplies meaning, the core stays meaning-free.

+---
+title: "ADR-0031: migrate the spec site from Antora (AsciiDoc) to Astro Starlight (MDX)"
+sidebar:
+  label: ADR-031 spec site → Starlight
+---
+
+*Status:* Proposed — 2026-06-06. A documentation-toolchain decision; it touches no
+engine semantics. Execution is gated on a de-risk spike (a Markdown emitter for the
+helper catalog, one converted page, and one live engine pane); the ADR flips to
+*Accepted* when that spike is green, and amends if it is not. Owner: Werner. The
+full sequencing, file map, and gate changes live in `STARLIGHT_MIGRATION_PLAN.md`
+at the repository root. Honours the design-system single-source-of-truth contracts of
+[ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) (tokens, vocabulary, one wordmark) and
+keeps the spec as the contract the packages target
+([ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/)).
+
+## Context
+
+The normative spec in `docs/` is the contract the PureScript packages target — 46
+AsciiDoc pages (≈7,360 lines), of which 31 are ADRs, built today by Antora
+(`npm run docs`). Antora has served well but carries friction this project keeps
+hitting:
+
+* *It builds from git HEAD, so a linked worktree cannot build it in place* — a
+  recurring footgun for a repo that uses worktrees.
+* *AsciiDoc cannot import the live engine.* The learner site (`tutorials/`, Astro 6 +
+  Preact) renders *real* engine output inline by importing `lab/vendor/flatbars-engine.mjs`;
+  the spec cannot, so every example in the contract is hand-transcribed rather than
+  machine-rendered.
+* *Search needs a bolt-on extension*, and the UI comes from a remote `ui-bundle.zip`
+  pinned at HEAD rather than from the project's own design system.
+
+A team review weighed three options — stay on Antora, adopt Docusaurus, or adopt
+Astro Starlight. Docusaurus was rejected: it is a *third* rendering stack (React)
+alongside the existing Astro/Preact, which would fork the shared wordmark and token
+layer ([ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/)) and duplicate the base-path /
+Lab-origin machinery the tutorials build already solves. Starlight wins on stack
+unity (same Astro family, reuses the design system and the Preact islands), built-in
+offline Pagefind search, and a direct path to live engine panes in the spec.
+
+The cost is real and was measured, not assumed: *1,223* `{{` openers (MDX
+treats `{{` and `<` as expression/JSX syntax — most sit inside source blocks,
+which become MDX-exempt fenced code, leaving a small prose-brace audit), and *353*
+`xref:` cross-references whose build-time integrity guarantee must be reconstructed,
+since MDX has none natively.
+
+## Decision
+
+Migrate the spec — and only the spec — to Astro Starlight, as follows.
+
+. *Target = Astro Starlight (MDX).* Same stack family as the tutorials; built-in
+  offline Pagefind; reuses the design system; avoids a third framework.
+
+. *Standalone app, not folded into `tutorials/`.* The spec ships as its own
+  Starlight project under `/spec`, linked to/from the tutorials via the existing
+  `PUBLIC_SPEC_BASE` seam — which already separates the two surfaces across several
+  pages. Isolating the contract's build keeps a careless tutorial edit from
+  red-building the spec's deploy. Shared look-and-feel comes from a factored
+  `shared/` module (wordmark, tokens, base-path/Lab helpers), *not* a merged build.
+
+. *Big-bang cutover.* One branch, one reviewable diff, one merge; rollback is a
+  revert while `docs/` stays intact until the final step.
+
+. *Versioning snapshots essential releases only.* The `starlight-versions` plugin,
+  triggered on tagged spec releases (first `0.1.0`), bounded to avoid folder-snapshot
+  bloat. HEAD is "current".
+
+. *All 31 ADRs convert; flat `adr/*.mdx`, status in frontmatter, grouped only in the
+  sidebar.* Status changes over an ADR's life; its URL must not, so status never
+  enters the path.
+
+. *Route `/spec`, dropping Antora's redundant component segment* (`/flatbars/spec/<page>`,
+  not `…/spec/flatbars/<page>`). A redirect map plus a new `check:redirects` gate keep
+  old URLs and in-repo `.adoc` links resolving — link stability is gated, not hoped.
+
+. *Build-time guarantees are reconstructed, not dropped.* `starlight-links-validator`
+  (build-failing) replaces Antora's `xref` integrity; `astro check` + `astro build`
+  replace the AsciiDoc parse gate; a `check:mdx-braces` lint fails on unescaped
+  `{{`/`<` outside fences.
+
+. *ADR-031 is recorded "Proposed" first and flipped to "Accepted" only after a
+  de-risk spike* proves the three unknowns together: the catalog Markdown emitter, a
+  representative page conversion (`concepts`), and one working live engine pane.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+
+*Docusaurus v3* was the other serious MDX candidate and is rejected. Its pitch rests
+on three claims that do not survive contact with this project's scope: (1) *stateful
+SPA interactivity* for "AST parsing labs" — but the interactive surfaces (`lab/`,
+framework-neutral HTML/JS/WASM on its own origin; the Preact islands in `tutorials/`)
+are *not* part of the spec and do not migrate, and Astro's islands architecture
+ships interactive components fine while emitting zero JS for the prose that dominates
+a contract document; (2) *native versioning* — genuinely more mature than Starlight's
+`starlight-versions` plugin, but down-weighted because this ADR snapshots essential
+releases only (D4), and both use the same folder-snapshot model; and (3)
+*future-proofing via Rspack + maintainer backing* — Rspack speeds builds, not the
+runtime payload Starlight already wins, and "institutional backing" is symmetric (Astro
+is a funded project with a first-party docs product). Decisively, Docusaurus is a
+*React* stack — a third frontend framework beside Astro/Preact — which would fork the
+design-system single-sources of [ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) (tokens,
+vocabulary, one wordmark) and duplicate the base-path / Lab-origin machinery the
+tutorials build already owns. Stack unity, less shipped JS for a prose spec, and design-system
+reuse outweigh Docusaurus's lone real edge in versioning maturity.
+
+## Consequences
+
+* *The codegen single-sources are preserved, not broken.* `FullBars.Catalog` gains a
+  `helperCatalogMarkdown` emitter beside the AsciiDoc one (same `preludeSchema`
+  source), so `check:catalog` stays a gate on the MDX partial. `gen:tokens` writes the
+  shared token CSS once for both sites; `check:adr-nav` and `check:glossary` repoint to
+  the MDX sources. The design-system invariants of
+  [ADR-017](/adr/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp/) survive intact.
+
+* *Scope is fenced.* The `tutorials/` site is *not* migrated: its 10 pages are
+  component-dominant interactive apps (live analyse panes, galleries, JSONata fixers),
+  not prose, and stay bespoke `.astro` + Preact. "Starlight everywhere" is rejected —
+  format follows content shape. Mermaid diagrams and a broad live-pane rollout are
+  out of migration scope (the mechanism is proven once in the spike; rollout is a
+  follow-up).
+
+* *A new capability is unlocked:* the spec can render real engine output inline, the
+  same way the tutorials do, closing the hand-transcription gap.
+
+* *`CLAUDE.md` is updated as part of the cutover* — its Antora-specific guidance
+  (`npm run docs`, the playbook, `supplemental-ui`, the worktree-HEAD caveat) is
+  rewritten for the Starlight toolchain.
+
+* *Follow-ups, tracked separately:* unified cross-site Pagefind search; promoting
+  `shared/` to a real `@flatbars/design-system` workspace package; the Mermaid
+  dialect-ladder diagram; the live-pane content rollout.
