+---
+title: Final ADR review (2026-06-01)
+sidebar:
+  label: Final ADR review
+---
+
+A cross-cutting review of the whole ADR set ([001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/)–[013](/adr/adr-0013-labelled-loops/))
+once they were drafted together. The goal was not to re-approve each record but to find the *seams
+between* them — the places where two ADRs are individually true and jointly misleading. Same cast as
+the ADR-001 review. Suggestions rated 1–5 (5 = adopt now).
+
+:::note
+*Post-review status (2026-06-01).* Several rating-5 items below were actioned in the same pass:
+the two extension axes are now named in [adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams](/adr/adr-0004-token-lexer-and-grammar-seams/);
+superset-vs-isolation is sharpened in [adr-0003-strict-layering](/adr/adr-0003-strict-layering/)/[adr-0005-dialect-ladder](/adr/adr-0005-dialect-ladder/);
+the engine-conformance checklist landed in [host-api](/engine/host-api/) §7.7; the "FullBars" term is split in
+[adr-0008-rawbars](/adr/adr-0008-rawbars/)/[adr-0009-fullbars](/adr/adr-0009-fullbars/) and the RawBars docstring fixed; the
+directives decision is recorded in [adr-0010-header-directives](/adr/adr-0010-header-directives/) and the `mustache` alias added
+to [directives](/engine/directives/). *Still open (code, not docs):* the recursion guard
+([adr-0012-recursion-budget](/adr/adr-0012-recursion-budget/)), the two regression tests, and the loop-variable warn-always
+change.
+:::
+
+## The tensions found
+
+### 1. Two different "extension points" wear one word
+
+*Devi:* "ADR-004 warns that a third *grammar seam* would be a smell, then ADR-007 cheerfully adds new
+*sigils*. A reader will think MinBars is the forbidden third seam. It isn't — there are *two
+orthogonal axes* and we never named them. Axis A is the **grammar seam**: `parseExpr`/`parseHead`,
+how a dialect parses a tag *interior* (`Parser.purs:57`). Axis B is the **shape gate**: `extras` and
+the MinBars sigils, which *tag shapes* a dialect admits (`Parser.purs:271`). Adding sigils grows axis
+B and is fine; adding a third grammar seam grows axis A and is the smell."
+
+*Mara:* "Agreed, and this is the deeper point behind ADR-001's reword. The parser is *name*-agnostic
+(axis-free), *shape-aware* and *shape-gated* (axis B), and *grammar-pluggable* (axis A). Three
+sentences, three mechanisms. Right now ADR-004 blurs A and B in one 'Watch' note."
+
+*Consensus:* name the two axes explicitly in ADR-004 and cross-link ADR-007's sigils to axis B.
+*Rating 5.*
+
+### 2. "RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars" vs. "no dialect imports another"
+
+*Petra:* "ADR-003 says dialects never import each other; ADR-005 says `maxbars → fullbars` is fine.
+Both are in the record, a click apart. That looks like the dogma cracked."
+
+*Kai:* "It didn't crack — it was never about imports. `⊂` is a *surface-superset* claim: every MaxBars
+template that avoids operators is a FullBars template. Package isolation is a *different* property,
+and RawBars *does* have it (FullBars-free closure, ADR-003). MaxBars deliberately trades isolation for
+reuse because it genuinely *is* a superset. The fix is wording: say 'no dialect imports another
+*except along the ladder's superset edge*,' and state plainly that `⊂` ≠ isolation."
+
+*Soren:* "Then make it falsifiable: a test asserting RawBars' closure excludes `fullbars`, so the one
+allowed exception can't quietly become two."
+
+*Consensus:* reword both ADRs to separate *superset* from *isolation*; add the closure test.
+*Rating 5.*
+
+### 3. The conformance checklist is promised in three ADRs and exists in none
+
+*Soren:* "ADR-001 promised an engine-conformance checklist. ADR-002 leans on it for safety. ADR-007
+needs it to even define what 'MinBars conforms' means. It is load-bearing in three records and
+written in zero files. We are accumulating an IOU."
+
+*Devi:* "It's small, though — escape fn, stringify, truthiness default, raw-output stance, sigil set,
+real-AST-shape-or-none. That's a table in `host-api.adoc`, not a research project."
+
+*Mara:* "Build it now, precisely because three ADRs depend on it. An undefined contract is worse than
+no contract — it lets every engine claim conformance."
+
+*Consensus:* write the checklist into [host-api](/engine/host-api/) before MinBars starts. *Rating 5.*
+
+### 4. Does MinBars retro-justify or violate ADR-003's "extract lazily"?
+
+*Mara:* "ADR-007 forces *new* kernel features — a per-engine truthiness default, a recursion guard.
+ADR-003 said extract lazily. Is MinBars making us extract *eagerly* for a thing that isn't built?"
+
+*Kai:* "The opposite. 'Extract lazily' means *on a proven second consumer*. The truthiness default
+already has two consumers the moment MinBars needs `mustache` while the others need `handlebars` —
+that *is* the second consumer. Same for the recursion guard: it hardens the reference `partialH`
+*today* (`Prelude.purs:501` is unbounded) and serves MinBars tomorrow. These are textbook lazy
+extractions, not speculation."
+
+*Devi:* "One caveat — do them as *P0 shared prereqs* (ADR-007's own phase plan) and keep them green
+under the existing suites, or we destabilise three shipped dialects for one unshipped one."
+
+*Consensus:* ADR-007's P0 ordering is correct; note in ADR-003 that MinBars is the worked example of
+its lazy-extraction rule. *Rating 4.*
+
+### 5. The loop-variable lint only fires with a schema
+
+*Soren:* "ADR-006 catches `length`/`first`/`key` shadowing *only when a schema is present*. Most
+templates have no schema. That's the majority case going unguarded for a footgun we *introduced* by
+dropping `@`."
+
+*Kai:* "Without a schema we can't know `first` is a data field rather than the loop var — there's no
+oracle. Erroring blindly would break legitimate templates."
+
+*Soren:* "Not an error — a *warning*. 'bare `first` resolves to the loop variable here; wrap the field
+as `(lookup this \"first\")` if you meant the datum.' Warn always, error only with a schema."
+
+*Mara:* "That's the right severity split and it matches how `escapingWarnings` already behaves —
+warn-by-default, never silently wrong."
+
+*Consensus:* ADR-006 gains a schema-less *warning* tier under the schema-present *error*. *Rating 4.*
+
+### 6. Granularity: are 003/004/005 over-split?
+
+*Devi:* "Three ADRs for one migration quarter. Merge?"
+
+*Petra:* "No — they have *different reversal costs*. Re-layering packages (003) is a quarter of work;
+swapping a grammar seam (004) is a function type; rearranging the ladder (005) is a dependency edge.
+A future change touches one, not all three. Separate records, heavily cross-linked, is correct."
+
+*Consensus:* keep them separate. *Rating 4* (for the cross-linking, which was thin in the first
+drafts).
+
+### 7. "FullBars" names two different things (ADR-008/009)
+
+*Kai:* "ADR-008 says RawBars' closure is *FullBars-free*, then RawBars' own docstring says it renders
+'against the FullBars reference engine.' Both ship. A reader cannot tell whether RawBars uses FullBars
+or not."
+
+*Devi:* "Because 'FullBars' is overloaded. There's *FullBars the engine* — value policy + prelude +
+`lower`, which moved to `kernel` (ADR-003) — and *FullBars the package/dialect*, which is now only the
+surface desugar + renderers + catalog. RawBars uses the former (via `kernel`) and not the latter. The
+prose conflates them, and ADR-008's own *Con* admits the docstring is stale."
+
+*Mara:* "This is the same disease as tension #1 and #2 — one word, two referents. Decide the
+vocabulary: 'the *reference engine*' = the `kernel` machinery; 'the *FullBars dialect*' = the package.
+Then RawBars' sentence becomes true: 'renders against the reference engine, with no surface desugar.'"
+
+*Petra:* "And fix the RawBars docstring in the same change, or we've documented the bug instead of
+the decision."
+
+*Consensus:* split the term — *reference engine* (kernel) vs *FullBars dialect* (package) — in ADR-008/009
+and the RawBars docstring. *Rating 4.*
+
+## Consensus summary
+
+. *Name the two extension axes* — grammar seam (`parseExpr`/`parseHead`) vs. shape gate
+  (`extras`/sigils) — in ADR-004; stop letting one word cover both.
+. *Separate "superset" from "isolation"* in ADR-003/005; the ladder's `⊂` is about surface, the
+  isolation rule is about imports, and they have exactly one sanctioned crossing (`maxbars → fullbars`).
+  (Later narrowed: the 2026-06-04 ADR-005 amendment redefines `⊂` as surface-superset *modulo
+  documented exceptions* — MaxBars borrows most of FullBars's surface, not all, so Kai's "genuinely
+  *is* a superset" above holds only up to those exceptions.)
+. *Write the engine-conformance checklist now* — it is load-bearing in ADR-001/002/007 and exists
+  nowhere.
+. *MinBars is the worked example of lazy extraction*, not a violation of it; its P0 prereqs
+  (truthiness default, recursion guard) land first and stay green.
+. *The loop-variable shadow check warns always, errors with a schema.*
+. *003/004/005 stay separate* — different reversal costs — but cross-linked.
+. *Disambiguate "FullBars"* — the *reference engine* (the `kernel` machinery) vs the *FullBars
+  dialect* (the package: surface desugar + renderers + catalog). RawBars uses the former, not the
+  latter; the prose must say so.
+
+## Potential future developments
+
+* *[ADR-012](/adr/adr-0012-recursion-budget/) (recursion & resource budget)* — now drafted
+  (Proposed); the depth/budget model (default 64, directive override, overflow behaviour) still needs
+  *implementation*, and it touches MinBars, labelled loops, and self-including partials.
+* *[ADR-013](/adr/adr-0013-labelled-loops/) (labelled loops)* — now drafted (Proposed); lifts the
+  ADR-006 §5 v1 outer-loop limit once a naming/scoping design is settled.
+* *Set-delimiters* shipped MinBars-only ([ADR-015](/adr/adr-0015-set-delimiters/) +
+  2026-06-04 scope narrowing); the dialect ladder deliberately excludes them. A future
+  cross-dialect demand reopens that ADR rather than the shape-gate axis.
+* *A third grammar seam*, if one is ever proposed, triggers a review of axis A rather than a quiet
+  addition (ADR-004 Watch).
+
+## Concrete suggestions for improvement
+
+. *Land the four rating-5 doc fixes* (axes naming, superset≠isolation wording, the checklist, the
+  cross-links) — they are corrections, and the set is quotably ambiguous without them.
+. *Add the engine-conformance checklist to [host-api](/engine/host-api/)*: escape fn · stringify · truthiness
+  default · raw-output safety stance · admitted sigil set · real-AST shape (or "none").
+. *Add two regression tests*: (a) `parse` yields the same `Sep` shape for `else` and `user` (ADR-001's
+  crown jewel); (b) RawBars' dependency closure excludes `fullbars` (ADR-003/005's isolation claim).
+. *Implement the recursion guard as ADR-007 P0* and immediately point the reference `partialH` at it,
+  closing the unbounded-recursion gap that exists *today* regardless of MinBars.
+. *Promote the loop-variable shadow check to warn-always* with the schema-present error retained.
+. *Add an ADR index page* (this nav group) so the set is navigable and new ADRs have an obvious home.
+. *Fix the RawBars module docstring* to say "the reference engine" rather than "the FullBars reference
+  engine," matching ADR-008/009's split term and ADR-008's own *Con*.

Two phases: a skeleton, then a walk + +The core is a *parser*. Its entire output is a *skeleton AST* — a uniform tree of `Content`, +`Output`, and `Block` nodes ([evaluation](/spec/evaluation/)). The parser attaches *no meaning*: it does not +know what any identifier does, does not know which identifiers are "helpers," does not know `else`, +and performs no checks beyond "is this well-formed structure." + +Meaning is a *second pass*: a *walk* over the skeleton, supplied by the engine you build. The walk +validates the tree against the engine's rules and interprets it — precisely the relationship +between a JSON document and a JSON Schema. FlatBars defines the tree and the walking contract; the +engine defines the schema and the interpreter. + +Everything below describes the interpretation of the reference engine, *FullBars*. A different engine may choose +differently; the core does not care. + +## 1. Everything is an operation + +A template is a sequence of *content* and *outputs*. An output evaluates one expression and writes +its value. The only compound expression is an *operation* — an *application* of a name. (At the host +API this same thing is called a *helper*, the term Handlebars uses; the [glossary](/concepts/#glossary) +pairs the native words with that synonym, and [host-api](/engine/host-api/) keeps it.) + +```text +{{{city}}} <1> +{{{lookup this "city"}}} <2> +{{{upcase (lookup this "name")}}} <3> +``` +<1> Calls the operation `city` with no arguments. Not a variable, not `this.city`. +<2> Reads the `city` field of the current context, by calling the operations `lookup` and `this`. +<3> `upcase` applied to one argument — the grouped sub-application `(lookup this "name")`. + +There are *no variables*. The parser sees `city` as an identifier at the head of an application; the +engine resolves it in the *environment* and invokes it. And there is no logic-less core for an operation +to be an *escape hatch from* — application *is* the language — so an operation is not a "helper" in the +subordinate, auxiliary sense the word carries elsewhere; it is the primary thing. + +## 2. Application is juxtaposition; parentheses are grouping + +`head arg1 arg2` applies. Parentheses do not mean "call"; they *group* a multi-token application so +it fits a single argument slot. A whole top-level expression therefore needs *no* parentheses: + +```text +{{{lookup this "age"}}} top-level application — no parens +{{{upcase (lookup this "name")}}} upcase of ONE argument (the group) +{{{upcase lookup this "name"}}} WRONG: upcase applied to THREE arguments +``` + +This is the Handlebars subexpression model (and ML/Haskell-style application), *not* Lisp prefix +notation where every call is parenthesized. The only parentheses you ever write group a nested +application that sits in argument position. + +## 3. The head of an application is always a name + +The operator position holds an *identifier*, never a computed value. Nothing in the language +produces a callable value, so nothing else can sit there. This is enforced syntactically for blocks +(the closing `{{/name}}` must repeat the name) and is what keeps a `Value` free of functions +([evaluation](/spec/evaluation/)). Higher-order use goes through a helper such as `apply`. + +## 4. Scope is helpers, installed by blocks + +Because a bare name is a helper call, *scoped state is just scoped helpers*. A block helper such as +`each` installs nullary helpers (`index`, `first`, the item context `this`, …) for the duration of +its body, then removes them. + +```text +{{#each people}} + {{{lookup this "name"}}} is number {{{index}}} <1> +{{/each}} +{{{index}}} <2> +``` +<1> Inside the block, `index` and `this` resolve — `each` installed them. +<2> Outside, `index` is undefined; resolving it is a validation error in the engine walk. + +This replaces Handlebars' `@index`/`@parent`/context-stack with ordinary lexical scoping over the helper +environment. There is no `@` namespace and no `../` operator in the core. + +## 5. No keywords — not even `else` + +The core reserves *nothing*. `true`, `false`, `null` are not literals; they are reference-engine +helpers `(true)`, `(false)`, `(null)`. HTML escaping is the helper `escapeHtml`; the core never +escapes. And *`else` is not special*: + +:::note[Important] +The *word* `else` never reaches the lexer or the parser. Branching is written with a *separator* — +the bare double-stash `{{ name args }}` — which the core keeps as a meaningless marker: + +[source,text] +``` +{{#if cond}} + yes + {{else}} <1> + no +{{/if}} +``` +<1> The lexer recognizes the double-stash *shape* and the parser emits `Sep "else" []` — a flat +marker sitting in `if`'s body. It assigns `else` no meaning. The reference `if` helper splits its +body at that separator ([evaluation](/spec/evaluation/)). The name is the engine's choice — `else`, `el`, +`elif`, `otherwise`, `case`, `default`; the core never singles any of them out. No sugar in the core + +If a construct can be explained as a rewrite to a smaller one, it does not belong in the core; it +belongs in the [surface dialect](/engine/surface/). `{{name}}` (escaped), `a.b.c`, `@index`, +`../x`, `as \|x\|`, and `{{> p}}` are *all* surface sugar. + +## 7. One parser, four languages + +Because the parser attaches no meaning, the *same* lexer and structural tree serve languages with +incompatible semantics — the dialect supplies the meaning through the `parseExpr` / `parseHead` seam +and the shape gates, never a fork of the grammar: + +* *RawBars* — the desugared core surface: the core skeleton syntax written out directly + (`{{{ lookup this "x" }}}`). RawBars is that core exposed; MaxBars is +FlatBars's own maximal language on top. The normative contract for all four is this spec, not any one +dialect. + +## 8. One compiler, too + +The same generalization carries to compilation ([ADR-011](/adr/adr-0011-compile-to-js/)): there is +*not* a per-dialect compiler. A single meaning-free *emit driver* (`FlatBars.Compile`) walks the lowered +core AST and calls into a pluggable `Emit` record — the fourth instance of the IoC pattern, alongside +interpret, desugar, and validate. That is a deliberate factoring — folding Mustache +semantics into the kernel `Emit` would add code and drift, not remove it — not a gap. + + + +## Glossary + +The native-dialect names for the model above. The host API ([host-api](/engine/host-api/)) keeps Handlebars' own word +*helper* for the same machinery, so a migrator's vocabulary still works; the table pairs each native term +with that synonym. + +| Native term | Meaning | Host-API synonym | +| --- | --- | --- | +| *operation* | What a name invokes at a call site — the only compound expression (§1). Either *inline* or *block*. | helper | +| *definition* | What a name resolves to in the environment; what a block or the host *installs*. A *nullary* definition is how a *value* appears — there are no variables, so a value is just an operation that takes no arguments. | (registered) helper / partial | +| *scope* | The set of definitions in force at a point. Not a separate mechanism, and not a "function": nothing produces a callable value (§3). | — | + +The lambda-vs-helper split of the Handlebars/Mustache family does *not* survive here. Mustache (logic-less, no +helpers) binds a *lambda* in the data, at a leaf; Handlebars registers a *helper* on the side — a binding-site +distinction across two languages. FlatBars has one binding site, the environment: a lambda bound to a data +leaf is a *nullary operation installed in scope*, and a "helper applied to a block" is a *block operation*. +One axis, not two. + +## A note on naming + +The mark is a set of *bare rods*: the Handlebars braces stripped to their vertical strokes. The triple +stash `{{{ }}}` — the core's one and only inline output form — is the logo's source.

+---
+title: "Header directives (`@trim`) and the truthiness model"
+---
+
+A *directive* is a `@key`/`@key: value` marker carried in a short `{{! … }}`
+comment at the **head** of a file. The core lifts directives meaning-free (the
+`Sep` precedent applied to comments — [grammar](/spec/grammar/)); the engine assigns
+meaning. Because carriage lives in the core parser, every dialect (RawBars,
+FullBars, MaxBars) inherits directives uniformly.
+
+## The mechanism
+
+```handlebars
+{{! @trim: none }}
+Hello {{ name }}!
+```
+
+Rules ([lexical](/spec/lexical/)):
+
+* Directives live **only** in short `{{! … }}` comments. A long
+  `{{!-- … --}}` comment is inert prose — so JSDoc `@param`, e-mail
+  handles, etc. are safe by construction.
+* The parser keys on `@<key>` heads (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*`); a value runs to
+  the next head or the block end, trimmed. A bare `@key` (no colon) is a flag
+  (`= @key:true`). Layout is free; canonical style is one `@key:value` per line.
+* **Header-only.** Directives are recognised before the first non-comment tag.
+  Leading content/whitespace does not close the header — only a real tag does. A
+  directive after that point is a `DirectiveAfterHeader` parse error.
+* Unknown keys are **carried but lint-warned** (forward compatibility), not an
+  error.
+
+## Truthiness — a fixed per-engine rule (ADR-022)
+
+:::note[Important]
+*The per-file `{{! @truthiness: … }}` directive was removed* — see
+[ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/). Truthiness is now each engine's *one fixed rule*: **FullBars**
+uses `handlebars` (Handlebars fidelity), **RawBars** and **MaxBars** use `nonEmpty`, **MinBars** uses
+`mustache`. (The dialects therefore *diverge* in value policy — RawBars/MaxBars are not Handlebars clones.)
+There is no per-file override, no per-partial scoping, and no alias/shape-list value to write. A leftover
+`@truthiness` directive in an old template is *inert* — carried, never an error, but **lint-warned as
+deprecated** so a stale directive does not silently mislead. The model below describes those fixed rules
+and how to write *portable* templates; the analyse mode (ADR-022 Part B) checks portability against real
+data.
+:::
+
+Each engine's rule decides which value *shapes* `if`/`unless`/`and`/`or`/`not` (and MaxBars' `&&`/`||`/`!`)
+treat as false. The named rules — the menu engines are built from — are:
+
+| Rule | Falsy set | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `handlebars` | `false null "" 0 []` | *FullBars*; `{}` truthy, `"0"` truthy |
+| `nonEmpty` | `false null "" [] {}` | *RawBars/MaxBars*; truthy ⟺ non-empty present value — `0` truthy (use `val > 0`), every empty container falsy |
+| `mustache` | `false null []` | *MinBars*; `0`/`""`/`{}` truthy |
+| `minimal` | `false null` | comparison only (analyse): only `false`/`null` false |
+| `presence` | `false null [] {}` | comparison only (analyse): present ⇒ truthy; matches *StringTemplate4* (see below) |
+
+Decisions worth stating: `"0"` is truthy under every rule; `0` is falsy only under `handlebars`; `{}`
+is falsy under `nonEmpty`/`presence`; `""` is falsy under `handlebars`/`nonEmpty`; `NaN` is always truthy;
+`safe ""` is falsy iff `""` is in the rule (content-based — [fullbars-compat](/engine/fullbars-compat/) §1.4).
+
+`includeZero` on a single `if`/`unless` makes the number `0` truthy *for that one test* — genuine
+Handlebars compat, but a Handlebars-only escape hatch (not portable). It is a per-call helper option, no
+longer tied to any falsy-set machinery.
+
+### Where other engines sit
+
+Each named rule is some real engine's rule — which is why they are the useful targets for a *portable*
+template, and the set the analyse mode replays to detect divergence.
+
+| Engine | Falsy set | FlatBars rule |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Handlebars (default) | `false null "" 0 []` | `handlebars` |
+| Mustache | `false null []` | `mustache` |
+| Ruby / Lua / Lisp `nil` | `false null` | `minimal` |
+| *StringTemplate4* | `false null [] {}` | `presence` |
+
+*StringTemplate4* (Parr's ST4) tests a conditional with `Interpreter.testAttributeTrue`:
+`null` and `Boolean false` are false; an empty `Collection`/`Map`/`Iterator` is
+false; **every other non-null object — including `""` and `0` — is true**
+("it's present"). That is exactly `presence`. ST4 thus disagrees with Handlebars on
+`""`/`0` (truthy in ST4, falsy in Handlebars) and with Mustache on `{}`
+(falsy in ST4, truthy in Mustache).
+
+### The portable core
+
+Reading the table by *shape* rather than by engine isolates what is safe to lean
+on across engines:
+
+* **Always falsy** (every rule): `false`, `null`.
+* **Always truthy** (every rule): a non-empty string, a non-zero number, a
+  non-empty array, a non-empty object, and `NaN`.
+* **Engine-dependent — the ambiguous four:** `""`, `0`, `[]`,
+  `{}`. No two of the mainstream engines agree on all four (`""`/`0`:
+  falsy in Handlebars, truthy elsewhere; `[]`: falsy everywhere except
+  `minimal`; `{}`: falsy only in `presence`/ST4).
+
+A template that must render identically under more than one engine should
+therefore **never put one of the ambiguous four in a boolean position.** Branch
+on them *explicitly* instead — `{{#each xs}}…{{else}}…{{/each}}` for a
+"non-empty list" (it renders `else` on empty on every engine), an explicit
+`{{#if (eq s "")}}` for "blank" — so the decision no longer rides on the
+host's truthiness rule. FlatBars cannot prove this statically (it has no value
+types — a name's runtime shape is unknown at parse time), so the guarantee is
+checked *against real data* by the analyse mode
+([ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/)): `pass:[flatbars analyse <template>
+<data.json>]` reports every condition that would branch differently on another
+engine, with a fix each, and `--emit-jsonata` emits a reviewable data-cleanup
+scaffold.
+
+## `@trim` — standalone whitespace (core, syntactic)
+
+`@trim: standalone | none` toggles Handlebars-style standalone-line trimming: a
+line holding only a block open/close or a comment has its indentation and
+trailing newline removed. **On by default.** This is the one directive the *core*
+itself acts on, because whitespace is syntactic (the core already owns `~`).
+
+Output tags (`{{ }}` / `{{{ }}}`) and bare `{{else}}`
+separators are never standalone-trimmed. Explicit `~` composes on top.
+
+Precedence (highest first): the `@trim` directive, the CLI `--trim standalone|none`,
+a `flatbars.json` `{ "trim": "standalone" | "none" }` in the working
+directory, then the built-in default (on).
+
+## Compilation
+
+Both interpreter and compiler honour `@trim` identically. Truthiness is a
+*callback* in both: the compiled module seeds its root frame with the engine's
+truthiness callback — `rt.truthyHandlebars` (FullBars), `rt.truthyNonEmpty`
+(RawBars/MaxBars), or `rt.truthyMustache` (MinBars) — so a compiled template
+branches under the same rule as the interpreter, asserted byte-for-byte by the
+conformance harness ([ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/)).

+---
+title: 6. The reference engine (prelude)
+sidebar:
+  label: 6. The reference engine
+---
+
+import HelperCatalog from "../../../partials/helper-catalog.mdx";
+
+The *reference engine*, *FullBars*, is a Phase-2 walk ([evaluation](/spec/evaluation/)) plus a set of helpers that,
+together with the [surface dialect](/engine/surface/), reproduces Handlebars.js. *None of it is in the core.*
+It is a library you register into the helper environment. Delete `each` and `{{#each}}` stops
+validating; the core is unaffected. Rename `escapeHtml` and update your Surface. This is what "no
+built-in helpers, no keywords" buys you.
+
+Helper signatures use the shapes from [evaluation](/spec/evaluation/): a helper is `Ctl m env -> Array Value
+-> m Value`; a block helper uses the control handle's `children`/`clause`/`render` and may split its
+`children` at a `{{name}}` separator via `splitClause`.
+
+## 6.1 Context and access
+
+| Helper | Arity | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `this` | 0 | Returns the current `context`. |
+| `root` | 0 | Returns the top-level context. Installed by the host at the outermost frame. |
+| `parent` | 0 or 1 | `(parent)` returns the enclosing block's context; `(parent (parent))` walks two levels. Installed by block helpers that shift context. |
+| `lookup` | ≥1 | `(lookup obj k1 k2 …)` indexes `obj` by each segment (string key or numeric index), returning `VNull` at the first miss. `(lookup obj)` is `obj`. |
+| `true` `false` `null` | 0 | The literal values `VBool true`, `VBool false`, `VNull`. |
+
+## 6.2 Output and safety
+
+| Helper | Arity | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `escapeHtml` | 1 | HTML-escapes the stringified argument (`&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`) and returns a `VSafe`. Idempotent on `VSafe` input. |
+| `safe` | 1 | Marks the stringified argument as `VSafe` *without* escaping — the explicit "trust this markup" helper. The analogue of `new Handlebars.SafeString(…)`. |
+| `json` | 1–2 | Serializes the first argument as JSON *text*, returned as a plain `VString` — so surface `{{ json x }}` HTML-escapes it and `{{{ json x }}}` emits it raw (e.g. inline `<script>` data). Objects/arrays are first-class; integral numbers print without a trailing `.0`; object keys come out in key order. Compact by default; an optional options object opts into two-space pretty-printing — `{{ json x pretty=true }}` (empty objects/arrays stay inline). |
+| `escapeJson` | 1–2 | The JSON analogue of `escapeHtml`: serializes to JSON *and* HTML-escapes, returning `VSafe`. For embedding JSON safely in HTML (e.g. an attribute). `escapeHtml` is idempotent on the result, so surface escaping never doubles up. Accepts the same `pretty=true` option. |
+| `raw` | block | A raw-block helper returning its captured body verbatim. |
+
+## 6.3 Conditionals (clause-reading block helpers)
+
+| Helper | Form | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `if` | block | `splitClauses` over its body: renders the nodes before the first separator when the argument is truthy; otherwise walks the `{{elif cond}}` clauses in order, rendering the first whose `cond` is truthy (evaluated lazily via `Ctl.eval`, so later conditions short-circuit), and falls back to a terminal `{{else}}`. |
+| `elif` | 1 | A *separator* the enclosing `if` interprets — `{{#if a}}…{{elif b}}…{{/if}}`. Rendered standalone it is inert (returns `""`), exactly like `else`. |
+| `unless` | block | The inverse of `if` (a single `{{else}}`, no `elif`). |
+
+`if`, `elif`, and `unless` *define* the meaning of nested `{{else}}…` / `{{elif}}…`;
+the core does not — they are ordinary separators. `if` rejects a malformed chain up front (a clause
+other than `elif`/`else`, or anything after `else`) as a `ClauseError`, so the error never depends on
+which branch the data takes.
+*Truthiness* is the *engine's* rule (a `Value -> Boolean` callback the conditionals test through;
+[ADR-022](/adr/adr-0022-analyse-mode/)), so it depends on the dialect: **FullBars** uses `handlebars`
+(`false`/`null`/`0`/`""`/`[]` falsy; `{}` and non-zero/non-empty truthy), **RawBars/MaxBars** use
+`nonEmpty` (`false`/`null`/`""`/`[]`/`{}` falsy — `0` truthy), **MinBars** uses `mustache`. The
+`includeZero` option makes the number `0` truthy for one `if`/`unless` test — `pass:[{{#if n (dict
+"includeZero" true)}}]` — which matters under `handlebars` (a no-op under `nonEmpty`, where `0` is
+already truthy).
+
+## 6.4 Iteration and context shift
+
+| Helper | Form | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `each` | block | Iterates an array or object. Per element it pushes a frame, sets `context` to the element, and installs scoped helpers `index` (0-based), `key`, `first`, `last`, `parent`. Optional binding-name arguments rename the element and index. On an *empty* collection it renders the `else` clause (via `splitClause "else"`). |
+| `with` | block | Pushes a frame, sets `context` to its argument, installs `parent`, renders the body. On a falsy/absent argument it renders the `else` clause. An optional binding-name argument also installs the shifted context under that name. |
+
+Scoped helpers installed by `each`:
+
+| Helper | Value inside the body |
+| --- | --- |
+| `this` | the current element |
+| `index` | 0-based position (number) |
+| `key` | property name (objects) or numeric index as string (arrays) |
+| `first` / `last` | `VBool` — first / last element? |
+| `parent` | the collection's enclosing context |
+| `parent-index` / `parent-key` / `parent-first` / `parent-last` | the *enclosing* loop's `index`/`key`/`first`/`last` — the target of surface `{{@../index}}` etc. (one `../` level). Installed by `each`/`with` only when an enclosing loop provided them. |
+
+## 6.5 Composition / data helpers
+
+| Helper | Arity | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `dict` | even ≥0 | `(dict "k1" v1 …)` builds a `VObject`. Target of the hash desugaring (5.4). |
+| `apply` | ≥1 | `(apply name args…)` — the higher-order escape hatch: `name` is a `VString` naming a helper, applied to the remaining arguments. How a "helper held in data" is called, since values are never functions. |
+| `log` | ≥1 | Emits its arguments to the host log (an effect in `M`) and returns `VNull`. |
+
+## 6.6 Partials
+
+| Helper | Form | Behaviour |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `partial` | 2–3 | `(partial name ctx hash?)` renders the registered partial `name` with `context = ctx`, the optional `hash` object merged onto it. *As a block* (`{{#partial name}}body{{/partial}}`) the body is the fallback (rendered if `name` is unregistered) and is exposed inside the partial as the scoped `partial-block` helper. Returns `VSafe`. |
+| `inline` | block | `{{#inline "name"}}body{{/inline}}` defines a partial named `name`. Definitions are *hoisted* into the registry before rendering (`FullBars.Surface.hoistInline`) and are global to the render; the block itself emits `""`. |
+| `partial-block` | 0 | Scoped helper installed by a *block* `partial`; returns the enclosing block body. Target of `{{> @partial-block}}`. |
+
+## 6.7 A minimal engine is enough
+
+You do not need all of the above. A static-site author might register only `this`, `lookup`,
+`escapeHtml`, `if`, and `each`; a configuration templater only `lookup`, `eq`, and `or`. The engine —
+the helpers *and* the clause vocabulary they read — is the product surface you design. The core never
+presumes which of these exist.
+
+## 6.8 Helper catalog (generated)
+
+The table below is *generated* from `FullBars.preludeSchema` — the same single source the validator
+uses (`FullBars.Catalog.helperCatalogAdoc`; regenerate with `npm run gen:catalog`, checked in CI by
+`npm run check:catalog`). It is the authoritative list of names, arities, block-ness, and one-line
+*descriptions*; each description is the operation's own `doc` (the same string the editor shows on
+hover), so it never drifts from the engine — the prose sections above remain the long-form reference.
+*Source* is `registered` for helpers with a runtime in `prelude` and `scoped` for variables a block
+helper installs (`root`/`parent`/`index`/`key`/`first`/`last`/`partial-block`).
+

+the one structural parser (`parse`) is unchanged, and Surface is a *desugaring walk* over the
+structural AST — part of the second pass ([host-api](/engine/host-api/) §7.1), naturally a `foldTemplate`
+([A.13.2](/appendix/handlebars/#engine-api)). `FullBars.Surface.desugar` performs the surface
+rewrites below (output and paths today; see the status note); it is distinct from
+`FullBars.Lower.lower`, which lowers the *core* skeleton to the engine's typed real AST for tooling.
+You can run the desugarer, swap it, or write your own.
+
+Surface adds nothing the core cannot already express. Every rule below is a *rewrite* of one
+structural node into core nodes. Where a rewrite names a helper (`escapeHtml`, `lookup`, `dict`,
+`partial`, …), that helper must exist in the [engine](/engine/prelude/).
+
+:::note
+*Implementation status.* `FullBars.Surface.desugar` (and the convenience
+`renderSurface` / `compileSurface`) implement §5.1 *output* (`{{ }}` ⇒
+escaped, `{{{ }}}` ⇒ raw), §5.2 *paths* (bare, dotted, numeric index,
+legacy slash, `this`/`.`, `../`), §5.3 *literals* and head-vs-argument, §5.5
+*`@data`* variables (`@index`, `@root.x`, …), and the §5.6 *`else if`* chain. The
+reference renderer still runs *core* syntax by default (`renderWith`); call
+`renderSurface` to author in the dialect. §5.2 paths include `[bracket]`
+segments (`a.[home town]`, `a.[1]` — dots and spaces inside the brackets are
+literal). *Partials* (§5.7) work via `renderSurfaceWith`: `{{> name}}`,
+`{{> name ctx}}`, dynamic `{{> (expr)}}`, and hash context
+`{{> name k=v}}` (the hash merges onto the partial's context) render a
+registered partial (unescaped). *Block partials* `{{#partial name}}body{{/partial}}`
+render the partial with `body` as the fallback (if missing) and the
+`{{> @partial-block}}` yield point; *inline partials*
+`{{#*inline "name"}}body{{/inline}}` (the Handlebars decorator form,
+with the `*` sigil) define a partial, hoisted into the
+registry before rendering. The bare `{{#inline "name"}}` is *rejected*
+(`DisallowedShape`): in FullBars, as in Handlebars, `inline` is a decorator, not
+a block helper. *Hash arguments* (§5.4) collect into a trailing `dict`:
+`{{ f a k=v k2="s"}}` ⇒ `{{{ escapeHtml (f (lookup this "a") (dict "k" … "k2" "s")) }}}`
+— this is what feeds `if`/`unless`' `includeZero`, e.g. `{{#if n includeZero=true}}`.
+*Block params* (§5.5) work too: `{{#each xs as \|item i\|}}` binds `item`/`i` as scoped
+helpers (the index/key), and `{{#with o as \|x\|}}` binds the context — a bare reference to an
+in-scope param desugars to a `(param)` call (lexically scoped, visible in nested blocks).
+
+*`@../` parent-data* is desugared for one `../` level: `{{@../index}}`
+(and `@../key`/`@../first`/`@../last`) reads the *enclosing* loop's datum via the
+`parent-index`/`…` scoped helpers that `each`/`with` install (the data analogue
+of `parent` for context). A deeper run (`@../../index`) still resolves to the
+immediate parent.
+
+The Handlebars block-partial *sigil* `{{#> name}}…{{/name}}` is also
+accepted and desugars to the same core form as the `{{#partial}}`
+spelling; the inline-partial *decorator* `{{#*inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}`
+is the *required* FullBars author form and desugars internally to the core
+`inline` helper. The core lexes `{{#>` and `{{#*` as the distinct
+`PartialBlock` and `Decorator` sigils — each with a clean head (the partial name
+for `{{#>}}`, the decorator name `inline` for `{{#*inline}}`) and a
+`{{/…}}` close that simply repeats that head. They are opt-in via
+`ParseOptions.partialBlocks` / `decorators` (on for FullBars; the austere dialects
+gate them off as a located `DisallowedShape`). The bare
+`{{#inline}}` is rejected by `FullBars.checkBareInline` with a located
+`DisallowedShape` error — this gate is FullBars-surface-only (RawBars and MaxBars
+still accept bare `{{#inline}}`). See the
+[compatibility matrix](/engine/fullbars-compat/) for per-feature status.
+:::
+
+:::note[Important]
+*Parenthesis convention.* A top-level expression inside `{{{ }}}` needs no grouping — it is
+already one `Expr`. Parentheses appear only around a *nested* application in argument position. So
+the desugaring of `{{ name }}` is `{{{ escapeHtml (lookup this "name") }}}` — `escapeHtml`
+is the top-level operator (no wrapper), and `(lookup this "name")` is parenthesized because it is an
+argument.
+:::
+
+## 5.1 Output: `{{ }}` and `{{{ }}}`
+
+| Surface | Core |
+| --- | --- |
+| `{{ E }}` | `{{{ escapeHtml E' }}}` |
+| `{{{ E }}}` | `{{{ E' }}}` |
+
+Handlebars' ampersand form `{{& E }}` (unescaped) is accepted as an alias of the triple-stash
+`{{{ E }}}` (see §5.6) — both mean "do not escape". The triple-stash is the canonical FullBars
+spelling; the austere RawBars and MaxBars dialects accept only it and reject `{{&}}`.
+
+`E'` is `E` after the *path rewrite* (5.2). If `E'` is itself a multi-token application it is wrapped
+in parentheses before being handed to `escapeHtml` (it is now an argument): `{{ upcase x }}` →
+`{{{ escapeHtml (upcase (lookup this "x")) }}}`.
+
+## 5.2 Paths become `lookup`
+
+| Surface path | Core |
+| --- | --- |
+| `name` | `(lookup this "name")` |
+| `a.b.c` | `(lookup this "a" "b" "c")` |
+| `a.1` or `a.[1]` | `(lookup this "a" 1)` |
+| `a.[home town]` | `(lookup this "a" "home town")` |
+| `a/b` (legacy slash) | `(lookup this "a" "b")` |
+| `this` or `.` | `this` |
+| `this.a` or `./a` | `(lookup this "a")` |
+| `../a` | `(lookup (parent) "a")` |
+| `../../a` | `(lookup (parent (parent)) "a")` |
+| `@x` | `(x)`  (a scoped data helper — 5.5) |
+| `@../x` | `(parent-x)`  (the enclosing loop's datum — 5.5) |
+
+(The right-hand forms are shown parenthesized because in Surface a path almost always lands in
+*argument* position — e.g. as the argument of `escapeHtml`. When a path is the whole top-level
+expression, e.g. `{{{ name }}}`, the desugaring is the unwrapped `{{{ lookup this "name" }}}`.)
+
+`lookup` is *variadic*: it walks segments left to right, indexing objects by string key and arrays by
+number, returning `VNull` at the first miss. `parent` is a scoped helper that block helpers install
+to expose the enclosing context (5.5); it replaces Handlebars' implicit context stack with an explicit,
+named one.
+
+:::note
+A bare path `name` resolves to a *data field* (`lookup this "name"`), never to a helper, because
+Surface always wraps it. This is the opposite of the core, where `{{{name}}}` *calls* the
+helper `name`. The two layers read the same text differently on purpose: Surface is for authors who
+think in data; the core is for the desugarer and the engine.
+:::
+
+## 5.3 Helper calls, literals, and subexpressions
+
+Anything that is not a bare path is a helper call, exactly as in the core, with two literal
+conveniences:
+
+| Surface | Core |
+| --- | --- |
+| `true` / `false` / `null` | `(true)` / `(false)` / `(null)` |
+| `(helper a b)` | unchanged — grouping is already core |
+| `helper a b` (tag head) | unchanged — application is already core |
+
+In *head* position a bare identifier is a helper; in *argument* position a bare identifier that is
+not a registered literal is a path. So `{{upcase name}}` →
+`{{{ escapeHtml (upcase (lookup this "name")) }}}`.
+
+## 5.4 Hash arguments become a trailing `dict`
+
+| Surface | Core |
+| --- | --- |
+| `{{helper a k1=v1 k2=v2}}` | `{{{ escapeHtml (helper a (dict "k1" v1 "k2" v2)) }}}` |
+| `{{#helper a k=v}}…{{/helper}}` | `{{#helper a (dict "k" v)}}…{{/helper}}` |
+
+All `key=value` pairs collapse into a single `dict` value appended *after* the positional arguments —
+the equivalent of Handlebars' `options.hash`.
+
+## 5.5 `@data` and block params become scoped helpers
+
+`each` and `with` install scoped helpers for the duration of their body; Surface `@`-variables are
+calls to them, and block params rename them:
+
+| Surface | Core / mechanism |
+| --- | --- |
+| `@index` `@key` `@first` `@last` | `(index)` `(key)` `(first)` `(last)` — installed by `each` |
+| `@../index` `@../key` `@../first` `@../last` | `(parent-index)` … — the *enclosing* loop's datum, installed by `each`/`with` (one `../` level) |
+| `@root` | `(root)` — installed by the host at the top frame |
+| `{{#each xs as \|item i\|}}` | `{{#each xs "item" "i"}}` — `each` also installs `item` and `i` |
+| `{{#with o as \|x\|}}` | `{{#with o "x"}}` — `with` installs `x` alongside the shifted `this` |
+
+Renaming via `as |…|` becomes positional *binding-name* arguments to the block helper.
+
+## 5.6 Branches
+
+`{{else}}` is already core — a separator ([grammar](/spec/grammar/) §2.4) — so Surface passes it
+through unchanged. Surface's only job here is the `else if` chain, which it lowers to the engine's
+flat `{{elif cond}}` separator (the condition is still path-rewritten):
+
+| Surface | Core |
+| --- | --- |
+| `{{#if c}}A{{else}}B{{/if}}` | `{{#if c}}A{{else}}B{{/if}}` |
+| `{{#each xs}}A{{else}}B{{/each}}` | `{{#each xs}}A{{else}}B{{/each}}` |
+| `{{#if a}}A{{else if b}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}` | `{{#if a}}A{{elif (lookup this "b")}}B{{else}}C{{/if}}` |
+
+`else`, `elif`, and `unless` are *engine* names ([prelude](/engine/prelude/) §6.3). A different engine could
+read a clause named `otherwise` or provide `case`/`default`; Surface simply targets whatever the
+engine defines. (Authoring `{{elif b}}` directly in Surface also works — it is a clause
+separator like `{{else}}`.)
+
+FullBars supports Mustache's inverted section `{{^x}}…{{/x}}` (and the triple variant
+`{{{^x}}}…{{{/x}}}`), desugaring it to `{{#unless x}}…{{/unless}}` — so "render when
+falsy" reads the way Handlebars authors expect. You may always write the `unless` helper explicitly
+instead. (The austere RawBars and MaxBars dialects do *not* accept `{{^}}` — there you write
+`unless`.) Unescaped output also has the `{{&x}}` alias for `{{{x}}}`.
+
+## 5.7 Partials become `partial` / `inline`
+
+| Surface | Core |
+| --- | --- |
+| `{{> name}}` | `{{{ partial "name" this }}}` |
+| `{{> name ctx}}` | `{{{ partial "name" ctx' }}}` |
+| `{{> name k=v}}` | `{{{ partial "name" this (dict "k" v) }}}` |
+| `{{> name ctx k=v}}` | `{{{ partial "name" ctx' (dict "k" v) }}}` |
+| `{{> (expr)}}` (dynamic) | `{{{ partial (expr) this }}}` |
+| `{{#partial name k=v}}body{{/partial}}` | `{{#partial "name" this (dict "k" v)}}body{{/partial}}` |
+| `{{> @partial-block}}` | `{{{ partial-block }}}` |
+| `{{#*inline "name"}}body{{/inline}}` | `{{#inline "name"}}body{{/inline}}` |
+
+Block partials are written with the *core spelling* `{{#partial}}`
+(a bare name is literalized like `{{> name}}`) *or* the equivalent
+Handlebars *sigil* `{{#> name}}…{{/name}}`. Inline partials use the
+Handlebars *decorator* `{{#*inline "name"}}…{{/inline}}`, which desugars to
+the core `inline` helper; the bare `{{#inline …}}` spelling is *rejected*
+(`DisallowedShape`) in FullBars — authors do not write `inline` bare. A block `partial`
+renders the named partial with its `body` as both the fallback (when the partial is missing) and the
+`{{> @partial-block}}` yield point; `inline` definitions are hoisted into the registry before
+rendering.
+
+Partials render *unescaped* — a partial produces markup, not a data value, so the desugaring is the
+plain triple-stash with no `escapeHtml`. The partial *name* desugars to a `STRING` literal; a dynamic
+partial keeps the computed expression. `partial`, `inline`, and the scoped `partial-block` are engine
+helpers; see [A.6](/appendix/handlebars/#partials). The scoped `partial-block` is also installed
+under the synonym `yield`, the hyphen-free spelling the non-Handlebars dialects use for the same yield
+(MaxBars `{{yield}}`, RawBars `{{{yield}}}`; see [maxbars](/engine/maxbars/)).
+
+## 5.8 What Surface does *not* change
+
+Comments, raw blocks, whitespace `~`, and brace-escaping are *core* features and pass through
+untouched.

+---
+title: "4. Validation & errors"
+---
+
+Errors fall in two phases. *Structural* errors come from the core parser: the bytes are not a
+well-formed skeleton. *Validation* errors come from the engine walk: the skeleton is well-formed but
+violates the engine's schema (an unknown helper, a bad arity, an illegal clause). The split mirrors
+"is this valid JSON?" versus "does this JSON satisfy the schema?".
+
+## 4.1 Structural (parse) errors — raised by the core
+
+| Error | Cause |
+| --- | --- |
+| `UnterminatedTag` | an opener with no matching closer before end of input |
+| `UnterminatedComment` | `{{!--` with no `--}}` |
+| `UnterminatedRaw` | `{{{{#name}}}}` with no `{{{{/name}}}}` |
+| `MismatchedBlock` | `{{/a}}` closing a `{{#b}}` |
+| `HeadNotIdent` | a group or literal in *head* position — a block/close/separator head must be an `Ident` (e.g. `{{#42}}`). A bare literal in *output* position, `{{42}}`, is allowed (it emits like `{{{42}}}`). |
+| `EmptyOutput` | `{{{}}}` with no expression |
+| `BadEscape` | an invalid string escape inside a `STRING` |
+
+Note what is *absent*: there is no `MultipleElse` or `ElseOutsideBlock`, because the core has no
+`else`. `{{else}}…` is just a block; if it appears where the engine does not expect
+a clause, that is a *validation* error (4.2), not a parse error. Every structural error carries a
+source offset (`parseErrorOffset`) pointing at the offending tag — an unclosed/mismatched block
+points at its *opener*. Given the source, `parseErrorAt src pe` returns the 1-based
+`{ line, column, offset, message }` (via `Span.lineColumn`), and `renderParseErrorAt src pe` formats
+it as `line:column: message` for a host to print.
+
+## 4.2 Validation errors — raised by the engine walk
+
+| Error | Cause |
+| --- | --- |
+| `UnknownHelper name` | `name` is not defined in any helper frame |
+| `ArityError` | a helper received the wrong number of arguments |
+| `TypeError` | a helper received an argument of the wrong shape |
+| `ClauseError` | a block contains a separator the helper does not accept, or in an illegal order |
+| `HelperError` | any other failure a helper chooses to raise |
+
+These are the engine's "schema" being enforced. A conforming engine MAY run this validation as a
+*separate up-front pass* over the whole `Template` (rejecting a template before any output, the way
+a schema validator rejects a document) or *lazily* during rendering. The reference engine, *FullBars*, validates
+lazily; a stricter engine can fold the same checks into a visitor that walks the AST once and
+reports every violation with its source span.
+
+:::note
+There is no "missing variable" error, because there are no variables. Reading an absent *data field*
+(`{{{lookup this "nope"}}}`) is *not* an error in the reference engine — `lookup` returns
+`VNull`, which stringifies to the empty string, matching Handlebars. A strict engine may install a
+`lookup` that raises instead ([A.9](/appendix/handlebars/#options)).
+:::
+
+## 4.3 Diagnostics quality
+
+Because validation is a walk over the AST, an engine SHOULD attach the originating node's source span
+to every diagnostic, so `UnknownHelper "uppcase"` points at the typo rather than at the document. The
+spans are available: every tag-level node carries one, and during rendering the control handle
+exposes it as `ctl.span` ([evaluation](/spec/evaluation/) §3.6) — so a helper that raises `HelperError` can
+quote `spanText`/`lineColumn` of the very tag it was called from. Implementing Phase 2 as an explicit
+visitor (rather than inlined into rendering) makes this — and whole-template linting —
+straightforward.

+---
+title: "3. The skeleton AST & the walk"
+sidebar:
+  label: "3. AST & the walk"
+---
+
+Phase 1 (the core) produces the *skeleton AST* defined here. Phase 2 (an engine you supply) *walks*
+it to validate and render. This chapter gives the AST and the value type normatively, then specifies
+the *walk contract* the reference engine, *FullBars*, implements.
+
+## 3.1 The skeleton AST (normative)
+
+```haskell
+type Template = Array Node
+type Span     = { start :: Int, end :: Int }   -- code-unit offsets of the opening tag
+
+data Node
+  = Content  String
+  | Output   Span Expr                       -- span, expression
+  | Block    Span Ident (Array Expr) Template -- span, head, args, body (one sub-tree)
+  | RawBlock Span Ident (Array Expr) String   -- span, head, args, verbatim body
+  | Sep      Span Ident (Array Expr)          -- span, head, args (a separator marker)
+
+data Expr
+  = Lit Value          -- only Str / Num arrive from the parser
+  | App Ident (Array Expr)
+```
+
+Every tag-level node carries the source `Span` of its opening tag, for diagnostics; `Content` does
+not (it is literal text). `Span.lineColumn` turns an offset into a 1-based line/column.
+
+There is no comment node (the lexer drops them), no inverse field on `Block` (branching uses `Sep`
+markers; [grammar](/spec/grammar/)), and no `Group` constructor — parentheses affect *parsing* only, so
+`(e)` and `e` produce the same `Expr`. *This tree carries no meaning.* `App "if" […]` and
+`Sep "else" []` are just identifiers and arguments; whether `if` exists, what it does, and whether
+`else` splits it are all Phase-2 questions.
+
+## 3.2 The value type (normative)
+
+```haskell
+data Value
+  = VString  String
+  | VNumber  Number
+  | VBool    Boolean
+  | VNull
+  | VArray   (Array Value)
+  | VObject  (Map String Value)
+  | VSafe    String          -- a string already safe to emit unescaped (see 3.6)
+```
+
+:::note[Important]
+`Value` has *no function case*. Helpers are not values; they live in the engine's environment under
+names and can never be produced, stored, or passed by the language — the direct consequence of "the
+head of an application is always a name" ([concepts](/concepts/)). Values stay serializable and
+comparable; higher-order behaviour goes through a helper such as `apply`.
+:::
+
+`VSafe` is the only non-data case and exists solely at the output boundary; see 3.6.
+
+## 3.3 The walk contract
+
+An *engine* is anything that turns a `Template` and some data into output. The contract is one
+function:
+
+```haskell
+runTemplate :: forall m env. Monad m => Engine m env -> Template -> m String
+```
+
+The driver is *polymorphic* in the result monad `m` (a pure host uses `Either Error`; an async one
+`ExceptT Error Aff`, under `MonadThrow Error m`) and in the environment type `env`. `env` is the
+engine's business; the reference engine uses a frame stack (as a newtype, `RefEnv m`, so the
+recursive `RefEnv → Helper → Ctl → RefEnv` is well-founded):
+
+```haskell
+newtype RefEnv m = RefEnv
+  { helpers :: List (Map Ident (Helper m (RefEnv m)))   -- a stack of frames; head is innermost
+  , context :: Value                                    -- what `this` returns
+  }
+```
+
+* `helpers` is a *stack of frames*. Resolution searches innermost-outward; first match wins. A block
+  helper pushes a frame for its body and pops it — the whole of "scope" ([concepts](/concepts/)).
+* `context` is the current data, reached only via `this`. `with`/`each` push a frame *and* set a new
+  `context`.
+
+## 3.4 Validation is part of the walk
+
+Before (or as) it interprets a node, the walk *validates* it against the engine's rules — exactly
+like checking a JSON document against a JSON Schema:
+
+* `App name` — is `name` a registered helper? (else `UnknownHelper`)
+* arity — did `name` get the argument count it requires? (`ArityError`)
+* argument shape — are the values the right kind? (`TypeError`)
+* block shape — are this block's separators (`else`, `case`, …) ones this helper allows, in a
+  legal arrangement? (`ClauseError`)
+
+The *core does none of this*. A conforming engine MAY validate the whole tree up front (a static
+pass, like schema validation) or lazily as it renders; the reference engine validates lazily. See
+[errors](/spec/errors/).
+
+## 3.5 The reference walk
+
+```text
+render env (Content s)            = s
+render env (Output e)             = stringify (eval env e)
+render env (Block name args body) = stringify (apply (resolve env name)
+                                                      (ctl env body)             -- Ctl handle
+                                                      [ eval env a | a <- args ])
+render env (RawBlock name args r) = stringify (apply (resolve env name)
+                                                      (ctl env [Content r])
+                                                      [ eval env a | a <- args ])
+render env (Sep name args)        = render env (Output (App name args))   -- a lone separator
+                                                                          -- is just an application
+
+eval env (Lit v)         = v
+eval env (App name args) = apply (resolve env name) (ctl env []) [ eval env a | a <- args ]
+
+-- ctl env children = { env, children, render, span, clause: \n -> splitClause n children }
+```
+
+Arguments are evaluated *eagerly, left to right*, before the helper runs. Block bodies are the
+exception: a helper receives its body *unevaluated* (as a `Template`) and decides what to do with it.
+
+## 3.6 Helpers and the control handle
+
+*FlatBars drives the whole walk — inversion of control.* It resolves and applies each helper,
+handing it a `Ctl`: a *control handle* whose fields are callbacks *into* FlatBars. A helper never
+traverses the tree itself; it asks FlatBars to render the sub-trees it chooses.
+
+```haskell
+type Ctl m env =
+  { env      :: env                          -- the current environment (the engine's type)
+  , children :: Template                     -- this block's body ([] for inline calls)
+  , span     :: Span                         -- source location of the enclosing tag
+  , eval     :: env -> Expr     -> m Value   -- FlatBars evaluates an expression for you
+  , render   :: env -> Template -> m String  -- FlatBars renders a sub-tree for you
+  , clause   :: Ident -> { before :: Template, body :: Maybe Template } }  -- split at a separator
+
+type Helper m env = Ctl m env -> Array Value -> m Value
+```
+
+An *inline* helper ignores the handle. A *block* helper uses it: it may `render` its `children` zero
+or more times, under environments it constructs (pushing scoped helpers, shifting `context`), and it
+may `clause` to split `children` at a `{{name}}` separator.
+
+```haskell
+-- if: render the body up to the {{else}} separator; render the else clause otherwise.
+ifHelper ctl [cond] =
+  let { before, body } = ctl.clause "else"
+  in if truthy cond
+       then VSafe <$> ctl.render ctl.env before
+       else VSafe <$> ctl.render ctl.env (fromMaybe [] body)
+
+-- ctl.clause "else" finds the first  Sep "else" _  in the children, returning
+-- the nodes before it and the nodes after it.
+```
+
+`each` calls `ctl.render` once per element with a per-element frame (installing `index`, `first`,
+`this`, …) and uses the same `ctl.clause "else"` for an empty-collection clause. `with` shifts
+`context`. None of this is in the core — it is the reference engine's reading of the `{{else}}`
+separator.
+
+## 3.7 Stringification, escaping, and safety
+
+`stringify` converts a `Value` to output text:
+
+| Value | Output |
+| --- | --- |
+| `VString s` / `VSafe s` | `s` |
+| `VNumber n` | the shortest round-tripping decimal of `n` |
+| `VBool b` | `"true"` / `"false"` |
+| `VNull` | the empty string |
+| `VArray` / `VObject` | host-defined; the reference host joins arrays with `","` and errors on objects |
+
+:::note[Important]
+*The core never escapes.* HTML escaping is the helper `escapeHtml`, which returns a `VSafe`. The
+`VSafe` tag makes escaping *idempotent at the boundary*: a value already escaped (or deliberately
+trusted via `safe`) is not escaped again as it flows through another helper. This is the FlatBars
+analogue of Handlebars' `SafeString`, carried in the value rather than implied by which braces you typed.
+:::
+
+## 3.8 Determinism
+
+Given the same template, context, starting frame, and pure helpers, the walk is deterministic and
+side-effect-free. Side effects (e.g. `log`) are confined to `M`.

+---
+title: 1. Lexical structure
+---
+
+This chapter defines how a template's bytes are split into *content* and *tags*, and how the pieces
+inside a tag are tokenized. The grammar in [grammar](/spec/grammar/) consumes these tokens to build the
+skeleton AST. Nothing here knows what any identifier *means*.
+
+## 1.1 Source
+
+A template is a sequence of Unicode characters; the host decodes bytes to text first. The lexer
+recognizes a small set of *tag openers* and treats everything else as literal *content*.
+
+## 1.2 Tag openers and the brace count
+
+| Opener | Closer | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `{{{` | `}}}` | *Output* — evaluate one expression, write its value. The only inline output form. |
+| `{{#` | `}}` … `{{/name}}` | *Block* — a named application that also captures one sub-template (its body). |
+| `{{#>` | `}}` … `{{/name}}` | *Partial block* — a `PartialBlock`-sigil block over a clean partial-name head. Opt-in via `ParseOptions.partialBlocks`. |
+| `{{#*` | `}}` … `{{/name}}` | *Decorator* — a `Decorator`-sigil block over a clean decorator-name head (e.g. `{{#*inline}}`). Opt-in via `ParseOptions.decorators`. |
+| `{{!` | `}}` | *Short comment* — discarded. May not contain `}}`. |
+| `{{!--` | `--}}` | *Long comment* — discarded. May contain `}}`, `{{`, and `--`. |
+| `{{{{#` | `}}}}` … `{{{{/name}}}}` | *Raw block* — body captured verbatim, never tokenized. |
+| `{{` _Ident_ `}}` |  | *Separator* — the bare double-stash `{{ name args }}`. A flat marker; the lexer reads the *shape*, never the name. |
+
+That is the entire opener set. `{{#` is the general block *opener* (`{{#>` and
+`{{#*` are its two opt-in specialisations); the bare double-stash
+`{{ … }}` is a *separator*, recognized by shape. There is deliberately no:
+
+* `{{^}}` inverse opener — "render when falsy" is the `unless` helper, not a syntax.
+* escaped-output `{{ }}` *in the core* — the double-stash is a separator here; escaping is the
+  helper `escapeHtml`. The [surface dialect](/engine/surface/) reuses `{{ E }}` for escaped
+  output, desugaring it to `{{{ escapeHtml … }}}`; the two layers read it differently.
+
+The separator's identifier — `else`, `elif`, `case`, `default` — is *opaque to the lexer and parser*
+([grammar](/spec/grammar/) §2.4). The lexer matches the *longest opener*: `{{{{` before
+`{{{` before `{{#*` / `{{#>` before `{{#` before a bare `{{`, and
+`{{!--` before `{{!`.
+
+## 1.3 Content and brace escaping
+
+Any run of characters not beginning a tag is *content*, emitted verbatim. A backslash immediately
+before a tag opener escapes it: the opener is emitted literally and the backslash is consumed.
+
+```text
+\{{{x}}}      emits the literal text {{{x}}}
+\{{x}}        emits the literal text {{x}}      (a bare {{ is a separator opener)
+\\{{{x}}}     emits a literal backslash, then evaluates {{{x}}}
+```
+
+:::note[Important]
+*`{{` is significant.* Because the bare double-stash is a separator opener (§1.2), a literal
+`{{` in content must be written `{{`. For blocks of text full of braces, a raw block
+(`{{{{#raw}}}}…{{{{/raw}}}}`, §1.7) is cleaner. This is a deliberate change from earlier
+drafts, where `{{ }}` was not part of the core at all ([ADR-001](/adr/adr-0001-structural-parser-and-walker/)).
+:::
+
+## 1.4 Whitespace control: `~`
+
+A tilde immediately inside a tag opener or before a tag closer trims *all* contiguous whitespace on
+that side of the tag, including newlines.
+
+```text
+{{{~ x ~}}}                    trims around this output
+{{~#each xs~}}…{{~/each~}}      trims around the block tags
+```
+
+`~` is resolved entirely in the lexer: it adjusts the adjacent content runs and disappears. It never
+reaches the AST, so it is not sugar — there is nothing to desugar.
+
+:::note[Important]
+FlatBars performs *no implicit "standalone" whitespace removal*. Handlebars.js silently strips the line
+around a block/partial/comment that stands alone; FlatBars does not. Whitespace is removed only where
+you write `~`. Predictable and explicit; see [A.7](/appendix/handlebars/#comments-raw-ws).
+:::
+
+## 1.5 Tokens inside a tag
+
+Within `{{{ … }}}`, `{{# … }}`, and the head of a raw block, the lexer produces:
+
+| Token | Definition | Examples |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `IDENT` | An identifier. One or more characters from `A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_`, `-`, `+`, `*`, `?`, `!`, `/`, `.`, `<`, `>`, `=` that does not parse as a `NUMBER`. Must not start with a digit, `-`+digit, `"`, `(`, `)`, or whitespace. | `each`  `escapeHtml`  `partial-block`  `>`  `eq` |
+| `STRING` | `"` … `"` or `'` … `'` with escapes `\\` `\"` `\'` `\n` `\t` `\r`. May contain spaces and any tag-like text; the lexer does not look inside strings. | `"home town"`  `'pro'` |
+| `NUMBER` | Optional `-`, decimal digits, optional fraction. No exponents in v1. | `3`  `-2.5`  `0` |
+| `LPAREN` `RPAREN` | `(` and `)` — grouping. | `(` `)` |
+| whitespace | Insignificant inside a tag (significant only via `~`). |  |
+
+The permissive `IDENT` set lets names like `>` (partial), `eq`, `+`, and `partial-block` be
+written. `.` is a legal `IDENT` character, so `a.b` lexes as a *single* identifier — the core never
+splits it. Dotted *paths* are a surface concept ([surface](/engine/surface/)).
+
+## 1.6 Comments
+
+```text
+{{! stripped, no }} allowed inside }}
+{{!-- stripped; may contain }} and {{ and -- dashes --}}
+```
+
+Both forms are discarded during lexing and never appear in the AST.
+
+## 1.7 Raw blocks
+
+```text
+{{{{#raw}}}}
+Hello {{name}} — emitted verbatim.
+{{{{/raw}}}}
+```
+
+After the `}}}}` closing the raw-block head, the lexer captures everything up to the matching
+`{{{{/IDENT}}}}` as one uninterpreted string. The closing `IDENT` must equal the opening one.
+
+## 1.8 Lexer summary (informative)
+
+```text
+CONTENT  --"\\" + opener-->  emit literal opener, stay in CONTENT
+CONTENT  --opener-->         switch to matching TAG / RAW / COMMENT state
+TAG      --"~"-->            mark trim, continue
+TAG      --tokens-->         IDENT | STRING | NUMBER | ( | )
+TAG      --closer-->         back to CONTENT (apply pending trims)
+RAW      --scan-->           capture verbatim until {{{{/name}}}}
+COMMENT  --scan-->           discard until }} (short) or --}} (long)
+```
